03-04.description: The Yorkist Edward, Earl of March, was proclaimed king in London, deposing the Lancastrian Henry VI. Weeks later he won the bloody Battle of Towton, securing his throne.

03-04.title: US Constitution takes effect as the first Congress meets
03-04.description: The new federal government began operation as Congress gathered at Federal Hall in New York, though it took weeks to reach a quorum. The Constitution is the oldest written national constitution still in force.

03-04.title: Abraham Lincoln inaugurated as 16th President
03-04.description: With seven states already seceded, Lincoln appealed to 'the better angels of our nature' in his inaugural address. War began at Fort Sumter five weeks later.

03-04.title: Tchaikovsky's 'Swan Lake' premieres at the Bolshoi
03-04.description: The first production in Moscow was poorly received. Revived in St Petersburg in 1895 with choreography by Petipa and Ivanov, it became the most famous of all ballets.

03-04.title: Franklin D. Roosevelt inaugurated in the depths of the Depression
03-04.description: With banks failing nationwide, Roosevelt told Americans 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself'. In his first hundred days Congress passed a wave of New Deal legislation.

03-04.title: John Lennon says the Beatles are 'more popular than Jesus'
03-04.description: The remark appeared in an interview in London's Evening Standard and passed unnoticed in Britain. Reprinted in the US months later, it led to record burnings and radio bans.

03-05.title: Emperor Julian sets out to invade Persia
03-05.description: Julian left Antioch with a large army to attack the Sasanian Empire. He reached Ctesiphon but was killed during the retreat in June, and with him ended the last attempt to restore paganism.

03-05.title: Nasir Khusraw sets out on his seven-year journey
03-05.description: The Persian poet and philosopher Nasir Khusraw set out on a pilgrimage to Mecca, taking an indirect route north toward the Caspian Sea. His account of the seven-year journey, the Safarnama, described the wealth of Fatimid Cairo.

03-05.title: Lithuania defeats the Livonian Order at Aizkraukle
03-05.description: Near Aizkraukle in present-day Latvia, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Traidenis defeated the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order, killing 71 knights, including the grand master, Ernst von Rassburg. Duke Nameisis of the Semigallians then recognised Traidenis as suzerain.

03-05.title: Henry VII commissions John Cabot to seek new lands
03-05.description: Letters patent authorised the Venetian navigator to sail under the English flag in search of unknown lands. His 1497 voyage reached North America and later underpinned English claims there.

03-05.title: British soldiers kill five in the Boston Massacre
03-05.description: Soldiers fired into a crowd taunting them in King Street, killing five men, including Crispus Attucks. Paul Revere's engraving of the scene became powerful propaganda against British rule.

03-05.title: Churchill warns of an 'iron curtain' across Europe
03-05.description: Speaking at Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill declared that an iron curtain had descended across the continent from the Baltic to the Adriatic. The speech popularised the phrase and the Cold War divide.

03-05.title: Joseph Stalin dies
03-05.description: The Soviet dictator died four days after a stroke at his dacha near Moscow. His rule had brought rapid industrialisation and victory over Germany, but also famine, purges and millions of deaths.

03-05.title: Alberto Korda photographs Che Guevara
03-05.description: At a Havana memorial for victims of a ship explosion, Korda captured Guevara's gaze in a photograph later titled 'Guerrillero Heroico'. It became one of the most reproduced images in the world.

03-05.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty enters into force
03-05.description: The treaty committed nuclear powers not to spread weapons and others not to acquire them, while promoting peaceful nuclear energy. With 191 parties, it is the most widely joined arms control agreement.

03-06.title: The Abbasids execute the 42 captives of Amorium at Samarra
03-06.description: The Abbasids executed at Samarra 42 Byzantine officers and notables, taken hostage in the sack of Amorium in 838, after they refused to convert to Islam. Repeated Byzantine efforts to ransom them had been rebuffed.

03-06.title: Philip II of France takes Château Gaillard
03-06.description: French troops captured Richard the Lionheart's great castle above the Seine after a six-month siege, some climbing in through a latrine chute. Normandy fell to France within months.

03-06.title: Tommaso Parentucelli is elected Pope Nicholas V
03-06.description: Meeting in the Roman basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva, the conclave elected Cardinal Tommaso Parentucelli to succeed Pope Eugene IV. He took the name Nicholas in memory of his obligations to Niccolò Albergati.

03-06.title: President Monroe signs the Missouri Compromise
03-06.description: Missouri was to enter the Union as a slave state and Maine as a free one, with slavery barred from the rest of the Louisiana Purchase north of 36°30'. The balance held for three decades.

03-06.title: The Alamo falls to Santa Anna
03-06.description: Mexican troops stormed the mission at dawn after a 13-day siege, killing nearly all of its roughly 200 defenders, including Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. 'Remember the Alamo' became the Texan battle cry.

03-06.title: US Supreme Court decides Dred Scott v. Sandford
03-06.description: Chief Justice Roger Taney ruled that Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not ban slavery in the territories. The decision deepened the crisis that led to civil war.

03-06.title: Clarence Birdseye's frozen foods go on sale
03-06.description: Shops in Springfield, Massachusetts, began selling quick-frozen vegetables, fruit, fish and meat using Birdseye's process. Frozen food went on to transform shopping and diets.

03-06.title: Ghana becomes independent
03-06.description: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana under Kwame Nkrumah, the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence from a European power after the war. It inspired independence movements across Africa.

03-07.title: Marcus Aurelius becomes Roman Emperor
03-07.description: On the death of Antoninus Pius, Marcus Aurelius succeeded and made his adoptive brother Lucius Verus co-emperor. A Stoic philosopher, he wrote his 'Meditations' while campaigning on the Danube.

03-07.title: Constantine I makes Sunday the Roman day of rest
03-07.description: Emperor Constantine I decreed that judges, towns and all trades rest on the day of the sun, making Sunday the Roman day of rest. The day honoured Sol Invictus, the official sun god of the late empire.

03-07.title: Conrad III is elected King of Germany at Coblenz
03-07.description: Conrad III, a former anti-king against Lothair III, was elected King of Germany at Coblenz in the presence of the papal legate Theodwin, becoming the first ruler of the Hohenstaufen dynasty. His election began a long rivalry with the Welfs.

03-07.title: Napoleon storms Jaffa
03-07.description: French troops took the port of Jaffa during Napoleon's Syrian campaign. Thousands of prisoners were then executed, and plague broke out in the army, which was halted at Acre.

03-07.title: Daniel Webster's 'Seventh of March' speech backs compromise
03-07.description: The Massachusetts senator supported Henry Clay's compromise proposals, including a tougher fugitive slave law, to preserve the Union. Many Northern abolitionists denounced him.

03-07.title: Alexander Graham Bell is granted his telephone patent
03-07.description: US Patent 174,465 covered a method of transmitting speech electrically. It became one of the most valuable patents ever issued and was defended in hundreds of lawsuits.

03-07.title: German troops reoccupy the Rhineland
03-07.description: Hitler sent soldiers into the demilitarised Rhineland in breach of the Versailles and Locarno treaties. France and Britain did not respond with force, encouraging further German expansion.

03-07.title: US troops seize the Remagen bridge over the Rhine
03-07.description: American soldiers captured the Ludendorff railway bridge at Remagen before German demolition charges could destroy it. It gave the Allies their first crossing of the Rhine.

03-07.title: 'Bloody Sunday' on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma
03-07.description: Alabama state troopers attacked about 600 civil rights marchers with clubs and tear gas. Televised images shocked the nation and helped secure the Voting Rights Act that August.

03-08.title: Ferdowsi completes the 'Shahnameh'
03-08.description: After some thirty years' work, the poet Ferdowsi finished his epic of the kings of Iran, around 50,000 couplets long. Written in Persian with few Arabic words, it is Iran's national epic.

03-08.title: Alfonso VII is proclaimed king of León after Urraca's death
03-08.description: Urraca, Queen of León, Castile and Galicia since 1109, died and was succeeded by her son Alfonso VII, who had been King of Galicia since 1111. Her reign had been troubled by civil war with her second husband, Alfonso I of Aragon.
links: Alfonso VII of León and Castile

03-08.title: Strasbourg's citizens defeat their bishop's army at Hausbergen
03-08.description: Near Strasbourg, the city's citizen militia won a decisive victory over the army of its bishop, Walter of Geroldseck, ending his lordship over the city. Strasbourg became in effect a self-governing free imperial city, and the bishops moved their seat to Saverne.

03-08.title: Anne becomes queen on the death of William III
03-08.description: William III died after a fall from his horse, and his sister-in-law Anne succeeded. During her reign England and Scotland united as Great Britain in 1707.

03-08.title: New York brokers form the New York Stock and Exchange Board
03-08.description: Brokers adopted a constitution and rented rooms on Wall Street, building on the Buttonwood Agreement of 1792. Their exchange became the New York Stock Exchange.

03-08.title: Raymonde de Laroche becomes the first licensed woman pilot
03-08.description: The Aéro-Club de France issued licence no. 36 to the French aviator. She set altitude records before dying in a crash in 1919.

03-08.title: Protests in Petrograd begin the February Revolution
03-08.description: On International Women's Day (23 February Old Style), women textile workers protesting about bread shortages began strikes that spread across the city. Within a week Tsar Nicholas II had abdicated.

03-08.title: Japanese forces occupy Rangoon
03-08.description: Japanese troops entered Burma's capital, abandoned by the British. The loss cut the Burma Road supply route to China, and by May Japan controlled most of Burma.

03-08.title: Joe Frazier beats Muhammad Ali in the 'Fight of the Century'
03-08.description: At Madison Square Garden, Frazier won a unanimous decision after knocking Ali down in the 15th round. It was Ali's first professional defeat.

03-09.title: Liu Che ascends the Han throne as Emperor Wu
03-09.description: Liu Che became the seventh emperor of the Han dynasty, known after his death as Emperor Wu. His reign of 54 years saw long campaigns against the Xiongnu, Han expansion into Central Asia and the promotion of Confucianism in government.

03-09.title: Gregory VII's synod condemns married and simoniac priests
03-09.description: At his Lenten synod in Rome, Pope Gregory VII barred married priests and those who had bought office from ministering. The reforms helped impose clerical celibacy in the Western Church.

03-09.title: Ivan Asen II routs Theodore of Epirus at Klokotnitsa
03-09.description: Tsar Ivan Asen II of Bulgaria routed and captured Theodore Komnenos Doukas, ruler of Epirus and Thessalonica, who had broken a treaty and invaded Bulgaria. The victory ended Epirote power and brought much of Thrace, Macedonia and Albania under Bulgarian rule.

03-09.title: Pedro Álvares Cabral sails from Lisbon
03-09.description: Cabral's fleet of 13 ships left for India, swinging far west into the Atlantic. On 22 April it sighted the coast of Brazil, which Cabral claimed for Portugal.

03-09.title: Napoleon Bonaparte marries Joséphine de Beauharnais
03-09.description: The civil wedding in Paris took place two days before Napoleon left to command the Army of Italy. Joséphine became empress in 1804, but he divorced her in 1810 for lack of an heir.

03-09.title: Supreme Court frees the Amistad Africans
03-09.description: The Court ruled that the Mende captives who had seized the slave ship Amistad had been illegally enslaved. Argued by John Quincy Adams, the case became a cause for abolitionists.

03-09.title: Monitor and Virginia fight the first battle between ironclads
03-09.description: At Hampton Roads, Virginia, USS Monitor and the Confederate CSS Virginia fought for hours without decisive damage. The duel showed that wooden warships were obsolete.

03-09.title: Pancho Villa raids Columbus, New Mexico
03-09.description: Some 500 of Villa's fighters attacked the border town, killing 18 Americans. The US sent General John Pershing on a punitive expedition into Mexico, which failed to catch Villa.

03-09.title: US firebombing raid devastates Tokyo
03-09.description: In the night of 9-10 March, some 300 B-29 bombers dropped incendiaries on Tokyo, burning about 41 square kilometres. Around 100,000 people died, the deadliest air raid in history.

03-10.title: Rome defeats Carthage at the Aegates Islands
03-10.description: A new Roman fleet destroyed a Carthaginian relief fleet off western Sicily. Carthage sued for peace, ending the First Punic War and ceding Sicily, Rome's first overseas province.

03-10.title: Liu Zhiyuan proclaims himself emperor, founding the Later Han
03-10.description: After the Khitan Liao army took Kaifeng and ended the Later Jin, the Shatuo general Liu Zhiyuan, governor of Taiyuan, proclaimed himself emperor. As the Khitan withdrew he entered Kaifeng and founded the Later Han, the shortest of the Five Dynasties.

03-10.title: Charles I dissolves Parliament and begins his Personal Rule
03-10.description: After clashes over taxation and religion, Charles dissolved Parliament and governed without one for eleven years. Financial need forced him to recall it in 1640, leading to civil war.

03-10.title: Upper Louisiana formally passes to the United States
03-10.description: In a ceremony at St Louis, the Spanish flag was lowered and the French tricolour raised, then the next day replaced by the Stars and Stripes. It completed the transfer of the Louisiana Purchase.

03-10.title: US Senate ratifies the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
03-10.description: The Senate approved the peace with Mexico, which ceded California and much of the Southwest. The United States paid 15 million dollars and assumed its citizens' claims against Mexico.

03-10.title: Bell makes the first telephone call
03-10.description: In his Boston laboratory Alexander Graham Bell spoke into his transmitter: 'Mr Watson, come here, I want to see you.' His assistant Thomas Watson heard him in the next room.

03-10.title: James Earl Ray pleads guilty to killing Martin Luther King Jr.
03-10.description: Ray was sentenced to 99 years in prison. Days later he recanted his plea and sought a trial for the rest of his life, fuelling persistent claims of a conspiracy.

03-10.title: Nasdaq peaks at the height of the dot-com bubble
03-10.description: The technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite index closed at 5,048, more than double its level a year earlier. It then fell by nearly 80 per cent by October 2002 as internet stocks collapsed.

03-11.title: Giovanni de' Medici proclaimed Pope Leo X
03-11.description: The son of Lorenzo the Magnificent was announced as pope at 37. A lavish patron of Raphael and others, he promoted the indulgence campaign for St Peter's that provoked Martin Luther in 1517.

03-11.title: The Daily Courant, Britain's first daily newspaper, appears
03-11.description: Published by Elizabeth Mallet near Fleet Street, the single-sheet Courant carried foreign news translated from continental papers. It ran until 1735, founding the British daily press.

03-11.title: Luddite machine-breaking begins in Nottinghamshire
03-11.description: After a protest in Nottingham was dispersed, framework knitters broke dozens of stocking frames at Arnold. Attacks on machinery spread across the Midlands and North under the name of 'Ned Ludd'.

03-11.title: Verdi's 'Rigoletto' premieres in Venice
03-11.description: The opera of a hunchbacked jester was a triumph at La Fenice. Verdi reportedly kept the aria 'La donna è mobile' secret until the final rehearsals, and it was soon sung in the streets.

03-11.title: British and Indian troops capture Baghdad
03-11.description: General Stanley Maude's army entered Baghdad after the Ottoman garrison withdrew, avenging the surrender at Kut a year earlier. Britain went on to rule Mesopotamia, later Iraq, under a League mandate.

03-11.title: Roosevelt signs the Lend-Lease Act
03-11.description: The act allowed the United States to lend or lease war supplies to nations whose defence was vital to America. Britain, the Soviet Union and China received some 50 billion dollars of aid.

03-11.title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes Soviet leader
03-11.description: The 54-year-old Gorbachev was chosen General Secretary the day after Konstantin Chernenko's death. His policies of glasnost and perestroika unleashed forces that ended the Soviet Union in 1991.

03-11.title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
03-11.description: The World Health Organization described the coronavirus outbreak as a pandemic, with cases in over 100 countries. Lockdowns followed worldwide, and millions died in the years that followed.

03-12.title: Vitiges ends his year-long siege of Rome
03-12.description: The Ostrogothic king Vitiges ended the siege of Rome, which Byzantine forces under General Belisarius had held against his numerically superior army since March 537. The siege, the first major clash of the Gothic War, played a decisive role in its course.

03-12.title: Odo of Châtillon elected Pope Urban II
03-12.description: Elected at Terracina while a rival pope held Rome, Urban II continued Gregory VII's reforms. In 1095 he preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont.

03-12.title: Konrad von Wallenrode is elected Grand Master of the Teutonic Order
03-12.description: Konrad von Wallenrode was elected the 24th Grand Master of the Teutonic Knights, the supreme head of the order, and served until 1393.

03-12.title: Charles II grants New Netherland to the Duke of York
03-12.description: The King granted his brother James lands between the Connecticut and Delaware rivers, then held by the Dutch. English ships seized New Amsterdam that August and renamed it New York.

03-12.title: Juliette Gordon Low founds the Girl Scouts in Savannah
03-12.description: Inspired by the Guide movement she had seen in Britain, Low gathered 18 girls for the first meeting of the American Girl Guides. Renamed the Girl Scouts in 1913, it has had tens of millions of members.

03-12.title: German troops march into Austria
03-12.description: The Wehrmacht crossed the border unopposed and was greeted by cheering crowds. The next day Austria was declared part of the German Reich, the Anschluss that Versailles had forbidden.

03-12.title: Truman announces the Truman Doctrine
03-12.description: Asking Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey, Harry Truman pledged to support 'free peoples who are resisting attempted subjugation'. The doctrine framed US Cold War policy of containment.

03-12.title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
03-12.description: At CERN in Geneva, Berners-Lee circulated 'Information Management: A Proposal' for a hypertext system linking documents across computers. His supervisor called it 'vague but exciting'.

03-13.title: The Praetorian Guard murders Emperor Elagabalus and his mother
03-13.description: The Praetorian Guard killed the teenage emperor Elagabalus, whose religious innovations had caused scandal, together with his mother, Julia Soaemias. His cousin Severus Alexander, the last ruler of the Severan dynasty, succeeded him.

03-13.title: Nicaea and Genoa conclude the Treaty of Nymphaeum against Venice
03-13.description: The Nicaean emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos and the Republic of Genoa concluded a trade and defence pact at Nymphaeum. Genoa promised naval help against the Latin Empire of Constantinople and Venice in return for tax-free trade and access to the Black Sea.

03-13.title: Hernán Cortés lands on the Mexican coast
03-13.description: Cortés's expedition of about 500 men reached the Tabasco coast. Within two and a half years, with Indigenous allies, he overthrew the Aztec Empire and captured Tenochtitlan.

03-13.title: New College in Massachusetts is named after John Harvard
03-13.description: The college at Cambridge took the name of John Harvard, a young minister who left it his library and half his estate. Founded in 1636, Harvard is the oldest university in the United States.

03-13.title: William Herschel discovers Uranus
03-13.description: From his garden in Bath, Herschel spotted an object he first took for a comet. It proved to be a new planet, the first discovered with a telescope, doubling the known size of the solar system.

03-13.title: Tsar Alexander II assassinated in St Petersburg
03-13.description: Members of the revolutionary group People's Will threw bombs at the Tsar's carriage. Alexander, who had freed the serfs, died within hours, and his son's reign brought harsh reaction.

03-13.title: Winter War ends as the Moscow Peace Treaty takes effect
03-13.description: Finland ceded about a tenth of its territory, including Karelia, to the Soviet Union. Its stubborn defence had cost the Red Army heavily and preserved Finnish independence.

03-13.title: Gunman kills 16 children and their teacher at Dunblane
03-13.description: Thomas Hamilton opened fire in the gym of Dunblane Primary School in Scotland before killing himself. Public campaigning led to a near-total ban on private handgun ownership in Britain.

03-14.title: Géza and Ladislaus defeat King Solomon of Hungary at Mogyoród
03-14.description: Dukes Géza and Ladislaus, claiming the throne, defeated their cousin King Solomon of Hungary at Mogyoród and forced him to flee to the kingdom's western borderland. Géza was proclaimed king that year, but Solomon kept the western regions.

03-14.title: A palace revolt in Granada deposes Muhammad III
03-14.description: On Eid al-Fitr the citizens of Granada stormed palaces in the city, deposed the Nasrid emir Muhammad III and placed his brother Nasr on the throne. Muhammad's capture of Ceuta had provoked an alliance of Castile, Aragon and the Marinids against Granada.

03-14.title: Admiral John Byng executed by firing squad
03-14.description: Convicted of failing to do his utmost to relieve Minorca, Byng was shot on the deck of HMS Monarch at Portsmouth. Voltaire mocked the English for killing an admiral 'to encourage the others'.

03-14.title: Eli Whitney patents the cotton gin
03-14.description: Whitney's machine separated cotton fibre from seeds far faster than by hand. It made short-staple cotton highly profitable and fuelled a vast expansion of slavery in the American South.

03-14.title: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm
03-14.description: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity transformed ideas of space, time and gravity. He won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

03-14.title: Gold Standard Act puts the dollar on gold
03-14.description: President McKinley signed the act fixing the dollar's value in gold and ending the long political fight over free silver. The US left the gold standard domestically in 1933.

03-14.title: Penicillin saves its first American patient
03-14.description: Anne Miller, dying of streptococcal blood poisoning after a miscarriage, was treated at a New Haven hospital with a scarce supply of penicillin. She recovered and lived to the age of 90.

03-14.title: Jack Ruby convicted of murdering Lee Harvey Oswald
03-14.description: A Dallas jury found the nightclub owner guilty of shooting Kennedy's accused assassin on live television and sentenced him to death. The verdict was overturned, and Ruby died before a retrial.

03-15.title: Sulpicius Galba and Aurelius Cotta become consuls in Rome
03-15.description: Publius Sulpicius Galba and Gaius Aurelius Cotta took office as consuls in Rome. Sulpicius, charged with Macedonia, persuaded the Comitia centuriata at a second session to vote for war on Philip V, beginning the Second Macedonian War.

03-15.title: Julius Caesar assassinated on the Ides of March
03-15.description: A group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed Caesar to death in the Curia of Pompey. Meant to save the Republic, the murder led to civil war and the rule of Augustus.

03-15.title: Theoderic the Great kills Odoacer at Ravenna
03-15.description: After a long siege ended in a power-sharing agreement, Theoderic murdered Odoacer at a banquet. The Ostrogothic king then ruled Italy for over thirty years.

03-15.title: Henry the Fowler defeats the Magyars at Riade
03-15.description: King Henry the Fowler of East Francia routed a Magyar army near the river Unstrut in northern Thuringia, after refusing to pay further tribute. The victory raised the prestige of the Saxon dynasty, though Magyar raids continued until 955.

03-15.title: Columbus returns to Spain from his first voyage
03-15.description: Columbus sailed into Palos, the port from which he had departed seven months earlier, with news of islands across the Atlantic. His voyages began lasting European contact with the Americas.

03-15.title: Akbar abolishes the jizya tax on non-Muslims
03-15.description: The Mughal emperor ended the poll tax on non-Muslim subjects, part of a policy of conciliating the Hindu majority of his empire. Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679.

03-15.title: Maine becomes the 23rd US state
03-15.description: Separated from Massachusetts, Maine entered the Union as a free state under the Missouri Compromise. Its admission balanced that of Missouri as a slave state.

03-15.title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
03-15.description: Facing revolution in Petrograd and mutiny in the army, Nicholas II gave up the throne for himself and his son. Over three centuries of Romanov rule ended, and a Provisional Government took power.

03-15.title: Gunman kills 51 at two Christchurch mosques
03-15.description: A white supremacist attacked worshippers at Friday prayers and livestreamed the killings. Within a month New Zealand's parliament banned most semi-automatic weapons.

03-16.title: Nebuchadnezzar II captures Jerusalem
03-16.description: The Babylonian Chronicle records that Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem, carried King Jehoiachin into exile and installed Zedekiah. A revolt led to the city's destruction in 587 BCE.

03-16.title: Han Lin'er is proclaimed emperor of a restored Song Dynasty
03-16.description: Amid the Red Turban Rebellion against the Yuan, Han Lin'er, a claimed descendant of Emperor Huizong of Song, was proclaimed emperor at Bozhou. He reigned in name only, with real power held first by Liu Futong and later by Zhu Yuanzhang.

03-16.title: Magellan's expedition reaches the Philippines
03-16.description: After crossing the Pacific, Ferdinand Magellan's ships sighted Samar and landed at Homonhon. Magellan was killed on Mactan in April, but one ship completed the first circumnavigation in 1522.

03-16.title: Long Parliament dissolves itself
03-16.description: First summoned in 1640, the Long Parliament voted its own dissolution and called new elections. The Convention Parliament that followed invited Charles II to return as king.

03-16.title: Congress establishes the US Military Academy at West Point
03-16.description: President Jefferson signed the act founding a military academy at West Point, New York. Its graduates included Grant, Lee and Eisenhower.

03-16.title: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fuelled rocket
03-16.description: At Auburn, Massachusetts, Goddard's petrol and liquid-oxygen rocket flew for 2.5 seconds and rose about 12 metres. The principle underlies most modern space launch vehicles.

03-16.title: Hitler announces German rearmament and conscription
03-16.description: Defying the Treaty of Versailles, Hitler reintroduced conscription and announced an army of 36 divisions. Britain, France and Italy protested, but took no effective action.

03-16.title: US soldiers massacre villagers at My Lai
03-16.description: American troops killed some 350 to 500 unarmed civilians, mostly women, children and old men, in a South Vietnamese hamlet. Exposed in 1969, the massacre deepened opposition to the war.

03-17.title: Julius Caesar defeats the Pompeian army at the Battle of Munda
03-17.description: In southern Spain, Julius Caesar defeated the Pompeian army of Gnaeus and Sextus Pompeius and Titus Labienus. Labienus was killed and Gnaeus Pompeius was caught and executed soon afterwards; it was Caesar's last battle of the civil war.

03-17.title: Traditional date of the death of Saint Patrick
03-17.description: By tradition Patrick, the Romano-British missionary to Ireland, died on 17 March, though the year is uncertain. His feast became Ireland's national day, celebrated by the Irish diaspora worldwide.

03-17.title: Edward the Black Prince receives the Duchy of Cornwall
03-17.description: Edward the Black Prince, eldest son of King Edward III, received the Duchy of Cornwall by a royal charter, having been made duke in parliament in February. It was the earliest creation of a duke in England.

03-17.title: British troops evacuate Boston
03-17.description: After Washington fortified Dorchester Heights with cannon hauled from Fort Ticonderoga, General Howe's army sailed for Halifax. The siege of Boston ended in an American success.

03-17.title: Stephen Perry patents the rubber band
03-17.description: Stephen Perry of the London firm Messrs Perry and Co patented bands made of vulcanised rubber for holding papers together. The humble invention became universal.

03-17.title: Einstein completes his paper on light quanta
03-17.description: Einstein finished a paper proposing that light comes in discrete packets of energy, explaining the photoelectric effect. It helped found quantum theory and earned him the Nobel Prize.

03-17.title: Brussels Treaty creates a Western European defence pact
03-17.description: Britain, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg agreed to defend one another against attack. The pact paved the way for NATO in 1949 and later became the Western European Union.

03-17.title: US launches Vanguard 1 satellite
03-17.description: The grapefruit-sized satellite, mocked by Khrushchev, showed that the Earth is slightly pear-shaped. Long silent, it is the oldest human-made object still in orbit.

03-18.title: A major earthquake strikes Arabia and the Levant
03-18.description: The first of two major Near Eastern earthquakes that year had its epicentre in the northwestern Arabian Peninsula, around Tabuk. The second, on 29 May, was most damaging in Ramla in Palestine; contemporary sources often merge the two.

03-18.title: Frederick II crowns himself King of Jerusalem
03-18.description: Having regained Jerusalem by treaty while excommunicated, the Emperor took the crown from the altar of the Holy Sepulchre and placed it on his own head. No cleric would crown him.

03-18.title: Mongols defeat the Polish armies at the Battle of Chmielnik
03-18.description: During the first Mongol invasion of Poland, Mongol forces defeated the Polish armies of Sandomierz and Kraków near Chmielnik, between Kraków and Kielce. The invasion culminated in the Mongol victory at Legnica in April.

03-18.title: Street fighting erupts in Berlin
03-18.description: Troops fired on a crowd outside the royal palace and barricade fighting spread through the city, leaving hundreds dead. King Frederick William IV withdrew the army and promised a constitution.

03-18.title: Parisians rise up and begin the Paris Commune
03-18.description: Attempts by the government to remove the National Guard's cannon from Montmartre provoked an uprising. The Commune ruled Paris until it was crushed in the 'Bloody Week' of May.

03-18.title: Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk
03-18.description: The Soviet cosmonaut spent about 12 minutes outside Voskhod 2. His suit ballooned in the vacuum, and he had to let out air to squeeze back into the airlock.

03-18.title: East Germany holds its first free elections
03-18.description: East Germans voted in their first free parliamentary elections. The conservative Alliance for Germany won, opening the way to rapid reunification with West Germany in October.

03-18.title: Russia signs a treaty annexing Crimea
03-18.description: Two days after a referendum held under Russian military control, Vladimir Putin signed a treaty absorbing Crimea. Most UN members regard the annexation as illegal.

03-19.title: Henry of Flanders defeats the Nicaeans at the Battle of Adramyttion
03-19.description: Latin crusader forces under Henry of Flanders defeated an army of the Empire of Nicaea, led by Constantine Laskaris, at Adramyttion. Nicaea was one of the Greek states founded after the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204.

03-19.title: Ugolino di Conti is elected Pope Gregory IX
03-19.description: Following the death of Pope Honorius III, Ugolino di Conti was elected pope and took the name Gregory IX. He reigned until 1241 and is known for issuing the Decretales and instituting the Papal Inquisition.

03-19.title: The Byzantine Empire and Venice renew their treaty
03-19.description: The Byzantine Empire and the Republic of Venice renegotiated their treaty of 1268 and extended it for two years. Emperor Michael VIII Palaiologos kept the Venetian fleet out of Charles of Anjou's crusade plans, while Venice gained wider trading privileges.

03-19.title: Mongol fleet destroys the last Song forces at Yamen
03-19.description: In a sea battle off the Pearl River delta, Yuan forces crushed the Song navy. The minister Lu Xiufu jumped into the sea with the child emperor, completing Kublai Khan's conquest of China.

03-19.title: Edict of Amboise ends the first French War of Religion
03-19.description: Catherine de' Medici's peace allowed Huguenot nobles to worship freely and others in limited places. Neither side was satisfied, and war resumed in 1567.

03-19.title: René-Robert de La Salle killed by his own men
03-19.description: The explorer who had claimed the Mississippi basin for France was shot by mutineers in east Texas after his colony went astray. His Fort Saint Louis was soon destroyed.

03-19.title: Gounod's 'Faust' premieres in Paris
03-19.description: Charles Gounod's opera, based on Goethe, opened at the Théâtre Lyrique. Revised with recitatives and a ballet, it became one of the most performed operas of the 19th century.

03-19.title: US adopts standard time zones and daylight saving time
03-19.description: The Standard Time Act gave legal force to time zones first used by the railways and introduced daylight saving time to save fuel. Daylight saving proved unpopular and was repealed in 1919.

03-19.title: Hitler issues the 'Nero Decree'
03-19.description: Hitler ordered the destruction of German industry, transport and supplies before they fell to the Allies. Armaments Minister Albert Speer worked to ensure it was largely not carried out.

03-20.title: Dutch East India Company is founded
03-20.description: The States General granted the VOC a monopoly on Dutch trade in Asia. Financed by publicly traded shares, it could wage war, make treaties and found colonies, and dominated the spice trade.

03-20.title: A papal conclave opens in Rome after Innocent XIII's death
03-20.description: The electors, largely the same as those who had chosen Pope Innocent XIII in 1721, met in Rome to elect his successor. On 28 May they elected Cardinal Pierfrancesco Orsini, a Dominican friar, as Pope Benedict XIII.

03-20.title: Napoleon returns to Paris
03-20.description: The day after Louis XVIII fled, Napoleon entered the Tuileries to cheering crowds. His restored rule, the Hundred Days, ended with defeat at Waterloo in June.

03-20.title: Harriet Beecher Stowe publishes 'Uncle Tom's Cabin'
03-20.description: Stowe's novel of slavery sold some 300,000 copies in America in its first year and stirred anti-slavery feeling in the North. Lincoln is said to have greeted her as the author who started the war.

03-20.title: Opponents of slavery meet at Ripon to form a new party
03-20.description: Meeting in a schoolhouse in Ripon, Wisconsin, opponents of the Kansas-Nebraska Act called for a new party. The Republican Party was organised that summer and won the presidency in 1860.

03-20.title: Kaiser Wilhelm II dismisses Bismarck
03-20.description: After disputes with the young Emperor, Otto von Bismarck's resignation as Chancellor was accepted. Without him, Germany's alliances shifted, as Britain's Punch caricatured in 'Dropping the Pilot'.

03-20.title: Einstein submits his general theory of relativity
03-20.description: 'The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity' reached the journal Annalen der Physik. It described gravity as the curvature of spacetime and predicted the bending of light, confirmed in 1919.

03-20.title: Himmler announces the Dachau concentration camp
03-20.description: Munich's police chief Heinrich Himmler announced a camp for political prisoners near Dachau, opened two days later. It became the model for the Nazi camp system; over 40,000 died there.

03-21.title: Heraclius restores the True Cross to Jerusalem
03-21.description: By tradition on this day, Emperor Heraclius returned the relic of the cross, captured by the Persians in 614, to Jerusalem. Within a decade the city fell to the Arab armies.

03-21.title: Charles Martel defeats Chilperic II and Ragenfrid at Vincy
03-21.description: Near Cambrai, Charles Martel and the Austrasians defeated the Neustrian king Chilperic II and his mayor of the palace, Ragenfrid, in the civil war after Pepin of Herstal's death. The victory was a decisive step in Charles's rise to power.

03-21.title: The Great Heathen Army defeats Northumbria's army at York
03-21.description: An army of the Anglo-Saxon Kingdom of Northumbria tried to recapture York from the Vikings of the Great Heathen Army and was defeated in the city. The Scandinavian army went on to overrun East Anglia and much of Mercia.

03-21.title: Thomas Cranmer burned at the stake in Oxford
03-21.description: The former Archbishop of Canterbury, author of the Book of Common Prayer, withdrew his recantations before Mary I's officials. He thrust the hand that had signed them into the flames first.

03-21.title: Great fire destroys much of New Orleans
03-21.description: A Good Friday fire burned 856 buildings in the Spanish colonial city. With a second fire in 1794, it led to the rebuilding of the French Quarter in brick and tile.

03-21.title: Pius VII crowned pope in Venice
03-21.description: With Rome occupied by the French, the cardinals met in Venice, where Barnaba Chiaramonti was crowned Pope Pius VII. He later signed a concordat with Napoleon and was held captive by him.

03-21.title: Germany launches its Spring Offensive
03-21.description: Operation Michael struck British lines on the Somme after a five-hour bombardment, gaining more ground in days than any attack since 1914. It ran out of steam, and the Allies counter-attacked that summer.

03-21.title: Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville
03-21.description: South African police fired on an unarmed crowd protesting against the pass laws, killing 69 people. The government banned the ANC and PAC, and 21 March is now Human Rights Day in South Africa.

03-22.title: Vikings defeat King Æthelred I of Wessex at Meretun
03-22.description: Vikings defeated the West Saxon army of King Æthelred I and his brother, the future King Alfred the Great, at Meretun, an unknown site in Wessex. Æthelred died after Easter that year and was succeeded by Alfred.

03-22.title: Pope Clement V suppresses the Knights Templar
03-22.description: Under pressure from Philip IV of France, Clement V issued the bull Vox in excelso at the Council of Vienne abolishing the Templars. Their property passed largely to the Hospitallers.

03-22.title: Plymouth Colony makes a treaty with Massasoit of the Wampanoag
03-22.description: The settlers of Plymouth Colony under Governor John Carver made a treaty of mutual defence with Massasoit, sachem of the Wampanoag, with Tisquantum interpreting. Massasoit kept the peace with the English until his death around 1661.

03-22.title: Powhatan attack kills 347 Virginia colonists
03-22.description: Warriors under Opechancanough struck English settlements along the James River, killing about a quarter of the colony's population. The English responded with years of retaliatory war.

03-22.title: Parliament passes the Stamp Act
03-22.description: The act taxed printed papers in the American colonies, from newspapers to playing cards. Colonists protested 'no taxation without representation', and Parliament repealed it the next year.

03-22.title: Enslaved insurgents win the Battle of Croix-des-Bouquets
03-22.description: Enslaved Black insurgents won a victory at Croix-des-Bouquets in the first major battle of the Haitian Revolution, their uprising against French colonial rule in Saint-Domingue.

03-22.title: Stephen Decatur killed in a duel
03-22.description: The naval hero of the Barbary Wars was mortally wounded by Commodore James Barron at Bladensburg, Maryland. His death strengthened public feeling against duelling.

03-22.title: Lumière brothers show their first film
03-22.description: At a meeting in Paris, Louis and Auguste Lumière projected 'Workers Leaving the Lumière Factory' with their Cinématographe. Their first paying public screening followed in December.

03-22.title: Arab League founded in Cairo
03-22.description: Egypt, Iraq, Transjordan, Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and Syria signed the pact founding the League of Arab States, with Yemen joining soon after. It now has 22 members.

03-23.title: The Quraysh defeat the Muslims at the Battle of Uhud
03-23.description: Near Mount Uhud, north of Medina, the Quraysh of Mecca under Abu Sufyan defeated the Muslims under Muhammad after archers left their posts. Muhammad was wounded and his uncle Hamza killed, but the Meccans did not follow up their victory.

03-23.title: Hồ Quý Ly deposes the Trần dynasty and founds the Hồ dynasty
03-23.description: The minister Hồ Quý Ly overthrew the emperor Thiếu Đế, his own grandson, ending 175 years of Trần rule in Đại Việt and founding the Hồ dynasty. The Ming used his usurpation as a pretext to invade in 1406.

03-23.title: Waltham Abbey surrenders, the last English monastery to close
03-23.description: The Augustinian abbey at Waltham in Essex was surrendered to Henry VIII's commissioners. It completed the Dissolution of the Monasteries, which transferred vast church lands to the Crown.

03-23.title: Patrick Henry declares 'Give me liberty, or give me death!'
03-23.description: At the Second Virginia Convention in Richmond, Henry urged the colony to raise a militia against Britain. The convention agreed, and fighting began at Lexington four weeks later.

03-23.title: Tsar Paul I murdered in St Michael's Castle
03-23.description: Conspiring officers killed the erratic Tsar in his bedroom in St Petersburg. His son Alexander I, aware of the plot, succeeded him and later led Russia against Napoleon.

03-23.title: Mussolini founds the Fasci di Combattimento in Milan
03-23.description: Benito Mussolini gathered veterans and nationalists in Piazza San Sepolcro to found a new movement. Its blackshirts helped him take power in 1922, and Fascism became a model for Hitler.

03-23.title: Reichstag passes the Enabling Act
03-23.description: With communists barred and others intimidated, the German parliament allowed Hitler's cabinet to make laws without it. Only the Social Democrats voted against, and the dictatorship had a legal basis.

03-23.title: Gemini 3 makes the first crewed Gemini flight
03-23.description: Gus Grissom and John Young flew three orbits and became the first astronauts to change their spacecraft's orbit. The Gemini programme prepared the techniques for Apollo.

03-24.title: Richard Fitzalan's English fleet attacks a wine fleet at Margate
03-24.description: During the Caroline War phase of the Hundred Years' War, an English fleet under Richard Fitzalan, Earl of Arundel, attacked a wine fleet of 250 to 360 French, Flemish and Castilian vessels. The battle continued into the next day.

03-24.title: Timur sacks Damascus
03-24.description: The Central Asian conqueror's army plundered and burned Damascus after its surrender, and its craftsmen were carried off to Samarkand. The Mamluk Sultanate survived, but Syria was devastated.

03-24.title: Elizabeth I dies and James VI of Scotland inherits England
03-24.description: Elizabeth died at Richmond Palace, and her cousin James VI became James I of England and Ireland. The crowns were united, though the kingdoms stayed separate until 1707.

03-24.title: Parliament passes the Quartering Act
03-24.description: The act required American colonies to provide barracks and supplies for British troops. Resentment of it was later listed among the grievances in the Declaration of Independence.

03-24.title: Tadeusz Kościuszko proclaims a general uprising in Kraków
03-24.description: In Kraków, Tadeusz Kościuszko proclaimed a general uprising against Russia and Prussia and took command of all Polish forces. His speech is considered the start of the Kościuszko Uprising, whose defeat led to the Third Partition of 1795.

03-24.title: Robert Koch identifies the tuberculosis bacterium
03-24.description: In a lecture in Berlin, Koch showed that tuberculosis, then causing about one in seven deaths in Europe, was caused by a bacterium. 24 March is now World Tuberculosis Day.

03-24.title: Allied prisoners break out in the 'Great Escape'
03-24.description: That night 76 airmen crawled through a tunnel out of Stalag Luft III in Sagan. Only three reached safety; on Hitler's orders, 50 of those recaptured were shot.

03-24.title: Military coup overthrows Isabel Perón in Argentina
03-24.description: A junta led by General Jorge Videla took power and began the 'Dirty War'. Thousands of people, estimated at up to 30,000, were 'disappeared' before military rule ended in 1983.

03-25.title: Theodosius III abdicates in favour of Leo III the Isaurian
03-25.description: The Byzantine emperor Theodosius III abdicated in favour of Leo III the Isaurian, the general who had captured his son. Leo founded the Isaurian dynasty and ended the Twenty Years' Anarchy, a period of rapidly changing emperors.

03-25.title: Robert the Bruce crowned King of Scots at Scone
03-25.description: Weeks after killing his rival John Comyn, Bruce was crowned in defiance of Edward I. Defeated and hunted that year, he fought back to win at Bannockburn in 1314.

03-25.title: The Council of Pisa convenes to end the Western Schism
03-25.description: A general council summoned by the cardinals met at Pisa to end the Western Schism. It went on to depose both rival popes, Benedict XIII of Avignon and Gregory XII of Rome, and to elect a third claimant, Alexander V.

03-25.title: A loveday at St Paul's reconciles Lancastrians and Yorkists
03-25.description: At St Paul's Cathedral, a loveday ritually reconciled the warring factions of the English nobility, the culmination of negotiations begun by King Henry VI. It brought a brief period of peace in the Wars of the Roses.

03-25.title: Christiaan Huygens discovers Titan
03-25.description: Using a telescope he had built with his brother, Huygens found Saturn's largest moon. Titan is now known to have a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane.

03-25.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
03-25.description: The Slave Trade Act received royal assent, banning British participation in the Atlantic slave trade. Slavery itself continued in British colonies until the Abolition Act of 1833.

03-25.title: Traditional start of the Greek War of Independence
03-25.description: Tradition holds that Bishop Germanos of Patras raised the banner of revolt on this day. After years of war and great-power intervention, Greece became independent in 1830.

03-25.title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire kills 146 in New York
03-25.description: Fire swept through a garment factory near Washington Square, and locked doors trapped workers, mostly young immigrant women. The disaster led to new fire safety and labour laws.

03-25.title: Treaty of Rome signed
03-25.description: France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg signed treaties creating the European Economic Community and Euratom. The EEC grew into today's European Union.

03-26.title: Emperor Maurice proclaims his son Theodosius co-emperor
03-26.description: The Eastern Roman emperor Maurice made his eldest son Theodosius, Caesar since 587, his co-emperor. Theodosius was deposed in a military revolt and was said to have been executed by Phocas's supporters.

03-26.title: James I of Aragon signs the Treaty of Almizra with Castile
03-26.description: James I of Aragon signed the Treaty of Almizra with the Castilian heir Alfonso, fixing the frontier between their conquests in al-Andalus. Valencia went to Aragon and Murcia to Castile, setting the southern limit of Aragonese expansion.

03-26.title: The Franco-Breton side wins the Combat of the Thirty
03-26.description: In the War of the Breton Succession, thirty champions of Charles of Blois under Jean de Beaumanoir met thirty men of the Anglo-Breton garrison of Ploërmel under Robert Bemborough. The Franco-Breton side won, and the fight became a celebrated example of chivalry.

03-26.title: William Caxton prints his English translation of Aesop's Fables
03-26.description: England's first printer completed his edition of the 'Fables of Esope' at Westminster, illustrated with woodcuts. Caxton's books helped standardise written English.

03-26.title: Earthquake devastates Caracas and Venezuela
03-26.description: On Holy Thursday a powerful earthquake destroyed Caracas and other towns held by the young republic, killing thousands. Royalist clergy called it divine punishment, and the First Republic soon fell.

03-26.title: Ludwig van Beethoven dies in Vienna
03-26.description: Beethoven died aged 56 during a thunderstorm. Despite growing deafness he composed nine symphonies and late string quartets that changed Western music, and some 20,000 people attended his funeral.

03-26.title: Bangladesh declares independence from Pakistan
03-26.description: After the Pakistani army's crackdown in Dhaka, independence was proclaimed in the name of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. Nine months of war followed, and Bangladesh won its freedom in December 1971.

03-26.title: Egypt and Israel sign a peace treaty
03-26.description: At the White House, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed the first peace treaty between Israel and an Arab state, building on the Camp David Accords. Israel returned the Sinai by 1982.

03-26.title: Schengen Agreement abolishes border checks in Europe
03-26.description: Seven European countries, including France and Germany, removed passport controls at their common borders. The Schengen Area now covers most of the European Union and several other states.

03-27.title: Pope John XXII condemns writings of Meister Eckhart as heretical
03-27.description: Pope John XXII condemned many writings of Meister Eckhart as heretical in the papal bull In Agro Dominico. Eckhart was a German priest, theologian, philosopher and mystic of the Dominican Order.

03-27.title: Juan Ponce de León sights Florida
03-27.description: Sailing north from Puerto Rico, Ponce de León sighted the coast he named La Florida, as it was the Easter season. He landed days later, beginning Spanish claims to the region.

03-27.title: Charles I becomes king on the death of James I
03-27.description: James I died at Theobalds and his son succeeded him. Charles's clashes with Parliament over money and religion led to civil war and his execution in 1649.

03-27.title: The Marquess of Rockingham forms his second British ministry
03-27.description: Charles Watson-Wentworth, 2nd Marquess of Rockingham, took office in Great Britain at the head of a ministry that began negotiations to end the American War of Independence. His second premiership lasted four months.

03-27.title: Congress passes the Naval Act, founding the US Navy
03-27.description: Prompted by Barbary corsairs seizing American ships, Congress authorised six frigates. Among them was USS Constitution, still in commission today.

03-27.title: Scotland and England play the first rugby international
03-27.description: At Raeburn Place in Edinburgh, Scotland beat England by a goal and a try to a try before about 4,000 spectators. It was the first international rugby match.

03-27.title: Two jumbo jets collide at Tenerife
03-27.description: A KLM 747 began its take-off in fog and struck a Pan Am 747 on the runway at Los Rodeos airport, killing 583 people. It remains the deadliest accident in aviation history.

03-27.title: Mount St Helens erupts for the first time in 123 years
03-27.description: A steam explosion blasted a crater in the summit of the Washington volcano after a week of earthquakes. On 18 May a massive eruption tore away its north face and killed 57 people.

03-28.title: Praetorians murder Pertinax and auction the empire
03-28.description: After killing Emperor Pertinax, the Praetorian Guard sold the throne to the senator Didius Julianus, who outbid his rival. He lasted 66 days before Septimius Severus took power.

03-28.title: Valentinian I makes his brother Valens co-emperor
03-28.description: At Constantinople, the Roman emperor Valentinian I made his brother Valens co-Augustus, giving him the eastern half of the empire and keeping the West for himself. Valens ruled until 378, when he was killed fighting the Goths at Adrianople.

03-28.title: Confederate Ireland signs the First Ormond Peace with Charles I
03-28.description: For the Supreme Council of Confederate Ireland, Donough MacCarty signed the First Ormond Peace with Ormonde for King Charles I, in exchange for greater freedom of religion. It was signed unbeknownst to the Confederate commanders and without the papal nuncio, Rinuccini.

03-28.title: Austria defeats France at the Battle of Vilshofen
03-28.description: In the War of the Austrian Succession, Austrian forces defeated the French and then plundered Vilshofen. The war was fought over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg lands after the death of Emperor Charles VI.

03-28.title: Britain and France declare war on Russia
03-28.description: The two powers joined the Ottoman Empire against Russia, beginning their part in the Crimean War. Battlefield reporting and Florence Nightingale's nursing made it a turning point in public views of war.

03-28.title: Henri Fabre makes the first seaplane flight
03-28.description: The French engineer took off from the Étang de Berre near Marseille in his float-equipped Hydravion. It was the first powered aircraft to take off from water.

03-28.title: Virginia Woolf drowns herself in the River Ouse
03-28.description: Fearing a return of mental illness, the novelist filled her pockets with stones and walked into the river near her Sussex home. Her novels include 'Mrs Dalloway' and 'To the Lighthouse'.

03-28.title: Partial meltdown at Three Mile Island
03-28.description: A cooling failure caused part of a reactor core to melt at the Pennsylvania nuclear plant. Little radiation escaped, but it was the worst US nuclear accident and stalled new reactor orders.

03-29.title: Viking raiders plunder Paris and hold it for ransom
03-29.description: A Viking fleet of 120 ships under the Norse chieftain Reginherus, or Ragnar, sailed up the Seine and plundered and occupied Paris, holding it for a large ransom. Reginherus has been tentatively identified with the legendary Ragnar Lodbrok.

03-29.title: Pope Innocent II endorses the Knights Templar in Omne datum optimum
03-29.description: In the papal bull Omne datum optimum, Pope Innocent II endorsed the Knights Templar, officially approving the Templar Rule and placing the order under papal protection. The order had been founded in Jerusalem to protect pilgrims.

03-29.title: The Ottoman Empire takes Thessaloniki from Venice after a long siege
03-29.description: After a siege begun in 1422, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Murad II captured Thessaloniki from the Republic of Venice. The city remained in Ottoman hands until it became part of the Kingdom of Greece in 1912.

03-29.title: Yorkists win the Battle of Towton
03-29.description: Fought in a snowstorm on Palm Sunday in Yorkshire, Towton is often called the bloodiest battle on English soil, with traditional estimates of 28,000 dead. It secured the throne for Edward IV.

03-29.title: Swedish settlers found New Sweden on the Delaware
03-29.description: Colonists from the Kalmar Nyckel and Fogel Grip landed at the site of Wilmington and built Fort Christina. The Dutch took New Sweden in 1655, but its log cabins became an American tradition.

03-29.title: Ice jam stops Niagara Falls
03-29.description: Ice blocking the Niagara River at Lake Erie reduced the falls to a trickle for over a day. Sightseers walked on the riverbed; it is the only time the falls are known to have stopped naturally.

03-29.title: Queen Victoria signs the British North America Act
03-29.description: The act united the Province of Canada, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick as the Dominion of Canada. Confederation took effect on 1 July, now Canada Day.

03-29.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg convicted of espionage
03-29.description: A New York jury found the couple guilty of conspiring to pass atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Their execution in 1953 remained controversial, especially over Ethel's role.

03-29.title: Last US combat troops leave South Vietnam
03-29.description: The final American combat units departed under the Paris Peace Accords, and the last prisoners of war were released. Some 58,000 Americans and millions of Vietnamese had died in the war.

03-30.title: The Avars lift their siege of the Byzantine stronghold of Tomis
03-30.description: In Maurice's Balkan campaigns, the Avars lifted their siege of Priscus' army at Tomis as Comentiolus led a Roman army along the Danube. They routed his troops, but plague later killed much of their army and seven sons of the khagan.

03-30.title: Sicilian Vespers uprising begins in Palermo
03-30.description: At the hour of vespers outside the church of Santo Spirito, Sicilians rose against Charles of Anjou's French rule, killing thousands. The island passed to Peter III of Aragon.

03-30.title: Edward I of England sacks Berwick-upon-Tweed
03-30.description: King Edward I of England sacked Berwick-upon-Tweed, then the richest Scottish burgh and the kingdom's main port for wool exports. It was the first significant battle of the First War of Scottish Independence.

03-30.title: Allied armies win the Battle of Paris
03-30.description: Russian, Prussian and Austrian forces stormed the heights around Paris, and the city capitulated that night. Coalition troops entered the next day, and Napoleon abdicated within a week.

03-30.title: Crawford Long uses ether to anaesthetise a patient
03-30.description: In Jefferson, Georgia, Dr Crawford Long removed a tumour from James Venable's neck after giving him ether. He did not publish until 1849, after William Morton's public demonstration.

03-30.title: Treaty of Paris ends the Crimean War
03-30.description: Russia accepted the neutralisation of the Black Sea, barring warships from its waters, and gave up southern Bessarabia. The powers guaranteed the integrity of the Ottoman Empire.

03-30.title: United States agrees to buy Alaska from Russia
03-30.description: William Seward signed a treaty to buy Alaska for 7.2 million dollars, about two cents an acre. Mocked as 'Seward's Folly', it proved rich in gold, fish and oil.

03-30.title: Ronald Reagan shot outside the Washington Hilton
03-30.description: John Hinckley Jr. wounded the President and three others, including press secretary James Brady. Reagan, hit in the chest, recovered quickly, and his humour in hospital boosted his popularity.

03-31.title: Bernard of Clairvaux preaches the Second Crusade at Vézelay
03-31.description: Bernard's sermon on a hillside at Vézelay moved Louis VII and crowds of nobles to take the cross after the fall of Edessa. The crusade ended in failure before Damascus in 1148.

03-31.title: Saladin arrests the leaders of a pro-Fatimid conspiracy in Cairo
03-31.description: Saladin, the Ayyubid ruler of Egypt, arrested the ringleaders of a conspiracy in Cairo to restore the Fatimid Caliphate, which he had abolished in 1171; among them was the poet Umara al-Yamani. The plot is known only from sources favourable to Saladin.

03-31.title: Pope Gregory X summons the Second Council of Lyon
03-31.description: Pope Gregory X convoked a general council of the Church to discuss reunion of the Churches, a crusade to the Holy Land and Church reform. The Second Council of Lyon met in 1274 and introduced strict conclave rules for papal elections.

03-31.title: Ferdinand and Isabella order the expulsion of Spain's Jews
03-31.description: The Alhambra Decree gave Jews four months to convert or leave. Tens of thousands left, and Sephardic communities took root in the Ottoman Empire, North Africa and the Low Countries.

03-31.title: René Descartes is born in Touraine
03-31.description: The philosopher and mathematician sought certainty through doubt, concluding 'I think, therefore I am'. He also devised the coordinate geometry that links algebra and geometry.

03-31.title: Gustave Eiffel inaugurates his tower in Paris
03-31.description: Eiffel climbed the stairs of his newly completed tower to raise the French flag for the Exposition Universelle. At 300 metres it was the tallest structure in the world until 1930.

03-31.title: United States takes possession of the Danish West Indies
03-31.description: Denmark transferred St Thomas, St John and St Croix, sold for 25 million dollars in gold. The US wanted to deny the islands to Germany and guard the approaches to the Panama Canal.

03-31.title: Lyndon B. Johnson says he will not seek re-election
03-31.description: In a televised address on Vietnam, Johnson announced a partial bombing halt and said he would not run again. Richard Nixon won the presidency that November.

04-01.title: Justin I makes his nephew Justinian co-emperor
04-01.description: The ageing Justin I raised Justinian to co-emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire. Within months he ruled alone, and his reign would reconquer Italy, codify Roman law and raise the Hagia Sophia.

04-01.title: Sea Beggars capture Brielle from Spain
04-01.description: Dutch rebel privateers known as the Sea Beggars seized the port of Brielle. It was the revolt's first secure foothold on land and set off a wave of risings across Holland and Zeeland against Spanish rule.

04-01.title: Sheridan breaks the Confederate line at Five Forks
04-01.description: Union troops under Philip Sheridan routed Confederates at Five Forks, Virginia, cutting Lee's last supply railway into Petersburg. Lee abandoned Petersburg and Richmond the next day.

04-01.title: Royal Air Force formed as the first independent air force
04-01.description: Britain merged the Royal Flying Corps and the Royal Naval Air Service into the Royal Air Force, the world's first air arm independent of army and navy control.

04-01.title: Munich court sentences Hitler to five years for the Beer Hall Putsch
04-01.description: Adolf Hitler received five years' detention for his failed coup of November 1923. He served barely nine months at Landsberg, where he dictated Mein Kampf.

04-01.title: Nazi regime stages a nationwide boycott of Jewish businesses
04-01.description: SA men stood outside Jewish-owned shops, offices and surgeries across Germany to turn customers away. The one-day boycott was the first nationally coordinated anti-Jewish action of the new regime.

04-01.title: Franco declares the Spanish Civil War over
04-01.description: With the last Republican forces surrendered, Francisco Franco announced the end of the war. His victory began a dictatorship that would last until his death in 1975.

04-01.title: US forces land on Okinawa
04-01.description: American troops came ashore on Okinawa in Operation Iceberg, the largest amphibious assault of the Pacific War. The 82-day battle that followed cost the lives of well over 100,000 soldiers and civilians.

04-01.title: Jobs, Wozniak and Wayne found Apple Computer
04-01.description: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne signed the partnership that created Apple Computer in California. Its first product was the hand-built Apple I; Wayne sold his share within days.

04-02.title: Charlemagne is born, by tradition on this day
04-02.description: Charlemagne, future King of the Franks and emperor in the West, was traditionally born on 2 April; the year may have been as late as 748. His empire united much of Western Europe for the first time since Rome.

04-02.title: Ponce de León sights the coast he names La Florida
04-02.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León sighted the Florida coast during the Easter season, Pascua Florida, which gave the land its name. His was the first recorded European landing in what is now the United States.

04-02.title: Bach's cantata Bleib bei uns is first performed in Leipzig
04-02.description: Johann Sebastian Bach's cantata Bleib bei uns, denn es will Abend werden, BWV 6, written for the Lutheran service on Easter Monday, was first performed in Leipzig. Bach had been cantor there since 1723.

04-02.title: US Coinage Act creates the dollar and the Mint
04-02.description: Congress passed the Coinage Act, establishing the United States Mint in Philadelphia and defining the dollar in silver and gold. It laid the foundations of American currency.

04-02.title: A British fleet defeats the Danish-Norwegian fleet at Copenhagen
04-02.description: Because Denmark had joined the League of Armed Neutrality, a British fleet under Sir Hyde Parker, with Horatio Nelson leading the attack, engaged the Danish-Norwegian fleet before Copenhagen. After hard fighting a truce was agreed and Denmark left the league.

04-02.title: Jefferson Davis abandons Richmond as Petersburg falls
04-02.description: As Union troops broke through the Petersburg lines, Confederate President Jefferson Davis and his government fled Richmond by train. Lee surrendered at Appomattox a week later.

04-02.title: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands
04-02.description: Argentine forces seized the British-held Falklands, which Argentina claims as the Malvinas. Britain sent a naval task force; the ten-week war ended in Argentine surrender and hastened the fall of the junta.

04-02.title: Pope John Paul II dies after a 26-year pontificate
04-02.description: John Paul II, the first non-Italian pope in over four centuries, died in the Vatican. His papacy, one of the longest in history, was closely tied to the fall of communism in his native Poland.

04-03.title: Polyeuctus is elected Patriarch of Constantinople
04-03.description: Polyeuctus was elected Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, archbishop of the city and senior bishop of the Eastern Orthodox Church, and held the office until 970. His feast in the Orthodox Church is on 5 February.

04-03.title: Edward the Confessor is crowned king at Winchester
04-03.description: Edward the Confessor, son of Æthelred the Unready and Emma of Normandy, was crowned king of the English in Winchester Cathedral, having succeeded his half-brother Harthacnut in 1042. He was the last reigning monarch of the House of Wessex.

04-03.title: Black Prince defeats Henry of Trastámara at Nájera
04-03.description: Edward the Black Prince routed the Castilian and French army of Henry of Trastámara at Nájera, restoring Peter of Castile. The victory proved short-lived: Henry killed Peter and took the throne two years later.

04-03.title: Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis ends the Italian Wars
04-03.description: France and Spain signed the treaty that closed more than sixty years of war over Italy, a day after a separate Anglo-French peace. Spanish dominance in Italy was confirmed for over a century.

04-03.title: Sweden signs a treaty of amity with the United States
04-03.description: Benjamin Franklin and the Swedish envoy Gustaf Philip Creutz signed a treaty of amity and commerce in Paris. Sweden became the first state not at war with Britain to recognise American independence by treaty.

04-03.title: Pony Express sets off on its first run
04-03.description: Riders left St Joseph, Missouri, and Sacramento, California, carrying mail across some 3,000 km in about ten days. The relay lasted only 18 months before the transcontinental telegraph made it obsolete.

04-03.title: Robert Ford shoots outlaw Jesse James in Missouri
04-03.description: Jesse James was shot dead at his home in St Joseph by Robert Ford, a member of his own gang hoping for a reward. The killing turned the train and bank robber into an enduring figure of American folklore.

04-03.title: British biplanes make the first flight over Everest
04-03.description: Two Westland aircraft of the Houston expedition flew over the summit of Mount Everest, crews breathing bottled oxygen in open cockpits. They brought back the first aerial photographs of the peak.

04-03.title: Martin Luther King gives his 'Mountaintop' speech
04-03.description: In Memphis, Martin Luther King Jr. told supporters he had 'seen the Promised Land' but might not get there with them. It was his last speech; he was assassinated the following evening.

04-04.title: Consul Agrippa Menenius Lanatus celebrates a triumph over the Sabines
04-04.description: Agrippa Menenius Lanatus, a consul of the Roman Republic, celebrated a triumph for his victory over the Sabines, an Italic people of the central Apennine Mountains. The triumph was a ceremonial procession through Rome granted to a victorious general.

04-04.title: Pulakeshin II's inscription records his victory over Harsha
04-04.description: Pulakeshin II, king of the Chalukyas of Badami, issued the Bijapur-Mumbai grant inscription, which mentions his victory over Harsha of Kanauj on the Narmada. The battle therefore took place earlier, probably in the winter of 618–619.

04-04.title: Alexios I Komnenos is crowned Byzantine emperor
04-04.description: Days after his troops took Constantinople from Nikephoros III, Alexios Komnenos was crowned emperor. His dynasty steadied Byzantium for a century, and his appeal to the Pope helped prompt the First Crusade.

04-04.title: US Congress fixes the flag at thirteen stripes
04-04.description: The Flag Act of 1818 set the American flag at thirteen stripes for the original colonies, with a star for every state added on the following 4 July. The rule still governs the flag today.

04-04.title: William Henry Harrison dies a month into his presidency
04-04.description: President William Henry Harrison died 31 days after taking office, the shortest presidency in US history. His death raised the first test of presidential succession, settled when John Tyler took full office.

04-04.title: Lincoln walks through the fallen Confederate capital
04-04.description: Abraham Lincoln toured Richmond, Virginia, two days after its evacuation, greeted by crowds of newly freed Black residents. He sat briefly at Jefferson Davis's desk in the Confederate White House.

04-04.title: Twelve nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty
04-04.description: Foreign ministers meeting in Washington signed the treaty that created NATO, committing members to treat an attack on one as an attack on all. The alliance anchored Western defence through the Cold War.

04-04.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated in Memphis
04-04.description: Martin Luther King Jr. was shot dead on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel, where he had come to support striking sanitation workers. Riots broke out in more than a hundred American cities.

04-04.title: Bill Gates and Paul Allen found Microsoft
04-04.description: Gates and Allen formed a partnership in Albuquerque, New Mexico, to sell a BASIC interpreter for the Altair 8800. Their company went on to dominate personal computer software.

04-05.title: Pope Paschal I crowns Lothar co-emperor in Rome
04-05.description: On Easter Sunday Pope Paschal I crowned Lothar, son of Louis the Pious, as co-emperor in St Peter's. The ceremony reinforced the idea that imperial legitimacy came through papal coronation in Rome.

04-05.title: The Fatimids launch their second invasion of Abbasid Egypt
04-05.description: The Fatimid Caliphate began its second invasion of Egypt, then under Abbasid rule, led again by the heir-apparent al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah. The Fatimids took Alexandria with ease, but the campaign, which lasted until 921, ended in failure.

04-05.title: Alexander Nevsky defeats the Teutonic Order on frozen Lake Peipus
04-05.description: Novgorod's forces under Prince Alexander Nevsky beat the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order in the Battle on the Ice, halting the Order's eastward expansion into Russian lands.

04-05.title: Jacob Roggeveen reaches Easter Island
04-05.description: Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen became the first known European to reach Rapa Nui, naming it after the day of his arrival, Easter Sunday. His crew recorded the island's great stone moai.

04-05.title: George Washington issues the first presidential veto
04-05.description: Washington vetoed a bill apportioning seats in the House of Representatives, judging it unconstitutional. It was the first use of a power that later presidents would wield thousands of times.

04-05.title: Chile declares war on Peru and Bolivia
04-05.description: Chile's declaration opened the War of the Pacific, fought over the nitrate-rich Atacama Desert. Victory gave Chile the coastal provinces and left Bolivia without access to the sea.

04-05.title: Winston Churchill resigns as Prime Minister
04-05.description: Aged 80 and in failing health, Winston Churchill stepped down as Prime Minister and was succeeded by Anthony Eden. It closed a career at the top of British politics spanning more than half a century.

04-05.title: Nirvana's Kurt Cobain dies in Seattle
04-05.description: Kurt Cobain, singer and guitarist of Nirvana, died at his Seattle home aged 27; his body was found three days later. His death closed the band that had carried grunge into the mainstream.

04-06.title: Julius Caesar defeats Metellus Scipio at the Battle of Thapsus
04-06.description: Near Thapsus, in present-day Tunisia, Julius Caesar defeated the Pompeian forces of Metellus Scipio and King Juba I of Numidia. The victory destroyed the republican cause in Africa, and Cato the Younger, Scipio and Juba took their own lives.

04-06.title: Scottish barons date the Declaration of Arbroath
04-06.description: Scotland's nobles sent Pope John XXII a letter asserting the kingdom's independence from England and their right to depose any king who submitted to it. It is one of the most celebrated statements of medieval national identity.

04-06.title: Mehmed II begins the siege of Constantinople
04-06.description: The Ottoman sultan Mehmed II laid siege to Constantinople, capital of the Byzantine Empire. After 53 days, in which heavy artillery played a major role, the city fell on 29 May, ending the Byzantine Empire and becoming the Ottoman capital.

04-06.title: Jan van Riebeeck arrives at the Cape of Good Hope
04-06.description: Jan van Riebeeck reached Table Bay to set up a supply station for the Dutch East India Company. The outpost grew into Cape Town and began European settlement in southern Africa.

04-06.title: Rama I takes the throne and founds the Chakri dynasty
04-06.description: The general Chao Phraya Chakri became king of Siam as Rama I and soon moved the capital across the river to Bangkok. His Chakri dynasty still reigns in Thailand today.

04-06.title: First modern Olympic Games open in Athens
04-06.description: King George I of Greece opened the first modern Olympics at the Panathenaic Stadium. Revived by Pierre de Coubertin, the Games drew some 240 athletes from 14 nations.

04-06.title: Peary and Henson claim to reach the North Pole
04-06.description: Robert Peary, Matthew Henson and four Inuit companions reported reaching the North Pole. Doubts over Peary's navigation mean historians still debate how close they actually came.

04-06.title: United States declares war on Germany
04-06.description: Congress approved President Wilson's request for war, provoked by unrestricted submarine warfare and the Zimmermann Telegram. American troops and resources helped tip the balance on the Western Front.

04-06.title: Gandhi breaks the salt law at Dandi
04-06.description: At the end of his 24-day march to the sea, Mohandas Gandhi picked up a lump of natural salt at Dandi, defying the British monopoly. The gesture launched a mass campaign of civil disobedience across India.

04-07.title: Justinian promulgates the first Code of Roman law
04-07.description: Emperor Justinian issued the Codex Justinianus, gathering imperial constitutions into a single authoritative collection. Revised in 534, it became the core of the Corpus Juris Civilis that shaped European law.

04-07.title: Charles IV founds the university in Prague
04-07.description: Charles IV, King of Bohemia, issued the charter founding a university in Prague, the first in Central Europe. Now Charles University, it later became a centre of the Hussite reform movement.

04-07.title: Antipope Felix V renounces his claim to the papacy
04-07.description: Felix V, the former Duke Amadeus VIII of Savoy, renounced his claim to the papacy, ending the reign of the last antipope. The Council of Basel had elected him in 1439, after he had retired to a hermitage.

04-07.title: Highwayman Dick Turpin is hanged at York
04-07.description: Dick Turpin, convicted of horse theft, was hanged on the Knavesmire at York. The violent robber was later romanticised in fiction as a dashing gentleman of the road.

04-07.title: Congress creates the Mississippi Territory
04-07.description: The US Congress organised the Mississippi Territory on land ceded by Spain in 1795. It was later enlarged and divided into the states of Mississippi and Alabama.

04-07.title: John Walker records the first sale of friction matches
04-07.description: Stockton-on-Tees chemist John Walker sold his newly invented 'friction lights', matches struck against sandpaper. He never patented them, and others soon copied the idea.

04-07.title: Italy invades Albania
04-07.description: Mussolini's forces landed at Durrës and other ports, and within days King Zog had fled. Albania was joined to the Italian crown, and the invasion later served as a base for Italy's attack on Greece.

04-07.title: Genocide against the Tutsi begins in Rwanda
04-07.description: Hours after President Habyarimana's aircraft was shot down, extremists began killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu. In about 100 days an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people were murdered.

04-08.title: Emperor Caracalla is murdered near Carrhae
