06-16.description: Yazdegerd III came to the throne of the Sasanian Empire at the age of eight. His death in 651, after successive defeats by the Rashidun Caliphate, marked the end of the last pre-Islamic Iranian empire.

06-16.title: Ming forces capture Hồ Quý Ly, ruler of Đại Ngu
06-16.description: Ming forces captured Hồ Quý Ly, founder of the Hồ dynasty, and his son Hồ Hán Thương in present-day Hà Tĩnh Province and brought them as prisoners to the Yongle Emperor in Nanjing. Đại Ngu became the Ming province of Jiaozhi.

06-16.title: Henry VII defeats the Yorkist rebels at Stoke Field
06-16.description: Henry VII crushed a rebel army supporting the pretender Lambert Simnel. It is often counted as the last battle of the Wars of the Roses.

06-16.title: Spain declares war on Britain
06-16.description: Spain joined France in the American War of Independence, aiming to recover Gibraltar and Minorca. The Great Siege of Gibraltar that followed lasted more than three years.

06-16.title: Lincoln delivers his 'House Divided' speech
06-16.description: Accepting the Illinois Republican nomination for the Senate, Abraham Lincoln warned that the nation could not endure 'permanently half slave and half free'. The speech raised his national profile.

06-16.title: Ford Motor Company is incorporated
06-16.description: Henry Ford and eleven investors founded the company in Detroit. Its Model T and moving assembly line made cars affordable to millions.

06-16.title: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space
06-16.description: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and orbited Earth 48 times in nearly three days. No other woman flew in space for 19 years.

06-16.title: Police fire on students in Soweto
06-16.description: Police shot at schoolchildren marching against compulsory Afrikaans teaching, killing 13-year-old Hector Pieterson among others. The uprising spread, and hundreds died in the months that followed.

06-17.title: Pope Martin I is arrested for opposing Monothelitism
06-17.description: Pope Martin I, an opponent of Monothelitism, was arrested in the Lateran in Rome with Maximus the Confessor on the orders of Emperor Constans II and taken to Constantinople. He was later banished to Cherson, where he died.

06-17.title: Caliph Uthman is assassinated in Medina
06-17.description: Rebels besieging the house of Uthman ibn Affan, the third Rashidun caliph, who had refused their demand for a new caliph, set it on fire, broke in and killed him. His murder triggered the First Fitna, a civil war.

06-17.title: Vlad the Impaler attacks the Ottoman camp by night
06-17.description: Vlad III of Wallachia led a night raid on Sultan Mehmed II's camp near Târgovişte, failing to kill the sultan. His reputation for cruelty later fed the legend behind Bram Stoker's Dracula.

06-17.title: Francis Drake claims Nova Albion for Elizabeth I
06-17.description: During his circumnavigation, Drake landed on the coast of what is now northern California and claimed it for England as Nova Albion. England made no attempt to settle it.

06-17.title: British take Breed's Hill at heavy cost in the Battle of Bunker Hill
06-17.description: After two failed assaults, British troops drove colonial militia from the heights near Boston. They suffered more than 1,000 casualties, proving the Americans could stand against regulars.

06-17.title: Iceland becomes a republic
06-17.description: At Þingvellir, the site of its ancient assembly, Iceland ended its union with the Danish crown and proclaimed a republic. Denmark was then under German occupation.

06-17.title: Five men are arrested in the Watergate building
06-17.description: Burglars linked to President Nixon's re-election committee were caught inside the Democratic National Committee offices in Washington. The cover-up led to Nixon's resignation in 1974.

06-17.title: O. J. Simpson leads police on a televised chase
06-17.description: About 95 million viewers watched police follow a white Ford Bronco carrying the former football star along Los Angeles freeways. Simpson was later acquitted of murdering his ex-wife and her friend.

06-18.title: Li Yuan proclaims himself emperor, founding the Tang dynasty
06-18.description: After the fall of the Sui, Li Yuan took the throne at Chang'an as Emperor Gaozu. The Tang dynasty presided over one of the most brilliant periods of Chinese culture.

06-18.title: A Rus' fleet sails into the Bosphorus and raids Constantinople's suburbs
06-18.description: A Rus' fleet of about 200 vessels sailed into the Bosphorus and began pillaging the suburbs of Constantinople. It was the only major Rus' expedition recorded in Byzantine and western European sources, and its outcome is unknown in detail.

06-18.title: Timur defeats Tokhtamysh at the Kondurcha River
06-18.description: After a long march across the steppe, Timur defeated his former protégé Tokhtamysh, khan of the Golden Horde, near the Kondurcha River east of present-day Samara. Together with a second defeat on the Terek in 1395, it ruined the Horde.

06-18.title: Charles VII's army defeats the English at Patay
06-18.description: The French vanguard, led by La Hire and Jean Poton de Xaintrailles, defeated an English army at Patay, the culmination of the Loire Campaign. The English lost 2,200 men, and John Talbot was among the senior commanders captured.

06-18.title: United States declares war on Britain
06-18.description: Madison signed the declaration after Congress narrowly voted for war. The War of 1812 ended in stalemate in 1815, but gave Americans 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

06-18.title: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon at Waterloo
06-18.description: The arrival of Blücher's Prussians broke Napoleon's final assault on Wellington's army near Brussels. Napoleon abdicated four days later and was exiled to St Helena.

06-18.title: De Gaulle calls on the French to fight on
06-18.description: Speaking on the BBC from London, General Charles de Gaulle rejected the coming armistice and urged French forces to continue resistance. The appeal founded the Free French movement.

06-18.title: Carter and Brezhnev sign the SALT II treaty
06-18.description: The treaty capped each side's strategic nuclear launchers. The US Senate never ratified it after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, though both sides largely observed its limits.

06-19.title: Louis IX orders Jews in France to wear a badge
06-19.description: An ordinance of Louis IX required Jews to wear a coloured circle of cloth, the rouelle, on their clothing. It enforced a rule of the Fourth Lateran Council of 1215 and marked Jews out for discrimination.

06-19.title: The Earl of Pembroke defeats Robert the Bruce at Methven
06-19.description: The army of Aymer de Valence, Earl of Pembroke, defeated Robert the Bruce's Scottish army at Methven during the Wars of Scottish Independence. Bruce, who had seized the throne that year, survived such early defeats and waged a guerrilla war.

06-19.title: An earthquake and landslides devastate Tongwei in Gansu
06-19.description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.5 struck Tongwei County in Gansu Province, in the Qing Empire, and caused tremendous damage. Landslides triggered by the earthquake killed at least 73,000 people.

06-19.title: Moreau defeats the Austrians at the Battle of Höchstädt
06-19.description: Near Höchstädt on the north bank of the Danube, the French under General Jean Victor Marie Moreau defeated the Austrians under Baron Pál Kray. Kray was forced back into Ulm and later withdrew into Bavaria, opening the Danube route towards Vienna.

06-19.title: Union troops proclaim emancipation in Galveston, Texas
06-19.description: General Gordon Granger announced that all enslaved people in Texas were free, two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation. The day is celebrated as Juneteenth, a US federal holiday since 2021.

06-19.title: Emperor Maximilian of Mexico is executed
06-19.description: Maximilian, the Austrian archduke installed by France as Emperor of Mexico, was shot by firing squad at Querétaro with two of his generals. Benito Juárez's republic was restored.

06-19.title: First Father's Day is held in Spokane
06-19.description: Sonora Smart Dodd organised the celebration to honour her father, a widower who raised six children. Father's Day became a permanent US national holiday in 1972.

06-19.title: Julius and Ethel Rosenberg are executed
06-19.description: The couple were electrocuted at Sing Sing for passing atomic secrets to the Soviet Union. Ethel's role, in particular, remains disputed.

06-19.title: Kuwait gains independence from Britain
06-19.description: An exchange of notes ended the 1899 agreement that made Kuwait a British protectorate. Iraq claimed the new state, and invaded it in 1990.

06-20.title: Aetius checks Attila at the Catalaunian Plains
06-20.description: A coalition of Romans and Visigoths under Aetius fought Attila's Huns to a halt in Gaul, on a date traditionally given as 20 June. Attila withdrew, and invaded Italy the following year.

06-20.title: The First Battle of Uji begins the Genpei War
06-20.description: The First Battle of Uji followed Prince Mochihito and Minamoto no Yorimasa's plan to raise an army to overthrow the Taira clan, and an edict urging the Minamoto clan, temples and shrines to revolt. It began the Genpei War.

06-20.title: Michael I Komnenos Doukas of Epirus becomes a vassal of Venice
06-20.description: A treaty negotiated by envoys of Michael I Komnenos Doukas, founder of the Despotate of Epirus, was confirmed by oath, making him a vassal of Venice. He granted the Venetians trading privileges and tax exemptions and promised an annual tribute.

06-20.title: British captives are confined in the 'Black Hole of Calcutta'
06-20.description: After the Nawab of Bengal took Calcutta, British prisoners were held overnight in a tiny guardroom, where many died. The numbers are disputed, but the story fuelled British retaliation.

06-20.title: Third Estate swears the Tennis Court Oath
06-20.description: Locked out of their hall, deputies of the National Assembly met in a royal tennis court at Versailles and vowed not to separate until France had a constitution.

06-20.title: Victoria becomes queen at the age of 18
06-20.description: Victoria was woken at Kensington Palace with news that William IV had died. Her 63-year reign saw industrial growth and the expansion of the British Empire.
profile: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

06-20.title: US and Soviet Union agree to set up a hotline
06-20.description: Signed in Geneva after the Cuban Missile Crisis, the agreement created a direct teletype link between Washington and Moscow. Popularly called the 'red telephone', it was never a telephone.

06-20.title: Bundestag votes to move Germany's government to Berlin
06-20.description: By 338 votes to 320, the parliament of reunified Germany chose Berlin over Bonn as the seat of government. The move was completed in 1999.

06-21.title: Hannibal ambushes a Roman army at Lake Trasimene
06-21.description: In morning mist on the lake shore, Hannibal trapped the consul Flaminius's army, killing about 15,000 Romans. The disaster led Rome to appoint Fabius Maximus as dictator.

06-21.title: William Clito defeats Thierry of Alsace at Axspoele
06-21.description: William Clito, imposed as Count of Flanders by Louis VI of France after the murder of Charles the Good, defeated his rival Thierry of Alsace at Axspoele. Clito died at the siege of Aalst that year, and Thierry became count.

06-21.title: Külüg Khan is enthroned as emperor of the Yuan Dynasty
06-21.description: Khayishan was enthroned as Külüg Khan, Emperor Wuzong of the Yuan Dynasty of China. He is regarded as the seventh Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, though the title was only nominal because the empire had divided.

06-21.title: An Imperial–Spanish army destroys the French at Landriano
06-21.description: Antonio de Leyva's Imperial–Spanish army destroyed the French army of the Count of Saint-Pol at Landriano in the War of the League of Cognac. It temporarily ended the struggle between Francis I and Emperor Charles V for control of northern Italy.
links: War of the League of Cognac

06-21.title: Edward Cornwallis founds Halifax, Nova Scotia
06-21.description: British settlers arrived to build a fortified town as a counterweight to French Louisbourg. Halifax became a key naval base for Britain and later for Canada.

06-21.title: New Hampshire's ratification puts the US Constitution into effect
06-21.description: New Hampshire became the ninth state to ratify, the number required for the Constitution to take effect. The new federal government began work in 1789.

06-21.title: Louis XVI and his family attempt to flee Paris
06-21.description: In the night of 20–21 June, King Louis XVI and the royal family tried to leave Paris for Montmédy, where he hoped to regain his freedom. Recognised at Sainte-Menehould, they were stopped and arrested at Varennes-en-Argonne.

06-21.title: Wellington routs Joseph Bonaparte at Vitoria
06-21.description: Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese and Spanish army broke the French in northern Spain, capturing their baggage train. Joseph fled, and French rule in Spain collapsed.

06-21.title: Three civil rights workers are murdered in Mississippi
06-21.description: James Chaney, Andrew Goodman and Michael Schwerner were killed by Klansmen, with the involvement of local law officers, during Freedom Summer. Their deaths spurred support for the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

06-22.title: Ptolemy IV defeats Antiochus III at the Battle of Raphia
06-22.description: Ptolemy IV Philopator of Egypt defeated the Seleucid king Antiochus III the Great near present-day Rafah in the Fourth Syrian War, with native Egyptian troops playing a significant role. The battle determined the sovereignty of Coele-Syria.

06-22.title: Rome defeats Macedon at Pydna
06-22.description: Lucius Aemilius Paullus's legions broke the Macedonian phalanx of King Perseus. The Antigonid kingdom was abolished, and Rome became the dominant power in the Greek world.

06-22.title: Khan Krum routs the Byzantine army at Versinikia
06-22.description: Khan Krum of Bulgaria routed the Byzantine army of Emperor Michael I Rangabe near Versinikia, not far from Adrianople in Thrace. The defeat led to Michael's overthrow in favour of Leo V the Armenian, and Krum went on to besiege Adrianople.

06-22.title: Stephen IV is elected pope after the death of Leo III
06-22.description: Stephen IV, of a noble Roman family, was elected pope after the death of Pope Leo III earlier in June. In October he crowned Louis the Pious as emperor at Reims.

06-22.title: Galileo is made to abjure before the Inquisition
06-22.description: Found 'vehemently suspect of heresy', Galileo formally abjured the view that the Earth moves around the Sun. He spent the rest of his life under house arrest.

06-22.title: Lord Mansfield rules in the Somerset case
06-22.description: The judge held that James Somerset, an enslaved man brought to England, could not be forcibly removed abroad. The ruling was widely taken to mean slavery had no basis in English law.

06-22.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
06-22.description: Operation Barbarossa sent some three million Axis troops across a front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. The war in the east became the largest and deadliest land conflict in history.

06-22.title: Roosevelt signs the G.I. Bill
06-22.description: The Servicemen's Readjustment Act gave veterans college tuition, low-cost home loans and unemployment pay. Millions took up its benefits, expanding higher education and home ownership.

06-23.title: Venice captures the whole Genoese fleet off Trapani
06-23.description: A Venetian fleet under Jacopo Dondulo captured all 27 ships of the Genoese fleet under Lanfranco Borbonino off Trapani, Sicily. The War of Saint Sabas between Genoa and Venice was fought over control of Acre.

06-23.title: Granada defeats Castile and León at the Battle of Moclín
06-23.description: Troops of the Emirate of Granada defeated the forces of Castile and León at Moclín, in the battle also called the Disaster of Moclín. Ruled by the Nasrid dynasty, Granada was the last independent Muslim state in Western Europe.

06-23.title: France and Flanders make peace at Athis-sur-Orge
06-23.description: King Philip IV of France and Robert III of Flanders signed the Treaty of Athis-sur-Orge, ending the Franco-Flemish War after the French victory at Mons-en-Pévèle. It imposed on Flanders a heavy indemnity, acts of penance and the demolition of town fortifications.

06-23.title: Battle of Bannockburn begins
06-23.description: On the first day, Robert the Bruce killed the English knight Henry de Bohun in single combat before the armies. Edward II's larger army was routed the next day.

06-23.title: Robert Clive defeats the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey
06-23.description: Helped by the defection of Mir Jafar, Clive's East India Company troops defeated Siraj ud-Daulah. The victory gave the Company control of Bengal and launched British territorial rule in India.

06-23.title: June Days uprising erupts in Paris
06-23.description: Workers rose after the government closed the National Workshops. General Cavaignac crushed them in four days; thousands were killed and many more deported.

06-23.title: Christopher Latham Sholes patents a typewriter
06-23.description: Sholes and his partners received a patent for a 'Type-Writer'. Developed further and sold by Remington, it popularised the QWERTY keyboard and transformed office work.

06-23.title: Nixon approves using the CIA to block the Watergate inquiry
06-23.description: In a taped conversation, Nixon agreed that the CIA should ask the FBI to halt its investigation. The release of this 'smoking gun' tape in August 1974 forced his resignation.

06-23.title: United Kingdom votes to leave the European Union
06-23.description: In a referendum, 52 per cent voted to leave the EU. Prime Minister David Cameron resigned, and Britain formally left in January 2020.

06-24.title: Western Roman emperor Glycerius is forced to abdicate
06-24.description: Glycerius, proclaimed emperor of the West in March 473 by the magister militum Gundobad and not recognised by the Eastern emperor Leo I, was forced to abdicate. The Western Roman Empire ended in 476, when the last emperor was deposed.

06-24.title: Afonso Henriques defeats his mother's forces at São Mamede
06-24.description: Near Guimarães, Afonso Henriques defeated the forces of his mother, Countess Teresa, and her Galician ally Fernão Peres de Trava. The victory gave him control of the County of Portugal and is traditionally seen as the founding event of Portuguese independence.

06-24.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Bannockburn
06-24.description: On the second day, Scottish spearmen drove the English army into the burns and marshes near Stirling. Edward II fled, and Scotland's independence was secured until England recognised it in 1328.

06-24.title: Edward III destroys the French fleet at Sluys
06-24.description: The English fleet of King Edward III attacked the French fleet assembled for an invasion of England in the Zwin estuary off Sluis, in Flanders, and destroyed it almost entirely. The victory gave England control of the Channel for years.

06-24.title: An outbreak of dancing mania begins in Aachen
06-24.description: One of the biggest outbreaks of dancing mania, in which groups of people danced erratically, allegedly until they collapsed from exhaustion, began in Aachen. It spread to Cologne, Flanders, Metz, Strasbourg, Utrecht and other places, and to Italy.

06-24.title: John Cabot makes landfall in North America
06-24.description: Sailing for Henry VII, the Venetian navigator John Cabot landed on the coast, probably of Newfoundland or Cape Breton. His voyage became the basis of later English claims in North America.

06-24.title: Premier Grand Lodge of England is founded
06-24.description: Four London lodges met at the Goose and Gridiron alehouse to form a Grand Lodge. It marks the beginning of organised modern Freemasonry.

06-24.title: Napoleon's Grande Armée crosses the Niemen into Russia
06-24.description: Some 450,000 troops in the first wave crossed into Russian territory. By December only a fraction had survived the retreat from Moscow.

06-24.title: Soviet Union begins the Berlin Blockade
06-24.description: Soviet forces cut road, rail and canal links to West Berlin. The Western Allies responded with an airlift that supplied the city's two million people for eleven months.

06-25.title: Charles the Bald and Louis the German defeat Lothair I at Fontenoy
06-25.description: Charles the Bald and Louis the German defeated their brother Lothair I and Pepin II of Aquitaine at Fontenoy, the largest battle of the Carolingian civil war. It was not decisive: fighting went on until the Treaty of Verdun in 843.

06-25.title: Venice defeats a Genoese relief fleet off Acre
06-25.description: Off Acre, the Venetian fleet won a crushing victory over a larger Genoese fleet under Rosso della Turca, sent to break the Venetian blockade of the Genoese quarter. It was part of the War of Saint Sabas.

06-25.title: Jews accused of a blood libel are burned in Schaffhausen
06-25.description: In Schaffhausen, in present-day Switzerland, 30 Jews accused in a blood libel of murdering a four-year-old boy were tortured into confessing and burned. The town's Jews had already been burned in 1349 after an accusation of well poisoning.

06-25.title: Elena Cornaro Piscopia becomes the first woman to earn a doctorate
06-25.description: The Venetian scholar was awarded a doctorate in philosophy by the University of Padua. She is the first woman known to have received a university doctoral degree.

06-25.title: Virginia ratifies the US Constitution
06-25.description: Despite Patrick Henry's opposition, Virginia narrowly ratified, the tenth state to do so. Without the largest state, the new union could hardly have worked.

06-25.title: Lakota and Cheyenne defeat Custer at the Little Bighorn
06-25.description: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors killed Lieutenant Colonel George Custer and some 268 soldiers in Montana Territory. The US Army responded with campaigns that ended Plains resistance.

06-25.title: North Korea invades South Korea
06-25.description: North Korean troops crossed the 38th parallel in force. The Korean War drew in UN forces and China and ended in a 1953 armistice near the original line.

06-25.title: Croatia and Slovenia declare independence
06-25.description: The two republics broke away from Yugoslavia on the same day. A brief war in Slovenia was followed by much longer conflicts in Croatia and Bosnia.

06-26.title: Benedict II is consecrated pope after imperial approval
06-26.description: Benedict II was consecrated bishop of Rome after receiving the approval of the Byzantine emperor, as popes then required. He was the last pope to need the emperor's confirmation; his successors needed only that of the exarch of Ravenna.

06-26.title: Mongols crush the Seljuks of Rûm at Köse Dağ
06-26.description: A Mongol army under Baiju defeated Sultan Kaykhusraw II in north-eastern Anatolia. The Seljuk sultanate became a Mongol vassal and broke into the principalities from which the Ottomans emerged.

06-26.title: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno
06-26.description: Przemysł II, Duke of Greater Poland, was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno Cathedral, the first royal coronation in Poland for over two centuries. He returned Poland to the rank of kingdom but was murdered at Rogoźno the following February.

06-26.title: The Council of Pisa elects Alexander V, a third rival pope
06-26.description: Having declared Gregory XII of Rome and Benedict XIII of Avignon deposed, the Council of Pisa elected Peter of Candia as Alexander V, a third claimant in the Western Schism. He died in 1410 and is now regarded as an antipope.

06-26.title: Warwick and the Earl of March land at Sandwich
06-26.description: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, landed at Sandwich with a rebel army and the Earls of Salisbury and March, and the three earls rode to London. Warwick and March went on to take King Henry captive at Northampton on 10 July.

06-26.title: George IV dies at Windsor
06-26.description: The former Prince Regent, known for extravagance and his patronage of architecture, died at 67. His brother William IV succeeded him, and the Great Reform Act followed in 1832.

06-26.title: Queen Victoria presents the first Victoria Crosses
06-26.description: In Hyde Park, Queen Victoria decorated 62 servicemen for valour in the Crimean War. The Victoria Cross remains Britain's highest award for gallantry.
profile: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

06-26.title: United Nations Charter is signed in San Francisco
06-26.description: Delegates of 50 nations signed the Charter creating the United Nations to maintain peace and security. It came into force in October 1945.

06-26.title: Kennedy tells West Berlin 'Ich bin ein Berliner'
06-26.description: Speaking at Rathaus Schöneberg to a crowd of about 450,000, President Kennedy declared solidarity with the people of the walled city two years after the Berlin Wall went up.

06-27.title: The Roman army proclaims Jovian emperor after Julian's death
06-27.description: After Emperor Julian was killed in battle on his Persian expedition, the Roman army declared Jovian, of the imperial bodyguard, his successor. Jovian then made a peace that let the Sasanian Empire under Shapur II recover Nisibis and other territories.

06-27.title: Agatho begins his pontificate as bishop of Rome
06-27.description: Agatho became bishop of Rome, serving until his death in 681. During his tenure the Sixth Ecumenical Council was convened to deal with monothelitism, and he is venerated as a saint by both the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.

06-27.title: The Stratford Martyrs are burned for their Protestant beliefs
06-27.description: Eleven men and two women, the Stratford Martyrs, were burned at the stake together for their Protestant beliefs during the Marian persecutions, at Stratford-le-Bow or Stratford, Essex, both near London.

06-27.title: George II leads his army to victory at Dettingen
06-27.description: In the War of the Austrian Succession, an allied army under George II beat the French in Bavaria. It was the last time a reigning British monarch commanded troops in battle.

06-27.title: Mormon founder Joseph Smith is killed by a mob
06-27.description: Militiamen stormed the jail in Carthage, Illinois, where Smith and his brother Hyrum were held, and shot them dead. Brigham Young later led most of his followers west to Utah.

06-27.title: Sailors mutiny aboard the battleship Potemkin
06-27.description: Crew of the Russian Black Sea Fleet battleship rose against their officers after a dispute over rotten meat. The mutiny became a symbol of the 1905 Revolution, later immortalised by Eisenstein.

06-27.title: UN Security Council calls on members to defend South Korea
06-27.description: Resolution 83 recommended that members help South Korea repel the North's attack. The Soviet Union was boycotting the Council and could not veto it.

06-27.title: Gordon Brown succeeds Tony Blair as Prime Minister
06-27.description: After ten years as Chancellor, Gordon Brown became Prime Minister. His premiership was dominated by the global financial crisis of 2008.

06-28.title: Alboin, king of the Lombards, is assassinated in Verona
06-28.description: Alboin, king of the Lombards, was murdered at Verona in a plot involving his wife Rosamund and instigated by the Byzantines. He had led the Lombards into Italy in 568 and conquered much of its north.

06-28.title: Crusaders break out of Antioch and rout Kerbogha
06-28.description: Besieged in the city they had just taken, and inspired by the supposed discovery of the Holy Lance, the crusaders defeated the army of Kerbogha of Mosul. The road to Jerusalem lay open.

06-28.title: Edward IV is crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey
06-28.description: Edward IV, the first Yorkist king, was crowned at Westminster Abbey after winning the throne in the Wars of the Roses with victories at Mortimer's Cross and Towton. He reigned, with a brief interruption, until 1483.

06-28.title: The French rout a Spanish and Neapolitan army at Seminara
06-28.description: In the First Italian War, a French force of gendarmes and Swiss pikemen routed a larger Spanish and Neapolitan army at Seminara in Calabria. The defeat led to Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's creation of the tercios.

06-28.title: Charles of Spain is elected Holy Roman Emperor
06-28.description: The electors chose Charles I of Spain over Francis I of France. As Charles V he ruled Spain, the Low Countries, Austria and much of Italy and the Americas.

06-28.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau is born in Geneva
06-28.description: Rousseau's The Social Contract and Émile shaped political thought and education, and his Confessions helped create modern autobiography. His ideas inspired French revolutionaries.

06-28.title: Archduke Franz Ferdinand is assassinated in Sarajevo
06-28.description: Gavrilo Princip shot the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne and his wife Sophie. Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia set off the July Crisis and the First World War.

06-28.title: Treaty of Versailles is signed
06-28.description: Germany signed the peace in the Hall of Mirrors, five years to the day after Sarajevo. It accepted territorial losses, disarmament and reparations, which fuelled lasting resentment.

06-29.title: Avars and Persians begin their assault on Constantinople
06-29.description: Some 80,000 Avars and Slavs, allied with the Sasanian Persians, began a coordinated assault on the walls of Constantinople, defended by some 12,000 Byzantine troops. After a month of bombardment, with their fleets sunk, the attackers abandoned the siege.

06-29.title: The former emperor Romanos IV Diogenes is blinded
06-29.description: The former emperor Romanos IV Diogenes had agreed to resign and enter a monastery in return for his life, but the caesar John Doukas broke the agreement and had him blinded at Kotyaion. He died in exile soon afterwards.

06-29.title: Nur al-Din defeats and kills Raymond of Poitiers at Inab
06-29.description: During the Second Crusade, the Zengid army of Nur al-Din Zengi destroyed the army of Raymond of Poitiers, Prince of Antioch, and the Assassins of Ali ibn-Wafa at Inab. Raymond was killed, and Antioch's eastern border was pushed west.

06-29.title: Skanderbeg defeats an Ottoman army at Torvioll
06-29.description: Leading the League of Lezhë, Skanderbeg defeated an Ottoman army under Ali Pasha at Torvioll in Albania, attacking its flanks and rear with troops hidden in the woods. It was his first major victory over the Ottomans.

06-29.title: Globe Theatre burns down during Henry VIII
06-29.description: A cannon fired for a stage effect set the thatched roof alight, and Shakespeare's playhouse burned to the ground within an hour. No one was killed, and it was rebuilt the next year.

06-29.title: Spanish found Mission San Francisco de Asís
06-29.description: Franciscan friars celebrated the first Mass at the mission later known as Mission Dolores, as Spain expanded northward in California. The settlement grew into San Francisco.

06-29.title: The Daily Telegraph is first published
06-29.description: The Daily Telegraph and Courier appeared in London. Under new owners it soon became a penny paper and for a time had the largest circulation in the world.

06-29.title: Roger Casement is sentenced to death for treason
06-29.description: The Irish nationalist and former British diplomat was condemned for seeking German help for the Easter Rising. Despite pleas for clemency he was hanged in August.

06-29.title: Sampoong Department Store collapses in Seoul
06-29.description: The five-storey store fell in seconds, killing 502 people. Investigators found illegal alterations and ignored warnings, prompting reforms of South Korean building safety.

06-30.title: Constantine V defeats the Bulgarian khan Telets at Anchialus
06-30.description: Byzantine Emperor Constantine V defeated the Bulgarian khan Telets near Anchialus on the Black Sea coast, one of the greatest victories of his long campaigns against Bulgaria. The defeat deepened a crisis in Bulgaria, where rulers were overthrown in quick succession.

06-30.title: Zhu Yunwen ascends the Ming throne as the Jianwen Emperor
06-30.description: After the death of the Hongwu Emperor, founder of the Ming dynasty, his grandson Zhu Yunwen ascended the throne as the Jianwen Emperor. Hongwu had named him successor when his father, the heir apparent Zhu Biao, died in 1392.

06-30.title: The Duchy of Milan defeats the Swiss at Arbedo
06-30.description: The forces of the Duchy of Milan defeated those of the Swiss Confederation, the alliance of Swiss cantons, at the Battle of Arbedo.

06-30.title: Cortés flees Tenochtitlan on the Noche Triste
06-30.description: Under attack by the Mexica, Cortés's forces fought their way out of the city along the causeways at night, losing hundreds of Spaniards and many more Tlaxcalan allies. He returned to besiege it in 1521.

06-30.title: Henry II of France is mortally wounded in a joust
06-30.description: A splinter from the lance of the Count of Montgomery pierced the king's eye at a tournament in Paris. His death ten days later left France to weak young sons on the eve of the Wars of Religion.

06-30.title: Einstein's paper on special relativity reaches the journal
06-30.description: Annalen der Physik received 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', which showed that measurements of time and space depend on motion. E = mc² followed in a short sequel that autumn.

06-30.title: Tunguska explosion flattens Siberian forest
06-30.description: An asteroid or comet fragment exploded above the Tunguska river, levelling some 2,000 square km of forest. It is the largest impact event in recorded history.

06-30.title: Hitler purges the SA in the Night of the Long Knives
06-30.description: SS squads killed SA chief Ernst Röhm and other rivals, including the former chancellor Kurt von Schleicher. The army welcomed the purge, and Hitler's grip on power tightened.

06-30.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
06-30.description: At midnight, at a ceremony attended by the Prince of Wales and President Jiang Zemin, sovereignty passed to China after 156 years of British rule. Hong Kong became a Special Administrative Region.

07-01.title: Crusaders defeat the Seljuk Turks at Dorylaeum
07-01.description: The First Crusade routed the army of Kilij Arslan I at Dorylaeum in Anatolia. The victory opened the road across Asia Minor and showed that the crusaders could beat the Seljuks in open battle.

07-01.title: Castile wins a modest victory at La Higueruela near Granada
07-01.description: The army of John II of Castile, led by Álvaro de Luna, defeated the forces of the Nasrid emir Muhammad IX outside Granada but did not take the city. Castile instead installed a rival claimant, Yusuf IV, as emir.

07-01.title: William III defeats James II at the Battle of the Boyne
07-01.description: William of Orange defeated the deposed James II on the River Boyne in Ireland (1 July Old Style). The victory secured the Protestant succession and is still commemorated by the Orange Order each July.

07-01.title: Continental Congress debates independence in a decisive test vote
07-01.description: Meeting as a committee of the whole, Congress debated Richard Henry Lee's resolution for independence; nine colonies backed it in a test vote. The formal vote followed the next day with twelve in favour.

07-01.title: Union guns repel Lee's assaults at Malvern Hill
07-01.description: Massed Union artillery shattered Confederate attacks at Malvern Hill near Richmond, the last of the Seven Days Battles. Though McClellan withdrew afterwards, Lee's costly assaults ended the campaign.

07-01.title: The Battle of Gettysburg begins in Pennsylvania
07-01.description: Confederate and Union forces collided at Gettysburg, opening the largest battle ever fought in North America. Three days later Lee's army withdrew, having suffered some 23,000 of the roughly 50,000 casualties.

07-01.title: British army suffers 57,470 casualties on the first day of the Somme
07-01.description: After a week-long bombardment, British and French infantry attacked along the Somme. Britain lost 57,470 men killed, wounded or missing, the heaviest single-day toll in the British Army's history.

07-01.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
07-01.description: At midnight sovereignty over Hong Kong passed from Britain to China, ending 156 years of British rule. The territory became a Special Administrative Region under the 'one country, two systems' principle.

07-02.title: Li Shimin kills his brothers in the Xuanwu Gate Incident
07-02.description: Prince Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji at the Xuanwu Gate of Chang'an. Within two months his father abdicated, and as Emperor Taizong he presided over a golden age of Tang China.

07-02.title: Wu Zetian is buried beside Emperor Gaozong at Qianling
07-02.description: Wu Zetian, the only woman to rule China as emperor in her own right, was interred in a joint burial with her husband, the Tang emperor Gaozong, in the Qianling Mausoleum, where he had been buried in 684.

07-02.title: A Breton-Viking army defeats the Franks at Brissarthe
07-02.description: A joint Breton-Viking army defeated the West Franks near Brissarthe in Neustria, killing the Neustrian margrave Robert the Strong and Ranulf I, Duke of Aquitaine. Robert's sons Odo and Robert I both later became kings of West Francia.

07-02.title: Spain ratifies the Treaty of Tordesillas
07-02.description: Spain ratified the Treaty of Tordesillas, signed on 7 June, which divided newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Castile along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands. It later allowed Portugal to claim Brazil.

07-02.title: Continental Congress votes for independence from Britain
07-02.description: Congress adopted the Lee Resolution declaring the colonies free and independent states, with twelve in favour and New York abstaining. John Adams predicted that 2 July would be celebrated for ever; posterity chose the 4th.

07-02.title: Union troops hold Little Round Top on Gettysburg's second day
07-02.description: Confederate assaults struck the Union left at Little Round Top, the Wheatfield and the Peach Orchard. The Union line held its high ground by a narrow margin, setting the stage for Pickett's Charge the next day.

07-02.title: First Zeppelin airship flies over Lake Constance
07-02.description: Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's LZ 1 made its maiden flight from a floating hangar on Lake Constance. It was the first flight of a rigid airship, beginning an era that ended with the Hindenburg disaster of 1937.

07-02.title: Amelia Earhart disappears over the Pacific
07-02.description: Amelia Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan vanished while searching for tiny Howland Island on the last long legs of their round-the-world flight. Despite a vast search, their fate has never been conclusively established.

07-02.title: Lyndon Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act
07-02.description: President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, outlawing discrimination on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex or national origin. It ended legal segregation in public places and was the most sweeping civil rights law since Reconstruction.

07-03.title: Constantine I defeats Licinius at the Battle of Adrianople
07-03.description: In their second civil war, Emperor Constantine I soundly defeated his rival and former colleague Licinius at Adrianople in Thrace. After a further defeat at Chrysopolis, Licinius surrendered and was executed in 325.

07-03.title: Hugh Capet is crowned King of the Franks
07-03.description: Hugh Capet was crowned, replacing the Carolingian line with his own family. The Capetians and their cadet branches would rule France almost without a break until 1848.

07-03.title: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec
07-03.description: Samuel de Champlain established a fortified trading post at Quebec on the St Lawrence. It became the capital of New France and the heart of French-speaking North America, a culture that endures in Canada today.

07-03.title: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to the French
07-03.description: Outnumbered and rain-soaked, the 22-year-old Washington surrendered Fort Necessity in western Pennsylvania. It was the only surrender of his military career and an opening clash of the French and Indian War.

07-03.title: George Washington takes command of the Continental Army at Cambridge
07-03.description: General George Washington, newly appointed commander-in-chief of the Continental Army and dispatched by the Second Continental Congress, took command of the Patriot soldiers camped on Cambridge Common, now regarded as the birthplace of the American army.

07-03.title: Pickett's Charge fails on the final day of Gettysburg
07-03.description: Some 12,500 Confederates advanced across open fields against the Union centre on Cemetery Ridge and were cut down. The repulse ended Lee's invasion of the North and is often called the high-water mark of the Confederacy.

07-03.title: Karl Benz drives his Motorwagen in public in Mannheim
07-03.description: Karl Benz made the first public drive of his three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen on the Ringstrasse in Mannheim. Patented that January, it is widely regarded as the first practical petrol-powered motor car.

07-03.title: USS Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Flight 655
07-03.description: The US cruiser Vincennes, mistaking the Airbus for an attacking fighter, shot down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 on board. The tragedy deepened hostility between Washington and Tehran.

07-04.title: Saladin destroys the Crusader army at the Battle of Hattin
07-04.description: Near Tiberias in Galilee, Sultan Saladin destroyed the army of the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem and captured its king, Guy of Lusignan. The victory allowed Saladin to retake Jerusalem later that year.

07-04.title: Sultan Mehmed II begins the siege of Belgrade
07-04.description: Ottoman forces led by Sultan Mehmed II began the siege of Belgrade, then held by Hungary and crucial for control of the Danube and the Balkans. The siege lasted until 22 July, and John Hunyadi relieved the city.

07-04.title: Continental Congress adopts the Declaration of Independence
07-04.description: Congress approved the final text of the Declaration, drafted chiefly by Thomas Jefferson. Its assertion that all men are created equal, with unalienable rights, became the founding statement of the United States.

07-04.title: US Military Academy opens at West Point
07-04.description: The United States Military Academy formally opened at West Point, New York. It went on to train generations of officers, among them Grant, Lee, Eisenhower and MacArthur.

07-04.title: John Adams and Thomas Jefferson die on the same day
07-04.description: Former presidents John Adams and Thomas Jefferson died within hours of each other on the 50th anniversary of the Declaration. Adams's reported last words were 'Thomas Jefferson survives', unaware his rival had died first.

07-04.title: Vicksburg surrenders to Ulysses S. Grant
07-04.description: After a 47-day siege, John Pemberton surrendered Vicksburg and nearly 30,000 men. With Port Hudson falling days later, the Union controlled the Mississippi and split the Confederacy in two.

07-04.title: Polish leader Władysław Sikorski dies in a crash at Gibraltar
07-04.description: General Sikorski, prime minister of the Polish government-in-exile, was killed when his aircraft crashed seconds after take-off from Gibraltar. His death removed the Allies' most respected Polish voice at a critical moment.

07-04.title: The Philippines gains independence from the United States
07-04.description: The Philippines became a sovereign republic after nearly half a century of American rule, as promised by the 1934 Tydings-McDuffie Act. For decades 4 July was celebrated as its Independence Day.

07-04.title: Mars Pathfinder lands on Mars
07-04.description: NASA's Pathfinder bounced to a landing on airbags in Ares Vallis and soon deployed Sojourner, the first rover on another planet. The mission returned thousands of images and revived public interest in Mars.

07-05.title: Constantine's Bridge over the Danube is officially opened
07-05.description: Constantine's Bridge, a Roman bridge over the Danube between Sucidava in present-day Romania and Oescus in Bulgaria, built by the architect Theophilus Patricius, was officially opened. Used to reconquer Dacia, it remained in use for four decades.

07-05.title: Louis of Burgundy defeats Ferdinand of Majorca at Manolada
07-05.description: At Manolada in the Peloponnese, Louis of Burgundy defeated and killed Ferdinand of Majorca, his rival for the Principality of Achaea. The result kept Achaea under Angevin supremacy and checked Ferdinand's allies, the Catalan Company occupying the Duchy of Athens.

07-05.title: Isaac Newton publishes the Principia
07-05.description: Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica was published in London. It set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation, giving physics the framework that dominated science for more than two centuries.

07-05.title: French forces capture Algiers
07-05.description: The Dey of Algiers surrendered to a French expeditionary force, beginning 132 years of French rule in Algeria. The colonisation ended only after a long and bloody war of independence.

07-05.title: William Booth begins the mission that becomes the Salvation Army
07-05.description: Methodist preacher William Booth began evangelising in London's East End, founding the Christian Mission. Renamed the Salvation Army in 1878, it grew into a worldwide church and charity.

07-05.title: Louis Réard unveils the bikini at a Paris swimming pool
07-05.description: Engineer and designer Louis Réard presented his two-piece swimsuit at the Piscine Molitor, modelled by dancer Micheline Bernardini. He named it after Bikini Atoll, where atomic tests had just begun.

07-05.title: The National Health Service launches in Britain
07-05.description: Aneurin Bevan's National Health Service began, offering comprehensive care free at the point of use to everyone in Britain. It became one of the defining institutions of the post-war welfare state.

07-05.title: Algeria becomes independent from France
07-05.description: Algeria proclaimed independence, 132 years to the day after French troops took Algiers. It followed an eight-year war of liberation and a referendum in which Algerians voted overwhelmingly for independence.

07-06.title: Thebes under Epaminondas defeats Sparta at Leuctra
07-06.description: The Thebans and their Boeotian allies under Epaminondas defeated a Spartan army near Leuctra in Boeotia, killing King Cleombrotus I. The defeat ended the belief in Spartan invincibility and began a decade of Theban supremacy in Greece.

07-06.title: Richard the Lionheart becomes King of England
07-06.description: Henry II died at Chinon, and his son Richard succeeded him. Famed as a crusader against Saladin, Richard spent barely six months of his ten-year reign in England.

07-06.title: Zheng He returns to Nanjing from the third treasure voyage
07-06.description: Admiral Zheng He returned to Nanjing from the third treasure voyage and presented his Sinhalese captives, including their king, taken in the Ming–Kotte War, to the Yongle Emperor. The emperor decided to free them and return them to their country.

07-06.title: Jan Hus is burned at the stake in Constance
07-06.description: The Czech reformer Jan Hus, condemned as a heretic by the Council of Constance despite a promise of safe conduct, was burned. His death provoked the Hussite revolt in Bohemia a century before Luther.

07-06.title: Richard III is crowned at Westminster Abbey
07-06.description: Richard, Duke of Gloucester, was crowned after his nephew Edward V was declared illegitimate. Two years later his death at Bosworth ended Plantagenet rule and brought the Tudors to the throne.

07-06.title: Monmouth's rebellion is crushed at Sedgemoor
07-06.description: Royal troops routed the Duke of Monmouth's rebel army at Sedgemoor in Somerset, often called the last pitched battle on English soil. Judge Jeffreys's 'Bloody Assizes' followed.

07-06.title: German ambassador Mirbach is assassinated in Moscow
07-06.description: Left Socialist Revolutionaries shot Count Wilhelm von Mirbach in the German embassy, hoping to wreck the Brest-Litovsk peace. Their uprising was crushed and the Bolsheviks became Russia's sole ruling party.

07-06.title: Fire sweeps a circus big top in Hartford, killing 167
07-06.description: The Ringling Bros. tent, waterproofed with paraffin and petrol, caught fire during a matinee in Hartford, Connecticut. At least 167 people died, many of them children, prompting tighter fire-safety rules.

07-07.title: Joan of Arc is cleared of heresy 25 years after her death
07-07.description: A retrial authorised by Pope Callixtus III quashed Joan of Arc's 1431 conviction and declared her innocent. She was canonised as a saint in 1920.

07-07.title: The Treaty of Nemours ends toleration of Protestants in France
07-07.description: At Nemours, the Queen Mother Catherine de' Medici, acting for King Henry III, signed articles with representatives of the House of Guise abolishing toleration of Protestants. Contemporaries saw the accord as a renewal of the French Wars of Religion.

07-07.title: American rearguard fights the British at Hubbardton
07-07.description: Retreating from Fort Ticonderoga, an American rearguard fought pursuing British and German troops at Hubbardton, Vermont. Though defeated, they slowed Burgoyne's advance towards eventual surrender at Saratoga.

07-07.title: Napoleon and Alexander I sign the first Treaty of Tilsit
07-07.description: Napoleon and Emperor Alexander I of Russia signed the first of the Treaties of Tilsit, ending hostilities between France and Russia in the War of the Fourth Coalition after the French victory at Friedland. Russia joined the Continental System against Britain.

07-07.title: President McKinley signs the resolution annexing Hawaii
07-07.description: McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution, annexing the Republic of Hawaii five years after American businessmen had overthrown Queen Liliuokalani. Hawaii became a US territory and, in 1959, the 50th state.

07-07.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident sparks war between China and Japan
07-07.description: A night-time clash between Japanese and Chinese troops at the Marco Polo Bridge near Beijing escalated into full-scale war. The Second Sino-Japanese War merged into the Second World War and cost millions of Chinese lives.

07-07.title: Boris Becker, 17, becomes Wimbledon's youngest men's champion
07-07.description: Unseeded West German Boris Becker beat Kevin Curren in four sets to win Wimbledon at 17. He remains the youngest men's singles champion in the tournament's history.

07-07.title: Suicide bombers kill 52 on London's transport network
07-07.description: Four bombers struck three Underground trains and a bus during the morning rush hour, killing 52 people. It was Britain's deadliest terrorist attack since Lockerbie, a day after London won the 2012 Olympics.

07-08.title: Crusaders process barefoot around the walls of Jerusalem
07-08.description: Weakened by thirst and heat, the crusaders fasted and walked barefoot around besieged Jerusalem, ending on the Mount of Olives. A week later their final assault took the city.

07-08.title: The Byzantines decisively defeat the Hungarians at Sirmium
07-08.description: The Byzantine army of Manuel I Komnenos, under Andronikos Kontostephanos, decisively defeated the Hungarians near Sirmium, forcing them to sue for peace on Byzantine terms. Byzantium was left in control of Syrmia, Dalmatia and Bosnia for a time.

07-08.title: Roger of Lauria defeats an Angevin fleet at Malta
07-08.description: An Aragonese fleet under Roger of Lauria defeated Angevin galleys at the entrance to Malta's Grand Harbour during the War of the Sicilian Vespers. The Angevin fleet had been sent to put down a rebellion on the island.

07-08.title: Vasco da Gama sails from Lisbon for India
07-08.description: Vasco da Gama left Lisbon with four ships on a voyage that rounded the Cape of Good Hope and reached Calicut in 1498. The sea route to India launched Portugal's maritime empire in Asia.

07-08.title: Peter the Great crushes the Swedish army at Poltava
07-08.description: Russian forces destroyed the army of Charles XII at Poltava in Ukraine. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and announced Russia as the dominant force in northern Europe.

07-08.title: The Declaration of Independence is first read in public in Philadelphia
07-08.description: Colonel John Nixon read the Declaration to a crowd in the State House yard, now Independence Square. Tradition holds that the Liberty Bell rang out, though this story dates from the nineteenth century.

07-08.title: Commodore Perry's 'Black Ships' arrive in Edo Bay
07-08.description: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored four warships off Uraga and demanded that Japan open its ports. The visit ended two centuries of restricted contact and set Japan on the path to rapid modernisation.

07-08.title: The Wall Street Journal publishes its first issue
07-08.description: Dow Jones and Company, founded by Charles Dow, Edward Jones and Charles Bergstresser, launched the Wall Street Journal. It became one of the world's most influential financial newspapers.

07-09.title: Avitus is acclaimed Western Roman Emperor near Arles
07-09.description: Backed by the Visigoths and the Gallo-Roman nobility, the senator Avitus was acclaimed emperor near Arles. His reign lasted barely a year, a sign of how weak the Western Empire had become.

07-09.title: Silla defeats Baekje at the Battle of Hwangsanbeol
07-09.description: Near present-day Nonsan, a large Silla army under Kim Yu-sin destroyed a small Baekje force; its commander, General Gyebaek, was killed. With a Tang army landing at the same time, the Baekje capital Sabi fell within days, ending the kingdom.

07-09.title: Jawhar al-Siqilli leads the Friday prayer in Fustat
07-09.description: The Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli led the Friday prayer in Fustat in the name of Caliph al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah, symbolically completing the conquest of Egypt. The Fatimids then founded Cairo as their new capital, making Egypt the centre of their power.

07-09.title: The Swiss defeat Duke Leopold III of Austria at Sempach
07-09.description: Swiss Confederates defeated the army of Duke Leopold III of Austria near Sempach, in the canton of Lucerne, killing Leopold and many of his nobles. Together with the victory at Näfels in 1388, it confirmed the Confederacy's independence from Habsburg rule.

07-09.title: New Yorkers topple George III's statue after the Declaration is read
07-09.description: Washington had the Declaration read to his troops in New York. That evening a crowd pulled down the gilded lead statue of George III on Bowling Green; much of the lead was later cast into musket balls.

07-09.title: Napoleon annexes the Kingdom of Holland to France
07-09.description: Days after his brother Louis abdicated rather than enforce the blockade of British trade, Napoleon decreed Holland's annexation to the French Empire. Dutch independence was restored only in 1813.

07-09.title: The 14th Amendment wins enough states for ratification
07-09.description: South Carolina's and Louisiana's approval gave the 14th Amendment the three-quarters of states it needed. It guaranteed citizenship to all born in the US and equal protection of the laws.

07-09.title: The first Wimbledon Championships begin
07-09.description: The All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club opened its first lawn tennis championship, with 22 men competing. Spencer Gore won the title ten days later, launching the world's oldest tennis tournament.

07-09.title: South Sudan becomes independent
07-09.description: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan after a referendum, becoming the world's newest internationally recognised state. Independence followed decades of civil war, but a new conflict erupted in 2013.

07-10.title: Prince Naka no Ōe assassinates Soga no Iruka
07-10.description: Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari killed the minister Soga no Iruka, beginning the Isshi incident, a plot to eliminate the main branch of the Soga clan. The end of Soga power opened the way to the Taika reforms.

07-10.title: Portugal and John of Gaunt sign the Treaty of Tagilde
07-10.description: King Ferdinand I of Portugal and representatives of John of Gaunt, Duke of Lancaster and claimant to the Crown of Castile, signed a treaty at the village of Tagilde. It is considered the first legal foundation of the Anglo-Portuguese Alliance.

07-10.title: The Earl of Warwick captures Henry VI at Northampton
07-10.description: Near the River Nene, Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, and Edward, Earl of March, defeated the Lancastrian army of King Henry VI and took the king prisoner. It was the first battle in England in which artillery was used.

07-10.title: Lady Jane Grey is proclaimed Queen of England
07-10.description: Days after Edward VI's death, the Duke of Northumberland had his Protestant daughter-in-law proclaimed queen to bar the Catholic Mary Tudor. Jane's reign lasted nine days; she was executed the following year.

07-10.title: William the Silent is assassinated in Delft
07-10.description: Balthasar Gérard shot William of Orange, leader of the Dutch revolt against Spain, at his home in Delft. He is often cited as the first head of state killed with a handgun.

07-10.title: Wyoming becomes the 44th US state
07-10.description: Wyoming joined the Union with women's suffrage intact; as a territory it had given women the vote in 1869. Congress accepted the state despite opposition to its equal-suffrage clause.

07-10.title: The Scopes 'Monkey Trial' opens in Tennessee
07-10.description: Teacher John Scopes went on trial in Dayton for teaching human evolution. The clash between Clarence Darrow and William Jennings Bryan turned a local case into a national debate on science and faith.

07-10.title: The Battle of Britain begins
07-10.description: The Luftwaffe began attacking Channel convoys and coastal targets, the date Britain uses for the start of the Battle of Britain. The RAF's survival over four months forced Hitler to postpone his invasion.

07-10.title: Telstar is launched, the first satellite to relay live TV
07-10.description: NASA launched AT&T's Telstar 1 from Cape Canaveral. Within hours it relayed the first television pictures across the Atlantic, opening the age of satellite communications.

07-11.title: Baldwin IV becomes king of Jerusalem at thirteen
07-11.description: After Amalric died, leaving an underage heir, the thirteen-year-old Baldwin IV became king of Jerusalem despite his leprosy. Raymond III of Tripoli served as regent and William of Tyre as chancellor.

07-11.title: Flemish militia defeat French knights at the Battle of the Golden Spurs
07-11.description: Flemish townsmen on foot routed the French cavalry at Courtrai, collecting hundreds of golden spurs from the dead. The battle showed that disciplined infantry could beat mounted knights.

07-11.title: Charles of Luxembourg is elected King of the Romans
07-11.description: Five prince-electors meeting at Rhens chose Charles of Luxembourg as rival king to Louis IV. Later crowned emperor as Charles IV, he issued the Golden Bull of 1356 that fixed imperial elections for centuries.

07-11.title: An imperial edict orders Zheng He's first treasure voyage
07-11.description: An imperial edict addressed to Zheng He, Wang Jinghong and others gave the order for the first Ming treasure voyage. Zheng He led seven such expeditions through South-East Asia and the Indian Ocean between 1405 and 1433.

07-11.title: Congress re-establishes the US Marine Corps
07-11.description: An Act of Congress created the US Marine Corps as a permanent service, reviving the Continental Marines of the Revolution. It grew into one of America's most celebrated fighting forces.

07-11.title: Aaron Burr mortally wounds Alexander Hamilton in a duel
07-11.description: Vice President Aaron Burr shot Alexander Hamilton at Weehawken, New Jersey; Hamilton died the next day. The death of the first Treasury Secretary ended Burr's political career.

07-11.title: Babe Ruth makes his major league debut for the Red Sox
07-11.description: Nineteen-year-old Babe Ruth pitched for the Boston Red Sox against Cleveland, winning his first major league game. He went on to become baseball's greatest slugger and a symbol of the 1920s.

07-11.title: Skylab falls to Earth over Western Australia
07-11.description: NASA's Skylab space station broke up on re-entry, scattering debris near Esperance in Western Australia. The local shire jokingly fined NASA for littering; an American radio host paid the fine in 2009.

07-12.title: Æthelstan receives the submission of northern rulers at Eamont
07-12.description: At Eamont, near Penrith, four rulers, among them King Constantine II of Alba, King Hywel Dda of Deheubarth and Ealdred of Bamburgh, accepted Æthelstan's overlordship. Seven years of peace in the north followed.

07-12.title: Acre surrenders to the armies of the Third Crusade
07-12.description: After a siege of almost two years, the garrison of Acre surrendered to Richard I and Philip II. The port became the crusaders' main base and later capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

07-12.title: Pope Benedict XII issues a bull to reform the Cistercians
07-12.description: At Sorgues, Pope Benedict XII issued the bull Fulgens sicut stella matutina to reform the Cistercian Order. It prescribed economic consolidation of indebted houses, compulsory attendance at the general chapter, stricter discipline and reorganised theological studies for monks.

07-12.title: The Ottomans capture Negroponte and the island of Euboea
07-12.description: Sultan Mehmed II personally led the Ottoman siege of Negroponte (Chalcis), capital of the Venetian possession of Euboea. After almost a month, and despite heavy losses, the Ottomans took both the city and the island.

07-12.title: Henry VIII marries Catherine Parr, his sixth wife
07-12.description: Henry VIII married the twice-widowed Catherine Parr at Hampton Court. She outlived him, helped reconcile the king with his daughters and became the first English queen to publish a book in her own name.

07-12.title: Williamite army wins the Battle of Aughrim
07-12.description: William III's forces under Godert de Ginkel defeated the Jacobite army at Aughrim in County Galway (12 July Old Style). The bloodiest battle in Irish history effectively decided the Williamite war.

07-12.title: Lincoln signs the act creating the Army Medal of Honor
07-12.description: President Lincoln signed a resolution authorising the Medal of Honor for army soldiers who distinguished themselves by gallantry. It remains the highest US military decoration.

07-12.title: Soviet and German tanks clash at Prokhorovka
07-12.description: Soviet tank armies counter-attacked the SS Panzer Corps at Prokhorovka, one of the largest tank battles in history. The Soviets lost heavily, but the German offensive at Kursk was halted.

07-12.title: Malala Yousafzai is born in Pakistan's Swat Valley
07-12.description: Malala Yousafzai was born in Mingora. Shot by the Taliban in 2012 for campaigning for girls' education, she survived and in 2014 became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.

07-13.title: Kalbid army defeats Emperor Otto II at Stilo
07-13.description: The forces of the Kalbid emir of Sicily routed Otto II's army near Stilo in Calabria, though the emir himself was killed. Otto barely escaped by swimming to a ship, and his plans to conquer southern Italy collapsed.

07-13.title: William the Lion of Scotland is captured at Alnwick
07-13.description: English knights surprised King William I of Scotland in fog outside Alnwick and took him prisoner. To win his release he accepted the Treaty of Falaise, submitting Scotland to Henry II's overlordship.

07-13.title: Alexander III is crowned king of Scots
07-13.description: Alexander III, king since 6 July, was crowned king of Scots. In his reign, later remembered as a golden age, Scotland gained the Western Isles and the Isle of Man from Norway by the Treaty of Perth.

07-13.title: Samogitians rout the Teutonic and Livonian knights at Durbe
07-13.description: Near Durbe, in present-day western Latvia, Samogitian forces routed the combined army of the Livonian Order and the Teutonic Order; about 150 knights died, including the Livonian master Burchard von Hornhausen. The defeat set off the Great Prussian Uprising.

07-13.title: Congress passes the Northwest Ordinance
07-13.description: The Confederation Congress set out how lands north-west of the Ohio River would be governed and admitted as new states. It also banned slavery there, shaping the pattern of American westward expansion.

07-13.title: Queen Victoria moves into Buckingham Palace
07-13.description: Three weeks after her accession, 18-year-old Victoria became the first monarch to live at Buckingham Palace. It has been the sovereign's principal London residence ever since.

07-13.title: The Treaty of Berlin redraws the map of the Balkans
07-13.description: The Congress of Berlin recognised the independence of Serbia, Montenegro and Romania and cut back the large Bulgaria created by Russia. Its compromises left grievances that fed later Balkan wars.

07-13.title: The Hollywoodland sign is dedicated in Los Angeles
07-13.description: A giant sign reading 'Hollywoodland' was unveiled in the hills above Los Angeles to advertise a housing development. Shortened to 'Hollywood' in 1949, it became a global symbol of the film industry.

07-14.title: Emperor Otto II is defeated at the Battle of Stilo
07-14.description: Near Crotone in Calabria, the forces of Emperor Otto II and his Italo-Lombard allies were defeated by those of Abu'l-Qasim, the Kalbid emir of Sicily, who had declared a holy war against the Germans.

07-14.title: Louis VIII becomes King of France on Philip Augustus's death
07-14.description: Philip II died at Mantes and his son Louis VIII succeeded him. In a reign of just three years Louis took Poitou from the English and led a royal crusade against the Cathars of the south.

07-14.title: Jan Žižka's Hussites defeat the crusaders at Vítkov Hill
07-14.description: On a hill at the eastern edge of Prague, Hussite forces under Jan Žižka repulsed the army of the first crusade against the Hussites, led by King Sigismund. Sigismund lifted the siege of Prague soon afterwards.

07-14.title: The Teutonic Order wins the Battle for Kneiphof
07-14.description: The Battle for Kneiphof, fought since April for Königsberg's port district, ended in a decisive victory for the Teutonic Order. In the Thirteen Years' War the Order faced the Prussian Confederation and its ally, Poland.

07-14.title: Parisians storm the Bastille
07-14.description: Crowds seeking gunpowder stormed the Bastille fortress, which held just seven prisoners. Its fall became the symbol of the French Revolution, and 14 July is France's national day.

07-14.title: John Adams signs the Sedition Act
07-14.description: The Sedition Act made it a crime to publish 'false, scandalous and malicious' writing against the US government. It was used to prosecute Republican editors and helped Jefferson win the 1800 election.

07-14.title: Edward Whymper's party makes the first ascent of the Matterhorn
07-14.description: A seven-man team led by Edward Whymper reached the summit of the Matterhorn. On the descent a rope broke and four men fell to their deaths, a tragedy that shocked Victorian Britain.

07-14.title: Nazi Germany becomes a one-party state
07-14.description: The Law against the Formation of New Parties declared the Nazi Party the only legal party in Germany. Less than six months after Hitler became chancellor, organised political opposition had been outlawed.

07-14.title: Iraqi army officers overthrow the Hashemite monarchy
07-14.description: Officers led by Brigadier Abd al-Karim Qasim seized Baghdad and killed King Faisal II and members of the royal family. The coup ended the British-backed monarchy and made Iraq a republic.

07-15.title: Mutinous guards kill the chancellor Yang Guozhong at Mawei
07-15.description: When the imperial party fleeing the An Lushan Rebellion stopped at Mawei Station, guard soldiers blaming the chancellor Yang Guozhong for the chaos killed him and his family. Emperor Xuanzong was forced to order the death of his consort Yang Guifei.

07-15.title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
07-15.description: Crusaders broke into Jerusalem and slaughtered many of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants. The capture fulfilled the First Crusade's goal and led to the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

07-15.title: Alexander Nevsky defeats the Swedes on the Neva
07-15.description: A Novgorodian army led by Alexander Nevsky, with Karelian allies, defeated a Swedish force that included Norwegian, Finnish and Tavastian troops on the Neva River near Ust-Izhora. The clash was part of the Swedish–Novgorodian Wars over the Gulf of Finland.

07-15.title: John Ball, a leader of the Peasants' Revolt, is executed
07-15.description: The priest John Ball, a leader of the Peasants' Revolt, was hanged, drawn and quartered in the presence of King Richard II. The rising had been put down after Wat Tyler was killed at Smithfield.

07-15.title: Poland and Lithuania crush the Teutonic Knights at Grunwald
07-15.description: King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas destroyed the army of the Teutonic Order at Grunwald, killing its grand master. One of medieval Europe's largest battles, it broke the order's power.

07-15.title: Napoleon surrenders aboard HMS Bellerophon
07-15.description: Unable to escape to America, Napoleon gave himself up to Captain Frederick Maitland of HMS Bellerophon off Rochefort. The British exiled him to Saint Helena, where he died in 1821.

07-15.title: William Boeing founds his aircraft company in Seattle
07-15.description: Timber merchant William Boeing incorporated the Pacific Aero Products Company, renamed Boeing Airplane Company the next year. It grew into a leading aerospace maker, builder of the 707 and 747.

07-15.title: Gianni Versace is shot dead outside his Miami Beach home
07-15.description: Fashion designer Gianni Versace was murdered on the steps of his villa by Andrew Cunanan, who had already killed four men. Cunanan killed himself eight days later as police closed in.

07-16.title: The Islamic calendar begins its first year
07-16.description: The first day of the year of the Hijra, 1 Muharram AH 1, corresponds to 16 July 622. Caliph Umar later chose the year of Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina as the starting point of the Islamic era.

07-16.title: The Byzantines defeat Tsar Samuel's Bulgarians at the Spercheios
07-16.description: A Byzantine army under General Nikephoros Ouranos defeated the Bulgarian army of Tsar Samuel on the Spercheios river near Lamia in central Greece. The victory virtually destroyed the Bulgarian army and ended its raids in the southern Balkans and Greece.

07-16.title: Papal legates excommunicate the patriarch of Constantinople in Hagia Sophia
07-16.description: During the liturgy in Hagia Sophia, Cardinal Humbert and his fellow legates, whose authority had lapsed with the pope's death, laid a charter excommunicating Patriarch Michael I Cerularius on the altar. Historians often date the East–West Schism from this act.

07-16.title: Christian kings defeat the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa
07-16.description: The kings of Castile, Aragon and Navarre routed the Almohad caliph's army in the Sierra Morena. The battle broke Almohad power in Iberia and opened Andalusia to Christian conquest.

07-16.title: Arjona elects the future Muhammad I of Granada as its leader
07-16.description: After the final Friday prayer of Ramadan, a mosque assembly in Arjona declared the town's independence from Ibn Hud and elected Muhammad ibn Yusuf as its leader. He went on to found the Nasrid dynasty and the Emirate of Granada.

07-16.title: Stockholms Banco issues Europe's first banknotes
07-16.description: Sweden's Stockholms Banco began issuing paper credit notes, the first banknotes in Europe. The bank over-issued and collapsed within a few years, but paper money was here to stay.

07-16.title: The first atomic bomb is detonated in New Mexico
07-16.description: The Trinity test at 5.29 am in the Jornada del Muerto desert proved the plutonium bomb worked. Oppenheimer later recalled the Bhagavad Gita: 'Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.'

07-16.title: Apollo 11 launches for the Moon
07-16.description: A Saturn V rocket lifted Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins from Kennedy Space Center. Four days later Armstrong and Aldrin became the first people to land on the Moon.

07-16.title: Fragments of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 begin hitting Jupiter
07-16.description: Over six days some 21 fragments of the comet slammed into Jupiter, the first collision between solar system bodies ever observed. They left dark scars in the atmosphere larger than Earth.

07-17.title: Zhu Di takes the Ming throne as the Yongle Emperor
07-17.description: Zhu Di, fourth son of the dynasty's founder, the Hongwu Emperor, became the third Ming emperor, having seized the throne from his nephew. He later moved the capital to Beijing and began building the Forbidden City.

07-17.title: Charles VII is crowned king of France at Reims
07-17.description: Charles VII, king of France since 1422, was crowned in Reims Cathedral, the traditional place of French coronations, after Joan of Arc had raised the siege of Orléans. He went on to recover northern France and Gascony from the English.

07-17.title: French artillery wins the Battle of Castillon
07-17.description: French cannon cut down an English army under John Talbot at Castillon in Gascony. It was the last battle of the Hundred Years' War, leaving Calais as England's only possession in France.

07-17.title: Deposed Tsar Peter III dies in captivity
07-17.description: Days after his wife Catherine seized the throne in a coup, Peter III died at Ropsha, almost certainly murdered by her supporters. Catherine the Great went on to rule Russia for 34 years.

07-17.title: Bolsheviks execute the Romanov family in Yekaterinburg
07-17.description: In the early hours, Nicholas II, his wife, their five children and four retainers were shot in the cellar of the Ipatiev House. Their remains were found decades later; the Orthodox Church canonised the family in 2000.

07-17.title: The Potsdam Conference opens
07-17.description: Truman, Stalin and Churchill, later replaced by Attlee, met at Cecilienhof near Berlin. They settled the occupation of Germany and issued the Potsdam Declaration demanding Japan's unconditional surrender.

07-17.title: American and Soviet spacecraft dock in orbit
07-17.description: An Apollo capsule docked with Soyuz 19, and Thomas Stafford and Alexei Leonov shook hands through the hatch. The first international crewed space mission was a landmark of Cold War détente.

07-17.title: TWA Flight 800 explodes off Long Island
07-17.description: A Boeing 747 bound for Paris exploded minutes after take-off from New York, killing all 230 on board. Investigators concluded that a spark had ignited fuel vapour in the centre wing tank.

07-18.title: Veii ambushes and destroys the Fabii at the Cremera
07-18.description: The Etruscan city of Veii ambushed the Roman Fabii, who had been raiding its territory, and killed them all at the Cremera. Only Quintus Fabius Vibulanus, too young to go to war, survived in Rome.

07-18.title: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out
07-18.description: Fire broke out near the Circus Maximus and raged for days, gutting ten of Rome's fourteen districts. Rumour blamed Nero; Tacitus records that he blamed the Christians, beginning their first persecution.

07-18.title: The Almohads defeat Alfonso VIII of Castile at Alarcos
07-18.description: The Almohad caliph Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur defeated King Alfonso VIII of Castile, whose army retreated to Toledo, while the Almohads retook Trujillo, Montánchez and Talavera. The battle marked the high point of Almohad power in Iberia.

07-18.title: Edward I orders the expulsion of the Jews from England
07-18.description: Edward I issued the Edict of Expulsion, ordering all Jews to leave England by 1 November. Several thousand were forced out, and Jews were not readmitted until the Cromwellian era of the 1650s.

07-18.title: England and France agree the Truce of Leulinghem
07-18.description: Richard II's England and Charles VI's France, both facing serious internal troubles, agreed the Truce of Leulinghem, ending the Caroline War of the Hundred Years' War. It began a 13-year peace, the longest of the war.

07-18.title: The 54th Massachusetts leads the assault on Fort Wagner
07-18.description: The 54th Massachusetts, one of the first Black regiments in the Union army, led a night attack on Fort Wagner near Charleston. The assault failed with heavy losses, but the regiment's courage changed Northern opinion.

07-18.title: The First Vatican Council defines papal infallibility
07-18.description: The council adopted Pastor aeternus, declaring the Pope free from error when he defines doctrine on faith or morals ex cathedra. The decree strengthened papal authority and caused a schism with the Old Catholics.

07-18.title: The first volume of Hitler's Mein Kampf is published
07-18.description: Hitler's autobiography and manifesto, written partly in prison, set out his antisemitism and his aim of conquering 'living space' in the east. Its ideas foreshadowed the policies of the Third Reich.

07-18.title: Military uprising launches the Spanish Civil War
07-18.description: Following the army revolt in Morocco the day before, garrisons across Spain rose against the Republic. The war lasted nearly three years and ended in General Franco's dictatorship.

07-19.title: The rebel general Leontius is crowned emperor at Tarsus
07-19.description: Leontius, a general of the Eastern Roman Empire, was crowned emperor at Tarsus in a rebellion against Emperor Zeno that lasted until 488. He was recognised in Antioch and made it his capital.

07-19.title: Tariq ibn Ziyad defeats King Roderic at Guadalete
07-19.description: Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeated and killed the Visigothic king Roderic, by the traditional date. Within a few years most of Iberia was under Muslim rule, the beginning of al-Andalus.

07-19.title: A Fatimid army defeats the Byzantines at the Battle of Apamea
07-19.description: Byzantine forces under Damian Dalassenos, besieging Apamea, were winning against a Fatimid relief army until a lone Kurdish rider killed Dalassenos and their army fled in panic. The defeat forced Emperor Basil II to campaign there in person the next year.

07-19.title: The English defeat the Scots at Halidon Hill
