09-23.title: Pope Callixtus II and Henry V agree the Concordat of Worms
09-23.description: At Worms, Pope Callixtus II and Emperor Henry V ended the Investiture Controversy. The emperor gave up investing bishops with ring and staff, while in Germany elections were held in his presence and he granted the elected bishop the regalia.

09-23.title: The French defeat the English at the Battle of Arnemuiden
09-23.description: At the start of the Hundred Years' War, a French force defeated the English in the war's first naval battle. It was the first recorded European naval battle using artillery: the English ship Christopher carried three cannons and one handgun.

09-23.title: The Yorkists win the Battle of Blore Heath
09-23.description: At Blore Heath in Staffordshire, near Market Drayton, the Yorkists won a battle of the Wars of the Roses, the struggle between the houses of Lancaster and York for the English throne that lasted until 1487.

09-23.title: The Royalists win the skirmish at Powick Bridge
09-23.description: In the first engagement between the principal field armies of the Royalists and Parliamentarians, Prince Rupert's Royalist force defeated a Parliamentarian detachment under Colonel John Brown south of Worcester. Brown had been sent to capture a Royalist convoy of valuables.

09-23.title: John Paul Jones captures HMS Serapis off Flamborough Head
09-23.description: In a brutal moonlit battle, John Paul Jones's sinking Bonhomme Richard captured HMS Serapis off Yorkshire. His later-reported reply 'I have not yet begun to fight' became a naval legend.

09-23.title: Johann Galle discovers Neptune
09-23.description: At the Berlin Observatory, Johann Galle found Neptune within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier had calculated. It was the first planet found by mathematical prediction.

09-23.title: Sigmund Freud dies in London
09-23.description: Freud, who had fled Nazi-occupied Vienna the year before, died aged 83 after his doctor gave him lethal doses of morphine at his request. His theories of the unconscious reshaped twentieth-century thought.

09-24.title: Pepin the Short dies, leaving the Franks to Charlemagne and Carloman
09-24.description: King Pepin died at Saint-Denis, dividing his kingdom between his sons Charles and Carloman, who were crowned in October. After Carloman's death in 771, Charlemagne ruled alone.

09-24.title: The Second Council of Nicaea opens
09-24.description: The Second Council of Nicaea opened in the church of Hagia Sophia at Nicaea, the site of the first ecumenical council. About 350 members attended under the presidency of Tarasios, and 308 bishops or their representatives signed its acts.

09-24.title: Basil I has Emperor Michael III assassinated
09-24.description: Basil I, a peasant's son whom Michael III had made co-emperor the year before, had Michael assassinated in his chamber and became sole ruler. He founded the Macedonian dynasty, which ruled for nearly two centuries.

09-24.title: Parliamentarians defeat Charles I at the Battle of Rowton Heath
09-24.description: Parliamentarian forces under Sydnam Poyntz inflicted a significant defeat on the Royalists under the personal command of King Charles I, with heavy losses, preventing him from relieving the siege of Chester.

09-24.title: Washington signs the Judiciary Act
09-24.description: The Judiciary Act set up the federal court system, fixed the Supreme Court at six justices and created the office of Attorney General. It remains the foundation of the US federal judiciary.

09-24.title: Gold price collapses on 'Black Friday'
09-24.description: Jay Gould and James Fisk's attempt to corner the gold market collapsed when the Grant administration sold Treasury gold. Prices crashed and many speculators were ruined.

09-24.title: B. R. Ambedkar and Hindu leaders sign the Poona Pact
09-24.description: Agreed with Gandhi during his fast, the Poona Pact was signed, replacing separate electorates for the 'depressed classes' with reserved seats. Gandhi ended his fast against separate electorates two days later.

09-24.title: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature
09-24.description: The CTBT, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN and was signed first by President Clinton. It has not entered into force, as key states have not ratified it.

09-25.title: Harold II defeats Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge
09-25.description: King Harold of England surprised and destroyed the Norwegian army near York, killing Harald Hardrada and Tostig. Three days later William of Normandy landed in the south, forcing Harold to march back.

09-25.title: Henry III and Alexander II agree the Treaty of York
09-25.description: At York, Henry III of England and Alexander II of Scotland agreed that Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland were subject to English sovereignty. The treaty fixed the Anglo-Scottish border almost as it remains, ending Scottish attempts to extend the frontier south.

09-25.title: Bayezid I routs Sigismund's crusaders at Nicopolis
09-25.description: On the lower Danube, the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I routed a crusading army led by King Sigismund of Hungary. The defeat ended the last large-scale joint crusade of medieval Europe and left the Ottomans firmly in control of Bulgaria.

09-25.title: Balboa becomes the first European to see the Pacific from the Americas
09-25.description: Vasco Núñez de Balboa climbed a peak on the Isthmus of Panama and sighted the 'South Sea'. Days later he waded into the water and claimed it and all its shores for Castile.

09-25.title: The Peace of Augsburg is signed
09-25.description: Agreed between Emperor Charles V's government and the Lutheran princes, the treaty let each ruler in the Holy Roman Empire choose Lutheranism or Catholicism as his state's official confession. Calvinism was not allowed until the Peace of Westphalia.

09-25.title: The English Parliament accepts the Solemn League and Covenant
09-25.description: The English Parliament and the Westminster Assembly accepted the Solemn League and Covenant with the Scottish Covenanters, already approved by the Church of Scotland. It promised religious reforms in England and Ireland in exchange for Scottish troops against King Charles I.

09-25.title: Ethan Allen fails to capture Montreal at Longue-Pointe
09-25.description: Ethan Allen and a small force of American and Quebec militia failed in an attempt to capture Montreal from the British. Major John Brown, who Allen claimed was to bring reinforcements, did not appear, leaving them isolated across the St Lawrence.

09-25.title: Congress proposes the amendments that become the Bill of Rights
09-25.description: The First Congress sent twelve proposed amendments to the states. Ten were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, protecting freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly.

09-25.title: Sonny Liston knocks out Floyd Patterson to win the world title
09-25.description: Sonny Liston took the world heavyweight title in Chicago by knocking out Floyd Patterson in 2 minutes 6 seconds of the first round. He lost the title to Cassius Clay in 1964.

09-26.title: Julius Caesar dedicates the Temple of Venus Genetrix
09-26.description: Amid the celebrations of his triumphs, Caesar dedicated a temple to Venus Genetrix, the mythical ancestress of his family, in his new forum. It proclaimed his divine lineage and unrivalled power.

09-26.title: William II of England is crowned king
09-26.description: William II, called Rufus, the third son of William the Conqueror, was crowned king of England. He put down rebellions by barons who favoured his elder brother Robert Curthose, and in 1096 took Normandy in pledge from Robert.

09-26.title: The Ottomans destroy a Serbian army at the Battle of Maritsa
09-26.description: At Chernomen on the Maritsa river, an Ottoman force under Lala Şahin Pasha destroyed the army of the Serbian king Vukašin and the despot Jovan Uglješa, both of whom were killed. The defeat opened Macedonia to the Ottomans.

09-26.title: A French army defeats the English at La Brossinière
09-26.description: In the Hundred Years' War, a French army defeated English forces at La Brossinière, in a battle also known as the Battle of la Gravelle.

09-26.title: Francis Drake returns from his voyage around the world
09-26.description: The Golden Hind sailed into Plymouth after nearly three years, laden with Spanish treasure. Drake was the first captain to complete a circumnavigation and was knighted aboard his ship the next April.

09-26.title: A Venetian shell blows apart the Parthenon
09-26.description: During the Venetian siege of the Acropolis, a mortar shell ignited Ottoman gunpowder stored in the Parthenon. The explosion destroyed the temple's centre and killed some 300 people.

09-26.title: Einstein's paper on special relativity is published
09-26.description: Annalen der Physik published Einstein's 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', which showed that measurements of time and space depend on the observer's motion. It transformed physics.

09-26.title: Stanislav Petrov judges a Soviet missile alert a false alarm
09-26.description: Duty officer Stanislav Petrov saw satellite warnings of US missile launches and reported them as a malfunction rather than an attack. He was right, and may have averted a nuclear war.

09-27.title: The Teutonic Order defeats the Poles at the Battle of Płowce
09-27.description: At Płowce, forces of the Kingdom of Poland fought the Teutonic Order; the Poles were defeated, but their leaders escaped capture.

09-27.title: The Treaty of Melno fixes the Prussian–Lithuanian border
09-27.description: Signed near Lake Melno by the Teutonic Knights and the Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, the treaty ended the Gollub War. The Order gave up its claims to Samogitia, and the border it fixed lasted about five centuries.

09-27.title: Suleiman the Magnificent begins the siege of Vienna
09-27.description: Suleiman the Magnificent attacked Vienna with over 100,000 men in the first Ottoman attempt to take the Habsburg capital, defended by no more than 21,000 under Niklas Graf Salm. The city held out until the siege ended on 15 October.

09-27.title: Pope Paul III approves the Society of Jesus
09-27.description: The bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae formally established Ignatius of Loyola's Jesuits. The order became a leading force of the Catholic Reformation, founding schools and missions worldwide.

09-27.title: Venice surrenders Candia to the Ottomans
09-27.description: The Venetians handed over Candia, modern Heraklion, ending a siege of more than 21 years, one of the longest in history. Crete passed to Ottoman rule.

09-27.title: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens
09-27.description: George Stephenson drove Locomotion No. 1, hauling coal wagons and hundreds of passengers, on the opening run. It was the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives.

09-27.title: Germany, Italy and Japan sign the Tripartite Pact
09-27.description: The three powers signed a ten-year military alliance in Berlin, pledging mutual aid if attacked by a power not yet at war, aimed chiefly at the United States. It formalised the Axis.

09-27.title: The Warren Commission report is made public
09-27.description: The commission's report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald alone had killed President Kennedy. Its findings have been widely debated ever since.

09-28.title: Pompey is murdered on landing in Egypt
09-28.description: Fleeing after Pharsalus, Pompey the Great was stabbed to death as he stepped ashore, on the orders of Ptolemy XIII's advisers. Caesar is said to have wept when shown his rival's head.

09-28.title: Duke Wenceslaus I of Bohemia is murdered by his brother Boleslaus
09-28.description: Wenceslaus I, Prince of Bohemia since 921, was murdered by nobles led by his younger brother Boleslaus, who became duke in his place. The year was probably 935, though 929 is also given.

09-28.title: William of Normandy lands at Pevensey
09-28.description: William's invasion fleet landed unopposed on the Sussex coast while King Harold was in the north. Just over two weeks later William won the Battle of Hastings.

09-28.title: Henry I of England defeats and captures Robert Curthose at Tinchebray
09-28.description: In Normandy, King Henry I of England defeated the Norman army of his elder brother Robert Curthose, Duke of Normandy, and captured him. Robert spent the rest of his life in captivity, and Henry reunited Normandy with England.

09-28.title: Louis IV defeats and captures Frederick the Fair at Mühldorf
09-28.description: Near Mühldorf am Inn, Louis IV of Bavaria defeated and captured his cousin and rival king Frederick the Fair of Austria. It is often described as one of the last great battles of mounted knights fought without firearms.

09-28.title: American and French armies begin the siege of Yorktown
09-28.description: Washington and Rochambeau's forces closed in on Cornwallis at Yorktown, Virginia, while a French fleet blocked escape by sea. Cornwallis surrendered on 19 October, effectively ending the war.

09-28.title: Alexander Fleming notices the mould that leads to penicillin
09-28.description: Back from holiday, Alexander Fleming found a mould killing bacteria on a culture plate in his London laboratory. Developed into a drug in the 1940s, penicillin opened the antibiotic era.

09-28.title: Ferdinand Marcos dies in exile in Hawaii
09-28.description: Former Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos died in Honolulu, three years after the People Power Revolution drove him from power. His regime was notorious for martial law and plunder.

09-29.title: Pompey celebrates his third triumph
09-29.description: Pompey the Great celebrated his third triumph, for his victories over the pirates and the end of the Mithridatic Wars, on his 45th birthday. The settlement of 63 BCE had seen Rome annex Pontus and Syria.

09-29.title: Pope Benedict III is restored by a popular uprising
09-29.description: After Louis II of Italy, Carolingian emperor, tried to replace him with his own favoured candidate, Benedict III was restored to the papacy by a popular uprising. He reigned as bishop of Rome until his death in April 858.

09-29.title: Pope Gregory IX excommunicates Emperor Frederick II
09-29.description: Gregory IX excommunicated Frederick II for again delaying his promised crusade. Frederick went anyway, regaining Jerusalem by treaty in 1229 and crowning himself in the Holy Sepulchre.

09-29.title: Henry III recognises Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales
09-29.description: In the Treaty of Montgomery, Henry III recognised Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales, with overlordship of the other Welsh lords, in return for homage and a large payment. Disputes over these led to Edward I's invasion of 1277.

09-29.title: Anglo-Breton forces win the Battle of Auray
09-29.description: At Auray, Anglo-Breton forces defeated the Franco-Breton army in the decisive battle of the War of the Breton Succession, the struggle between the counts of Blois and the Montforts for the Duchy of Brittany. The war ended the following April.

09-29.title: Horatio Nelson is born in Norfolk
09-29.description: Horatio Nelson was born at Burnham Thorpe, the son of a rector. He won the battles of the Nile and Copenhagen and died at his greatest victory, Trafalgar, in 1805.

09-29.title: London's Metropolitan Police go on patrol for the first time
09-29.description: Constables of Robert Peel's new Metropolitan Police began patrolling London. Nicknamed 'Bobbies' or 'Peelers', they set a model of uniformed, civilian policing by consent.

09-29.title: Munich conference hands the Sudetenland to Germany
09-29.description: Chamberlain, Daladier, Hitler and Mussolini agreed at Munich that Czechoslovakia must cede the Sudetenland; the deal was signed after midnight. Czechoslovakia was not consulted.

09-30.title: St Jerome dies in Bethlehem
09-30.description: The scholar Jerome died in Bethlehem, where he had translated most of the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek. His Vulgate became the standard Bible of the Western Church for over a thousand years.

09-30.title: Theodoric the Great defeats Odoacer at the Battle of Verona
09-30.description: Theodoric the Great, leading his Ostrogoths in person, won a decisive victory at Verona over Odoacer, king of Italy, who fled to Ravenna. Theodoric was then free to take Pavia and Milan, and by 493 he ruled Italy.

09-30.title: Türgesh tribesmen capture the baggage train of an Umayyad army
09-30.description: Retreating across the Oxus from Khuttal, the Umayyad army of Asad ibn Abdallah al-Qasri lost its baggage train, sent ahead, to the pursuing Türgesh. The failed campaign ended Arab control of the upper Oxus valley and opened Khurasan to the Türgesh.

09-30.title: A great earthquake strikes the Caucasus near Ganja
09-30.description: One of the worst earthquakes in history struck around Ganja, in lands of the Seljuk Empire and the Kingdom of Georgia. Its disputed death toll of 230,000 to 300,000 makes it one of the deadliest earthquakes ever recorded.

09-30.title: An Anglo-Breton army defeats a larger Franco-Breton force at Morlaix
09-30.description: Near Lanmeur in Brittany, an Anglo-Breton army defeated a far larger Franco-Breton force in the first land battle of the Hundred Years' War. England had sided with John of Montfort in the Breton Civil War, France with Charles of Blois.

09-30.title: Parliament accepts Richard II's deposition and Henry IV's claim
09-30.description: Richard II's abdication was read to an assembly at Westminster, which then acclaimed Henry Bolingbroke as Henry IV. The Lancastrian usurpation sowed the seeds of the Wars of the Roses.

09-30.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute premieres in Vienna
09-30.description: Die Zauberflöte opened at the Theater auf der Wieden with Mozart conducting. It was a popular success, and he died nine weeks later at the age of 35.

09-30.title: Chamberlain returns from Munich promising 'peace for our time'
09-30.description: Neville Chamberlain landed at Heston waving the declaration signed with Hitler and later spoke of 'peace for our time'. Within six months Germany had seized the rest of Czechoslovakia.

09-30.title: James Dean dies in a car crash aged 24
09-30.description: Actor James Dean was killed when his Porsche collided with another car in California. Two of his three starring films were released after his death, making him a lasting icon of youth.

10-01.title: Alexander defeats Darius III at Gaugamela
10-01.description: Alexander the Great routed the far larger army of the Persian king Darius III near Gaugamela in northern Mesopotamia. The victory broke Achaemenid power and opened the road to Babylon, Susa and Persepolis.

10-01.title: The Wonderful Parliament opens at Westminster
10-01.description: Called to meet King Richard II's need for money, the Wonderful Parliament met in Westminster Abbey but soon turned to reforming his administration. The Lords and Commons united against him and his unpopular chancellor, Michael de la Pole.

10-01.title: The Congress of Vienna is due to open formally
10-01.description: Europe's statesmen had gathered in Vienna to redraw the continent after Napoleon's fall, and 1 October was fixed for the Congress's formal opening. Its settlement shaped a balance of power that endured for decades.

10-01.title: John Philip Sousa takes charge of the US Marine Band
10-01.description: The 25-year-old John Philip Sousa became leader of the United States Marine Band. Over the next twelve years he turned it into a celebrated ensemble and began the career that earned him the name 'The March King'.

10-01.title: Congress creates Yosemite National Park
10-01.description: An Act of Congress established Yosemite National Park in California's Sierra Nevada, protecting the high country around the Yosemite Valley. John Muir's campaigning had helped make the case for preservation.

10-01.title: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China
10-01.description: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China. Communist victory in the civil war placed the world's most populous country under a new regime.

10-01.title: 'In God We Trust' first appears on US paper money
10-01.description: The first US banknotes carrying 'In God We Trust', one-dollar silver certificates, entered circulation. Congress had made the phrase the national motto in 1956, at the height of Cold War anxieties about 'godless' communism.

10-01.title: Nigeria gains independence from Britain
10-01.description: Nigeria, Africa's most populous country, became independent from Britain with Abubakar Tafawa Balewa as prime minister. It was one of seventeen African states to win independence in 1960, the 'Year of Africa'.

10-02.title: Julius Caesar arrives in Egypt and learns of Pompey's death
10-02.description: Julius Caesar, pursuing Pompey, arrived at Alexandria, capital of Ptolemaic Egypt, and learned of his rival's death. Kept there by the Etesian winds, he went on to arbitrate the civil war between the child pharaoh Ptolemy XIII and Cleopatra.

10-02.title: Theophilos succeeds his father Michael II as Byzantine emperor
10-02.description: On the death of Michael II, first ruler of the Amorian dynasty, his son Theophilos became Byzantine emperor. He reigned until 842, fought the Abbasids, and was the last emperor to support iconoclasm.

10-02.title: Otto I crushes the rebels at the Battle of Andernach
10-02.description: At Andernach on the Rhine, followers of King Otto I of Germany decisively defeated rebels led by Eberhard of Franconia, the brother of the late King Conrad I. The rebel leaders were killed, and Franconia came directly under the crown.

10-02.title: Saladin takes Jerusalem from the Crusaders
10-02.description: After a short siege, Saladin accepted the surrender of Jerusalem, ending 88 years of Crusader rule. Most inhabitants were allowed to ransom themselves, and the city's loss prompted the Third Crusade.

10-02.title: Scots and Norwegians fight the Battle of Largs
10-02.description: On the Ayrshire coast near Largs, Scots fought part of the storm-battered fleet of Haakon IV of Norway, who sought to reassert Norwegian sovereignty over Scotland's western seaboard. Haakon withdrew, and in 1266 his successor ceded the Hebrides and Man to Scotland.

10-02.title: Major John André is hanged as a British spy
10-02.description: Major John André, captured carrying Benedict Arnold's plans to surrender West Point, was hanged at Tappan, New York. His composure won sympathy even among his captors, while Arnold's name became a byword for treason.

10-02.title: Texan settlers fire the first shots of the Texas Revolution
10-02.description: At Gonzales, Texan colonists refused to hand back a small cannon to Mexican troops and fired on them beneath a flag reading 'Come and Take It'. The skirmish opened the war that led to Texan independence in 1836.

10-02.title: Mohandas Gandhi is born in Porbandar
10-02.description: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born in Porbandar, on India's western coast. His method of non-violent mass resistance, satyagraha, drove the Indian independence movement and inspired civil rights campaigns worldwide.

10-02.title: Mexican troops open fire on students at Tlatelolco
10-02.description: Soldiers and police fired on a student rally in Mexico City's Plaza de las Tres Culturas, ten days before the Olympic Games opened. Estimates of the dead range from about 30 to several hundred; the government long concealed the toll.

10-03.title: Antony and Octavian fight Brutus and Cassius at Philippi
10-03.description: In the first battle of Philippi, Mark Antony defeated Cassius and took his camp, while Brutus overran Octavian's troops. The battle was a tactical draw, but Cassius, believing it lost, took his own life to avoid capture.

10-03.title: Theodosius I settles the Goths inside the Roman Empire
10-03.description: Emperor Theodosius I concluded a treaty allowing the Goths to settle south of the Danube as semi-autonomous allies. Giving a whole people land within the frontier set a precedent that reshaped the late Roman world.

10-03.title: Heraclius the Younger's rebel fleet reaches Constantinople
10-03.description: The fleet of Heraclius the Younger, who with his father, the Exarch of Africa, had rebelled against Emperor Phocas in 608, reached Constantinople. Heraclius went on to execute Phocas and be proclaimed emperor, founding the Heraclian dynasty.

10-03.title: Francis of Assisi dies at the Porziuncola
10-03.description: Francis of Assisi died at the Porziuncola chapel below Assisi. The merchant's son who embraced radical poverty had founded the Franciscan order, and he was canonised less than two years later.

10-03.title: Dafydd ap Gruffydd, last native Prince of Wales, is executed
10-03.description: Dafydd ap Gruffydd, who had claimed the title Prince of Wales after his brother Llywelyn's death, was hanged, drawn and quartered at Shrewsbury on the orders of Edward I. He was the last native Prince of Wales before Edward's conquest.

10-03.title: Lincoln proclaims a national day of Thanksgiving
10-03.description: Amid the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln proclaimed the last Thursday of November a national day of thanksgiving. The proclamation answered years of campaigning by the editor Sarah Josepha Hale and began an annual federal holiday.

10-03.title: King Alexander renames his realm the Kingdom of Yugoslavia
10-03.description: Alexander I renamed the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes as Yugoslavia, 'land of the South Slavs', as part of his royal dictatorship. The new name was meant to override the national rivalries dividing the state.

10-03.title: Germany is reunified
10-03.description: The German Democratic Republic acceded to the Federal Republic, reuniting Germany 45 years after its division. The peaceful merger, less than a year after the Berlin Wall opened, marked the close of the Cold War in Europe.

10-04.title: Lülin rebels sack Chang'an, the capital of Wang Mang's Xin dynasty
10-04.description: During the Lülin peasant rebellion, rebels captured and sacked Chang'an, capital of Wang Mang's short-lived Xin dynasty; Wang Mang was killed two days later. The Eastern Han government later made Luoyang its primary capital.

10-04.title: Pope Innocent III crowns Otto IV emperor in Rome
10-04.description: Otto IV of the Welf dynasty, son of Henry the Lion and king of Germany since 1198, was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome by Pope Innocent III. He later broke with the pope and lost power after Bouvines in 1214.

10-04.title: Zhu Yuanzhang wins the Battle of Lake Poyang
10-04.description: On Lake Poyang, the smaller fleet of Zhu Yuanzhang destroyed the tower ships of his rival Chen Youliang with fire ships, and Chen was killed by an arrow. The victory made Zhu, the future Hongwu Emperor, master of central China.

10-04.title: Skanderbeg and Venice make peace, ending the Albanian–Venetian War
10-04.description: Skanderbeg and the Republic of Venice signed a peace negotiated by Georgius Pelino. Venice kept Dagnum but ceded Buzëgjarpri, at the mouth of the Drin, agreed to pay Skanderbeg 1,400 ducats and let him buy salt tax-free from Durazzo.

10-04.title: Catholic Europe switches to the Gregorian calendar
10-04.description: In Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, Thursday 4 October 1582 was followed directly by Friday 15 October. Pope Gregory XIII's reform dropped ten days to realign the calendar with the solar year.

10-04.title: Belgium's provisional government declares independence
10-04.description: Following the September uprising in Brussels, Belgium's provisional government declared independence from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. The great powers recognised the new state, and later guaranteed its neutrality.

10-04.title: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1
10-04.description: The Soviet Union placed Sputnik 1, an 84-kilogram metal sphere, into orbit, the first artificial satellite. Its radio beeps, picked up worldwide, shocked the West and launched the Space Race.

10-04.title: Paul VI becomes the first pope to visit the United States
10-04.description: Pope Paul VI flew to New York for a one-day visit, the first by a reigning pope to the United States. He appealed for peace at the United Nations General Assembly and celebrated Mass at Yankee Stadium.

10-05.title: Heraclius is crowned Byzantine emperor
10-05.description: Having reached Constantinople on 3 October at the head of the revolt against the unpopular emperor Phocas, Heraclius was crowned in the Chapel of St Stephen within the Great Palace. He reigned until 641.

10-05.title: Pope Stephen IV crowns Louis the Pious emperor at Reims
10-05.description: Louis the Pious, co-emperor with his father Charlemagne since 813 and sole ruler of the Franks since 814, received an imperial coronation from Pope Stephen IV at Reims. The next year he settled his succession in the Ordinatio imperii.

10-05.title: The Fourth Council of Constantinople opens
10-05.description: A church council opened in Constantinople that deposed the patriarch Photius. Counted by the Catholic Church as the eighth ecumenical council but rejected by the Orthodox, it foreshadowed the later schism between East and West.

10-05.title: Alfonso VII recognises Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal
10-05.description: In the Treaty of Zamora, Alfonso VII of León and Castile acknowledged his cousin Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal, in the presence of the papal legate. The treaty is regarded as the founding act of the Kingdom of Portugal.
links: Alfonso VII of León and Castile

10-05.title: Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice premieres in Vienna
10-05.description: Christoph Willibald Gluck's Orfeo ed Euridice was first performed at the Burgtheater in Vienna. Its simplicity and dramatic directness began Gluck's reform of opera away from showy vocal display.

10-05.title: Parisian women march on Versailles
10-05.description: Thousands of Parisians, led by market women angry at the price of bread, marched to Versailles. The next day they brought Louis XVI and his family back to Paris, placing the monarchy under the eye of the Revolution.

10-05.title: The Beatles release their first single, 'Love Me Do'
10-05.description: Parlophone released 'Love Me Do', the Beatles' debut single in Britain. It reached only number 17, but within a year the band from Liverpool had become a national sensation.

10-05.title: Dr. No premieres, launching the James Bond films
10-05.description: Dr. No, starring Sean Connery as Ian Fleming's secret agent, premiered at the London Pavilion. It began one of the longest-running series in cinema history.

10-06.title: The Cimbri and Teutons crush two Roman armies at Arausio
10-06.description: Between Arausio, now Orange, and the Rhône, the Cimbri under Boiorix and the Teutons under Teutobod defeated two Roman armies under the proconsul Quintus Servilius Caepio and the consul Gnaeus Mallius Maximus. It was Rome's worst defeat of the Cimbrian War.

10-06.title: Lucullus defeats Tigranes the Great at Tigranocerta
10-06.description: In the Third Mithridatic War, a Roman army under the consul Lucius Licinius Lucullus defeated King Tigranes the Great of Armenia and captured his capital, Tigranocerta. The war ended with Armenia an allied client state of Rome.

10-06.title: Rebels kill Wang Mang as Chang'an falls
10-06.description: Rebel forces broke into Chang'an and killed Wang Mang, the usurper who had founded the Xin dynasty. His death cleared the way for the restoration of the Han dynasty under Emperor Guangwu.

10-06.title: Wang Shichong defeats Li Mi at the Battle of Yanshi
10-06.description: Blockaded in Luoyang for months, Wang Shichong led his troops out and surprised Li Mi's besieging army north of Yanshi, winning a decisive victory. Li's followers joined Wang, who later deposed the Sui puppet ruler Yang Tong.

10-06.title: Peri's Euridice, the oldest surviving opera, is performed
10-06.description: Jacopo Peri's Euridice was staged at the Pitti Palace in Florence during celebrations for the marriage of Maria de' Medici to Henry IV of France. It is the earliest opera whose music survives complete.

10-06.title: The Jazz Singer premieres in New York
10-06.description: Warner Bros released The Jazz Singer, starring Al Jolson, the first feature film with synchronised dialogue and singing. Its success ended the silent era within a few years.

10-06.title: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on Yom Kippur
10-06.description: Egyptian and Syrian forces launched surprise attacks on Israeli positions in Sinai and the Golan Heights on the holiest day of the Jewish year. The war ended in Israeli counter-offensives and reshaped Middle Eastern diplomacy.

10-06.title: Egyptian president Anwar Sadat is assassinated
10-06.description: Islamist army officers shot Anwar Sadat during a military parade in Cairo marking the 1973 war. Sadat had signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1979 and shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Menachem Begin.

10-07.title: The epoch of the Hebrew calendar
10-07.description: The Hebrew calendar counts its years from a date equivalent to 7 October 3761 BCE, the traditional date of creation calculated from biblical chronology. Year 1 of this reckoning is still used to number the Jewish year.

10-07.title: Spanish and imperial troops defeat a Venetian army at La Motta
10-07.description: At Schio in the Veneto, a combined Spanish and imperial army under Ramón de Cardona and Fernando d'Ávalos decisively defeated a Venetian army under Bartolomeo d'Alviano, in a significant battle of the War of the League of Cambrai.
links: War of the League of Cambrai

10-07.title: The Holy League defeats the Ottoman fleet at Lepanto
10-07.description: Galleys of the Holy League under Don John of Austria destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet off western Greece. Lepanto was the last great battle of oared galleys and ended the image of Ottoman naval invincibility.

10-07.title: A cyclone and storm surge devastate Calcutta and Bengal
10-07.description: A violent cyclone struck the Hooghly delta, wrecking ships and much of Calcutta. Contemporary reports put the dead at 300,000, a figure modern historians consider greatly exaggerated.

10-07.title: George III bars settlement west of the Appalachians
10-07.description: After Britain gained France's North American territories, King George III issued a proclamation reserving the lands west of the Appalachians for Indigenous nations and forbidding settlement there. The restriction angered colonists.

10-07.title: American forces defeat Burgoyne in the second Battle of Saratoga
10-07.description: Near Saratoga, New York, American forces under Horatio Gates and Benedict Arnold decisively defeated General John Burgoyne's British army, which surrendered on 17 October. Burgoyne's surrender persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point of the war.

10-07.title: Luna 3 photographs the far side of the Moon
10-07.description: The Soviet probe Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side, which is never visible from Earth. The grainy images revealed a surface with far fewer dark lunar 'seas' than the near side.

10-07.title: The US and Britain begin air strikes on Afghanistan
10-07.description: American and British forces began bombing Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan, four weeks after the 11 September attacks. The war toppled the Taliban but lasted nearly twenty years.

10-08.title: The Council of Chalcedon opens
10-08.description: Bishops summoned by Emperor Marcian met at Chalcedon, across the Bosporus from Constantinople. Its definition of Christ as one person in two natures became orthodoxy in the West and Byzantium but split the eastern churches.

10-08.title: Louis the Younger defeats Charles the Bald at Andernach
10-08.description: Near Andernach, the East Frankish king Louis the Younger defeated his uncle, the West Frankish king and emperor Charles the Bald, who had tried to seize the western lands of Louis's inheritance.

10-08.title: Isabella of Angoulême is crowned queen of England
10-08.description: Isabella of Angoulême, heiress of the county of Angoulême and second wife of King John, was crowned queen of England. The marriage provoked the Lusignans and helped bring on the loss of Normandy.

10-08.title: The Great Stand on the Ugra River begins
10-08.description: The forces of Grand Prince Ivan III of Moscow and Akhmat Khan of the Great Horde began a stand-off on opposite banks of the Ugra River. The Horde withdrew without a decisive battle, traditionally marking the end of Tatar overlordship over Muscovy.
links: Great Stand on the Ugra River

10-08.title: Chinese officials board the Arrow at Canton
10-08.description: Qing officials boarded the Arrow, a Chinese-owned ship flying a British flag, and arrested its crew on suspicion of piracy. Britain used the incident as grounds for the Second Opium War.

10-08.title: The Great Chicago Fire breaks out
10-08.description: Fire broke out in a barn on DeKoven Street and, driven by strong winds, burned for two days across Chicago. About 300 people died and 100,000 lost their homes, but rebuilding made the city a centre of modern architecture.

10-08.title: Corporal Alvin York captures 132 German soldiers
10-08.description: In the Argonne Forest, Corporal Alvin York led a small patrol that silenced German machine guns, killing about 25 soldiers and taking 132 prisoners. He received the Medal of Honor and became a national hero.

10-08.title: Che Guevara is captured in Bolivia
10-08.description: Bolivian troops, aided by the CIA, wounded and captured Ernesto 'Che' Guevara in the Yuro ravine. He was executed the next day at La Higuera, and his image became an enduring icon of revolution.

10-09.title: James I of Aragon enters the city of Valencia
10-09.description: After defeating the Moors of the taifa of Balansiya, King James I of Aragon entered the city of Valencia, an event regarded as the dawn of the Kingdom of Valencia, a component realm of the Crown of Aragon.

10-09.title: King Sejong promulgates the Korean alphabet
10-09.description: Sejong the Great of Joseon published the Hunminjeongeum, introducing a new phonetic script now called Hangul. Designed so ordinary people could read and write, it is commemorated each year on Hangul Day.

10-09.title: The Catholic cantons declare war on Protestant Zürich
10-09.description: Pressed by a food embargo, the five Catholic cantons of Central Switzerland declared war on the Protestant canton of Zürich, starting the Second War of Kappel. On 11 October they defeated Zürich at Kappel, where the reformer Huldrych Zwingli was killed.

10-09.title: Connecticut charters the school that became Yale
10-09.description: The Connecticut General Assembly chartered the Collegiate School to train ministers and public leaders. It later settled in New Haven and in 1718 was renamed Yale College after the benefactor Elihu Yale.

10-09.title: Peter I of Russia defeats a Swedish convoy at Lesnaya
10-09.description: In the Great Northern War, Peter I of Russia caught a Swedish convoy under General Adam Ludwig Lewenhaupt at Lesnaya, in present-day Belarus, and defeated it. The convoy was carrying reinforcements and supplies to the main Swedish army in Ukraine.

10-09.title: The Treaty of Bern founds the Universal Postal Union
10-09.description: Representatives of 22 countries signed the Treaty of Bern, creating a single postal territory for exchanging letters. Its anniversary is marked as World Post Day.

10-09.title: John Lennon is born in Liverpool
10-09.description: John Winston Lennon was born at Liverpool Maternity Hospital. As co-founder and songwriter of the Beatles, and later as a solo artist and peace campaigner, he became one of the defining figures of 20th-century popular culture.

10-09.title: Uganda gains independence from Britain
10-09.description: Uganda became independent with Milton Obote as prime minister and the Kabaka of Buganda later as president. Its early decades were marked by political upheaval, including the dictatorship of Idi Amin.

10-10.title: Theodosius II inaugurates the second church of Hagia Sophia
10-10.description: Emperor Theodosius II inaugurated the church he had commissioned in Constantinople, the second on the site of Hagia Sophia. A fifth-century list of monuments named it the Great Church; the present building, the last of three, was completed in 537.

10-10.title: Husayn ibn Ali is killed at the Battle of Karbala
10-10.description: Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, who had refused to recognise the Umayyad caliph Yazid I, was killed with most of his small band by Yazid's forces at Karbala. His death became central to Shia identity.

10-10.title: Charles Martel defeats an Umayyad army near Tours
10-10.description: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Arab and Berber army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi between Tours and Poitiers; the traditional date is 10 October. How decisive the battle was remains debated.

10-10.title: Sten Sture the Elder defeats Christian I at Brunkeberg
10-10.description: On a ridge outside Stockholm, the Swedish regent Sten Sture the Elder, with peasants, miners and burghers, defeated King Christian I of Denmark, who sought to enforce his rule over Sweden under the Kalmar Union. The victory secured Sture's regency.

10-10.title: The Ndyuka Maroons win autonomy by treaty with the Dutch
10-10.description: The Ndyuka, a Maroon people of Suriname descended from Africans who escaped slavery, signed a treaty with the Dutch colonial authorities recognising their territorial autonomy. In 2010 Suriname made 10 October a national holiday, the Day of the Maroons.

10-10.title: The US Naval School opens at Annapolis
10-10.description: The Naval School, renamed the United States Naval Academy in 1850, opened at Fort Severn in Annapolis, Maryland, with 50 midshipmen. It has trained American naval officers ever since; Jimmy Carter was among its graduates.

10-10.title: The Wuchang Uprising sparks the Chinese revolution
10-10.description: Revolutionary soldiers mutinied at Wuchang, beginning the Xinhai Revolution. Within months the Qing dynasty abdicated, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

10-10.title: Woodrow Wilson triggers the blast that floods the Panama Canal cut
10-10.description: From the White House, President Wilson sent a telegraph signal that detonated the Gamboa dike. Water flowed into the Culebra Cut, joining the canal's waters ten months before it opened to shipping.

10-10.title: The Outer Space Treaty enters into force
10-10.description: The Outer Space Treaty came into effect, forming the basis of international space law. It bars nuclear weapons from orbit and forbids any nation from claiming sovereignty over the Moon or other celestial bodies.

10-11.title: A great earthquake strikes Aleppo and northern Syria
10-11.description: An earthquake struck Aleppo and northern Syria a day after a smaller shock, causing damage and chaos across the area. The toll of 230,000 later reported by Ibn Taghribirdi probably conflated it with other earthquakes.

10-11.title: The Treaty of Shaoxing between Jin and Song is ratified
10-11.description: The Treaty of Shaoxing, signed in 1141, was formally ratified when a Jin envoy visited the Song court. The Southern Song gave up its claims north of the Huai, including Kaifeng, and agreed to a yearly tribute to the Jin.

10-11.title: Pope Leo X names Henry VIII 'Defender of the Faith'
10-11.description: Pope Leo X granted Henry VIII the title Fidei Defensor for his treatise attacking Martin Luther. Henry later broke with Rome, yet British monarchs still use the title, abbreviated 'F.D.' on coins.

10-11.title: Catholic cantons defeat Zürich at the Battle of Kappel
10-11.description: Near Kappel am Albis, the Catholic cantons of central Switzerland defeated Protestant Zürich, and the reformer Huldrych Zwingli, who accompanied the Zürich army as chaplain, was killed. The Second Peace of Kappel halted the spread of the Reformation in the Confederacy.

10-11.title: A British force defeats Benedict Arnold's fleet at Valcour Island
10-11.description: On Lake Champlain, a British force under General Guy Carleton captured or destroyed most of the American fleet commanded by Benedict Arnold. The American defence of the lake nonetheless stalled British plans to reach the upper Hudson River valley.

10-11.title: The Second Boer War begins in South Africa
10-11.description: War broke out when Britain let a Boer ultimatum expire. In the three-year conflict that followed, British concentration camps saw the deaths of about 26,000 Boer women and children and many thousands of black Africans.

10-11.title: Roosevelt receives Einstein's warning about atomic bombs
10-11.description: The economist Alexander Sachs delivered to Franklin Roosevelt a letter signed by Albert Einstein, warning that Germany might build a uranium bomb. Roosevelt set up an advisory committee that led eventually to the Manhattan Project.

10-11.title: Pope John XXIII opens the Second Vatican Council
10-11.description: More than 2,000 bishops gathered in St Peter's Basilica for the opening of the Second Vatican Council. Over three years it introduced vernacular liturgy, embraced ecumenism and affirmed religious freedom.

10-12.title: Persian forces of Cyrus the Great enter Babylon
10-12.description: After invading Babylonia, the Persian forces of Cyrus the Great entered the city of Babylon, ending the Chaldean, or Neo-Babylonian, Empire. The Babylonian Chronicles and the Cyrus Cylinder described the city taken without battle; Herodotus and Xenophon reported a siege.

10-12.title: Cadwallon and Penda defeat and kill Edwin at Hatfield Chase
10-12.description: Near Doncaster, Cadwallon ap Cadfan of Gwynedd and Penda of Mercia defeated and killed Edwin, the Christian king of Northumbria. Northumbria split into its two kingdoms of Deira and Bernicia, and Cadwallon ravaged it for a year.

10-12.title: Vytautas cedes Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights at Salynas
10-12.description: On an islet of the Neman River, Vytautas the Great, ruler of Lithuania, and Grand Master Konrad von Jungingen signed the Treaty of Salynas, promising Samogitia to the Teutonic Knights for the third time. The dispute dragged on until 1422.

10-12.title: Columbus makes landfall in the Bahamas
10-12.description: After 33 days crossing the Atlantic, Christopher Columbus's expedition landed on an island its Taíno inhabitants called Guanahani. The encounter began sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, with vast consequences for both.

10-12.title: Crown Prince Ludwig's wedding gives rise to Oktoberfest
10-12.description: Crown Prince Ludwig of Bavaria married Princess Therese of Saxe-Hildburghausen, and Munich's citizens were invited to celebrate on the fields before the city gates. The festivities, crowned by a horse race, became the annual Oktoberfest.

10-12.title: Pedro I is acclaimed Emperor of Brazil
10-12.description: In Rio de Janeiro, Prince Pedro was acclaimed constitutional Emperor of Brazil, five weeks after declaring independence from Portugal. Brazil became the only lasting monarchy in independent Latin America.

10-12.title: Germans execute the British nurse Edith Cavell
10-12.description: A German firing squad in Brussels executed Edith Cavell, who had helped some 200 Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium. Her death caused international outrage and became a powerful theme of Allied propaganda.

10-12.title: Bombings in Bali kill 202 people
10-12.description: Militants of Jemaah Islamiyah bombed two nightclubs in the tourist district of Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people from 21 countries. It remains the deadliest terrorist attack in Indonesia's history.

10-13.title: Nero becomes Roman emperor at 16
10-13.description: On the death of Claudius, reputedly poisoned by his wife Agrippina, her 16-year-old son Nero was proclaimed emperor. His reign began promisingly but ended in tyranny, rebellion and his suicide in 68.

10-13.title: Emperor Taizong abandons the siege of Ansi
10-13.description: With winter approaching and food supplies running out, Emperor Taizong ordered the Tang army to withdraw from its siege of Ansi in the Goguryeo–Tang War. Goguryeo repulsed the first Tang invasions of 645–648.

10-13.title: Henry III's rebuilt Westminster Abbey is consecrated
10-13.description: The present church of Westminster Abbey, rebuilt in Gothic style under Henry III from 1245, was consecrated. It replaced the church of Edward the Confessor, consecrated in 1065, where monarchs had been crowned since William the Conqueror in 1066.

10-13.title: Philip IV of France orders the arrest of the Templars
10-13.description: In dawn raids across France, Philip IV's officers arrested hundreds of Knights Templar on charges of heresy and blasphemy. The heavily indebted king coveted their wealth, and the order was suppressed in 1312.

10-13.title: Hungarian forces destroy an Ottoman army at Breadfield
10-13.description: Near Orăștie in Transylvania, Hungarian forces under Stephen Báthory and Paul Kinizsi destroyed a large Ottoman raiding army. It was the greatest Hungarian victory over the Ottomans in the reign of Matthias Corvinus and kept Transylvania free of major raids for years.

10-13.title: The cornerstone of the White House is laid
10-13.description: Freemasons laid the cornerstone of the President's House in the new federal city of Washington. Designed by James Hoban, it has housed every US president since John Adams.

10-13.title: Greenwich is chosen as the world's prime meridian
10-13.description: Delegates at the International Meridian Conference in Washington voted to adopt the meridian through Greenwich as the zero of longitude. The decision underpins maps, navigation and the world's time zones.

10-13.title: Italy declares war on Germany
10-13.description: Five weeks after its armistice with the Allies, Pietro Badoglio's Italian government declared war on its former Axis partner. German forces nonetheless occupied northern and central Italy until 1945.

10-14.title: William of Normandy defeats Harold II at Hastings
10-14.description: After a day-long battle near Hastings, Norman forces killed King Harold II and broke the English army. The conquest replaced England's ruling class and transformed its language, law and architecture.

10-14.title: Robert the Bruce routs Edward II at Old Byland
10-14.description: A Scottish army under Robert the Bruce defeated English forces at Old Byland in Yorkshire, and Edward II narrowly escaped capture. The defeat pushed England towards the truce of 1323.

10-14.title: King Tabinshwehti of Burma begins his invasion of Siam
10-14.description: A Toungoo force of 12,000 led by Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung invaded Siam through the Three Pagodas Pass and advanced to Ayutthaya. It failed to take the fortified capital, and Siamese counterattacks broke the siege in January 1549.

10-14.title: Mary, Queen of Scots, goes on trial at Fotheringhay
10-14.description: Mary was tried before a commission of English peers and officials at Fotheringhay Castle, accused of plotting Elizabeth I's death in the Babington Plot. Found guilty, she was beheaded in February 1587.

10-14.title: An Austrian army surprises Frederick the Great at Hochkirch
10-14.description: In the Third Silesian War, an Austrian army of 80,000 under Leopold Josef Graf Daun surprised Frederick the Great's Prussian army of 30,000–36,000 at Hochkirch, near Bautzen in Saxony, and forced a general retreat. It was a rare defeat for Frederick.

10-14.title: Dwight D. Eisenhower is born in Texas
10-14.description: Dwight David Eisenhower was born in Denison, Texas. He commanded the Allied invasion of Europe in 1944 and served two terms as the 34th US president, warning on leaving office of the 'military-industrial complex'.

10-14.title: Chuck Yeager flies faster than sound
10-14.description: Captain Chuck Yeager piloted the rocket-powered Bell X-1 past Mach 1 high over the Mojave Desert. It was the first confirmed supersonic flight in level flight, opening the age of supersonic aviation.

10-14.title: Soviet leaders oust Nikita Khrushchev
10-14.description: Recalled from holiday, Nikita Khrushchev was forced out by the Communist Party's Central Committee. Leonid Brezhnev succeeded him as party leader and steered the Soviet Union into two decades of stability and stagnation.

10-15.title: Al-Hakam II succeeds his father as caliph of Córdoba
10-15.description: On the death of his father Abd al-Rahman III, al-Hakam II became the second Umayyad caliph of Córdoba. A scholar and bibliophile, he assembled a library said to hold some 400,000 volumes and enlarged the Great Mosque of Córdoba.

10-15.title: Latin emperor Henry of Flanders defeats Theodore I Laskaris
10-15.description: At the Rhyndacus, the Latin emperor Henry of Flanders defeated Theodore I Laskaris, founder of the Empire of Nicaea. Theodore had gathered Byzantine refugees in Bithynia after the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople in 1204.

10-15.title: The Ottomans abandon the siege of Vienna
10-15.description: After just over two weeks, Suleiman the Magnificent's army of over 100,000 ended its siege of Vienna, defended by no more than 21,000 men under Niklas Graf Salm. Bad weather, long supply lines and a determined defence forced the withdrawal.

10-15.title: The Gregorian calendar takes effect
10-15.description: Friday 15 October 1582 was the first day of the Gregorian calendar in Italy, Spain, Portugal and Poland, following directly on Thursday 4 October. Protestant and Orthodox countries adopted it only over the following centuries.

10-15.title: Pilâtre de Rozier makes the first human balloon ascent
10-15.description: In Paris, Jean-François Pilâtre de Rozier rose about 25 metres in a tethered Montgolfier hot-air balloon, the first human ascent. Five weeks later he made the first free flight.

10-15.title: Napoleon arrives in exile at Saint Helena
10-15.description: HMS Northumberland anchored off Jamestown, Saint Helena, carrying the defeated Napoleon. On this remote South Atlantic island he spent his last six years, dying there in 1821.

10-15.title: Cologne Cathedral is completed after 632 years
10-15.description: Kaiser Wilhelm I attended celebrations marking the completion of Cologne Cathedral. Begun in 1248 and left unfinished for centuries, the Gothic church was completed using its medieval plans.

10-15.title: Mata Hari is executed by a French firing squad
10-15.description: The Dutch-born dancer Margaretha Zelle, known as Mata Hari, was shot at Vincennes after conviction as a German spy. Historians still dispute how much, if any, useful intelligence she passed on.

10-16.title: Wu Zetian proclaims herself emperor of China
10-16.description: Wu Zetian, long the power behind the Tang throne, took the title of emperor and founded her own Zhou dynasty. She remains the only woman to rule China in her own name, and expanded recruitment by examination.

10-16.title: Abd al-Rahman III becomes emir of Córdoba
10-16.description: Abd al-Rahman III became the eighth emir of Córdoba. He went on to reunite al-Andalus and in 929 proclaimed himself caliph, founding the Caliphate of Córdoba; his reign marked the height of Andalusi power.

10-16.title: Jadwiga is crowned king, not queen, of Poland
10-16.description: Jadwiga, youngest daughter of Louis I of Hungary, was crowned king of Poland, rather than queen, to highlight her sovereign status. Under the Union of Krewo she later married the Lithuanian grand duke Jogaila, beginning the dynastic union of Poland and Lithuania.

10-16.title: Marie Antoinette is guillotined in Paris
10-16.description: After a two-day trial before the Revolutionary Tribunal, the former queen Marie Antoinette was executed on the Place de la Révolution. She was 37, and her husband Louis XVI had been executed nine months earlier.

10-16.title: Jourdan's French army wins the Battle of Wattignies
10-16.description: After two days of combat at Wattignies, a French army under Jean-Baptiste Jourdan defeated a Coalition army directed by Prince Josias of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld. The victory allowed the French to raise the siege of Maubeuge.

10-16.title: The Battle of Leipzig begins
10-16.description: Austrian, Prussian, Russian and Swedish armies attacked Napoleon around Leipzig. With some 600,000 soldiers engaged over three days, the 'Battle of the Nations' was the largest in Europe before the First World War.

10-16.title: Margaret Sanger opens the first US birth control clinic
10-16.description: Margaret Sanger, her sister and a colleague opened a birth control clinic in Brownsville, Brooklyn. Police closed it nine days later, but Sanger's campaign led to the organisation that became Planned Parenthood.

10-16.title: Ten Nazi leaders are hanged at Nuremberg
10-16.description: Ten men sentenced by the International Military Tribunal, including Ribbentrop, Keitel and Streicher, were hanged in Nuremberg prison's gymnasium. Göring had taken poison the night before.

10-17.title: The English capture David II of Scotland at Neville's Cross
10-17.description: An English force defeated a Scottish invasion at Neville's Cross near Durham and captured King David II. He spent eleven years as a prisoner before being ransomed.

10-17.title: The Second Battle of Kosovo begins between Hunyadi and Murad II
10-17.description: A Hungarian-led crusader army under the regent John Hunyadi, seeking to avenge the defeat at Varna, met the Ottoman army of Sultan Murad II on the Kosovo plain. After three days of fighting the Ottomans prevailed.

10-17.title: The University of Greifswald is founded
10-17.description: The University of Greifswald was founded in the Baltic town of Greifswald in Pomerania, with the support of Duke Wartislaw IX and the burgomaster Heinrich Rubenow. Under Swedish rule from 1648 to 1815 it was the oldest university of the Swedish realm.

10-17.title: Apraksin's Russian army defeats Armfeldt's Finnish army at Pälkäne
10-17.description: In the Great Northern War, a Russian army under Admiral Fyodor Apraksin defeated the defending Finnish army of the Swedish Empire under General Carl Gustaf Armfeldt at Pälkäne, though Armfeldt withdrew his army in good order.

10-17.title: Burgoyne surrenders his army at Saratoga
10-17.description: British General John Burgoyne surrendered nearly 6,000 men to American forces at Saratoga, New York. The victory persuaded France to ally with the United States, a turning point in the Revolutionary War.

10-17.title: Edison files his first motion picture caveat
10-17.description: Thomas Edison filed a patent caveat describing an 'optical phonograph' to record and reproduce moving images. The idea, developed largely by his assistant William Dickson, became the Kinetoscope.

10-17.title: The Queen opens Calder Hall nuclear power station
10-17.description: Elizabeth II opened Calder Hall in Cumberland, the world's first nuclear power station to supply electricity to a national grid on a commercial scale. It also produced plutonium for Britain's weapons programme.

10-17.title: Mother Teresa is named winner of the Nobel Peace Prize
10-17.description: The Norwegian Nobel Committee announced its Peace Prize for Mother Teresa, founder of the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta, for her work among the poorest and dying.

10-18.title: Chlothar II issues the Edict of Paris
10-18.description: After reuniting the Frankish kingdoms, the Merovingian king Chlothar II issued the Edict of Paris following a church council. Its 24 articles confirmed the rights of the church and aristocracy and required royal officials to be appointed from the regions they governed.

10-18.title: Dagobert I becomes ruler of all the Frankish kingdoms
10-18.description: Dagobert I, king of Austrasia since 623, became ruler of Neustria and Burgundy as well, and so of all the Frankish kingdoms. After him, real power passed increasingly to the mayors of the palace.

10-18.title: Caliph al-Hakim has the Holy Sepulchre demolished
10-18.description: On the orders of the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim, the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem was torn down. Its destruction shocked Christendom and was remembered as a grievance when the First Crusade was preached.

10-18.title: Cnut's Danes defeat Edmund Ironside at the Battle of Assandun
10-18.description: A Danish army led by King Cnut defeated the English under King Edmund Ironside at Assandun, in Essex. A treaty then divided England between them, and when Edmund died shortly afterwards Cnut became undisputed king, as agreed.

10-18.title: Robert Guiscard's Normans defeat Alexios I at Dyrrhachium
10-18.description: In the Byzantine–Norman wars, the Normans of southern Italy under Robert Guiscard, Duke of Apulia and Calabria, defeated the army of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos outside Dyrrhachium, the major Byzantine stronghold in the western Balkans.

10-18.title: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes
10-18.description: By the Edict of Fontainebleau, Louis XIV outlawed Protestant worship in France. Some 200,000 Huguenots fled abroad to England, the Dutch Republic and Prussia, taking valuable skills with them.

10-18.title: Mason and Dixon complete their boundary survey
10-18.description: Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon finished surveying the boundary between Pennsylvania and Maryland. Their line later became the symbolic divide between free and slave states.

10-18.title: The United States takes possession of Alaska
10-18.description: At Sitka, the Russian flag was lowered and the US flag raised, formally transferring Alaska, bought for 7.2 million dollars. Critics mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly' until gold and oil proved its value.

10-18.title: The British Broadcasting Company is founded
10-18.description: Wireless manufacturers formed the British Broadcasting Company to run Britain's first national radio service. Under John Reith it became the public British Broadcasting Corporation in 1927.

10-19.title: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama
10-19.description: Publius Cornelius Scipio defeated Hannibal near Zama in North Africa; 19 October is the traditional date. The victory ended the Second Punic War, leaving Rome dominant in the western Mediterranean.

10-19.title: King John dies at Newark Castle
10-19.description: King John died of dysentery at Newark during a civil war with his barons and a French invasion. His nine-year-old son became Henry III, and his regents reissued Magna Carta to win back support.

10-19.title: Heidelberg University holds its first lecture
10-19.description: A day after a Pontifical High Mass established it, Heidelberg University, founded by Rupert I, Elector Palatine, held its first lecture, making it the oldest university in present-day Germany. By March 1390 it had 185 students.

10-19.title: Bordeaux falls to the French, ending the Hundred Years' War
10-19.description: Three months after the English defeat at Castillon, Bordeaux surrendered to the French, ending three centuries of English rule in Gascony. No more hostilities followed, and the Hundred Years' War was over.

10-19.title: The Second Peace of Thorn ends the Thirteen Years' War
10-19.description: The Polish king Casimir IV Jagiellon and the Teutonic Knights made peace at Toruń, ending the longest of the Polish–Teutonic Wars. Royal Prussia, with Danzig and Marienburg, passed to Poland; the Order kept the rest as a Polish fief.

10-19.title: Cornwallis's army surrenders at Yorktown
10-19.description: Besieged by American and French forces, Lord Cornwallis's army of about 8,000 surrendered at Yorktown, Virginia. The defeat effectively ended major fighting in the American Revolutionary War.

10-19.title: Napoleon retreats after defeat at Leipzig
10-19.description: The Battle of the Nations ended with Napoleon's army in retreat from Leipzig, its rearguard trapped when a bridge was blown too early. He lost control of Germany, and the Allies invaded France within months.

10-19.title: Black Monday: stock markets crash worldwide
10-19.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 508 points, or 22.6 per cent, its largest one-day percentage fall. Markets crashed worldwide, though the wider economy recovered far faster than after 1929.

10-20.title: Murad II defeats John Hunyadi in the Second Battle of Kosovo
10-20.description: The Ottoman army of Sultan Murad II defeated the Hungarian and Wallachian army of John Hunyadi on the Kosovo plain, ending his hope of reversing the defeat at Varna. He was then briefly held captive by the Serbian despot Đurađ Branković.

10-20.title: The Duke of Alba defeats William the Silent at Jodoigne
10-20.description: At Jodoigne, the royal Habsburg army of the Duke of Alba, governor of the Netherlands, defeated a Protestant rebel army led by William the Silent, Prince of Orange, who had to abandon his plans to invade the Habsburg Netherlands.

10-20.title: Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands
10-20.description: The death of Emperor Charles VI left his 23-year-old daughter Maria Theresa ruler of Austria, Hungary and Bohemia. She fought off Frederick the Great's challenge and reformed the state over a 40-year reign.

10-20.title: The First Continental Congress adopts the Continental Association
10-20.description: Meeting in Carpenters' Hall in Philadelphia, the First Continental Congress adopted the Continental Association, a colonial boycott of British trade. Congress hoped the sanctions would pressure Parliament to address the colonies' grievances, especially by repealing the Intolerable Acts.

10-20.title: The US Senate ratifies the Louisiana Purchase
10-20.description: The Senate approved the treaty buying Louisiana from France by 24 votes to 7. For 15 million dollars, the United States gained some 828,000 square miles, roughly doubling its territory.

10-20.title: Allied fleets destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian navy at Navarino
10-20.description: British, French and Russian squadrons destroyed the Ottoman and Egyptian fleet in Navarino Bay, Greece. The last major battle fought entirely by sailing ships, it secured Greek independence.

10-20.title: US forces land on Leyte as MacArthur returns
10-20.description: American troops landed on Leyte, and General Douglas MacArthur waded ashore to fulfil his 1942 promise to return to the Philippines. Days later, the Battle of Leyte Gulf crippled the Japanese navy.

10-20.title: Muammar Gaddafi is captured and killed near Sirte
10-20.description: Rebel fighters captured Muammar Gaddafi near his hometown of Sirte and killed him shortly afterwards. His death ended 42 years of rule and the Libyan civil war.

10-21.title: El Cid routs an Almoravid army at the Battle of Cuarte
10-21.description: Months after El Cid captured Valencia, an Almoravid army under Muhammad ibn Tashfin, sent to recover the city, camped on the plain of Cuarte. El Cid sallied out and routed it, the first major defeat of the Almoravids in the Iberian Peninsula.

10-21.title: Seljuk Turks destroy the People's Crusade at Civetot
10-21.description: The undisciplined People's Crusade, inspired by Peter the Hermit, was ambushed and annihilated by Seljuk forces near Civetot in Anatolia. On its way east, the movement had massacred Jewish communities in the Rhineland.

10-21.title: The First Crusade reaches Antioch and begins its siege
10-21.description: A day after forcing the Iron Bridge over the Orontes, the First Crusade reached Antioch, Bohemond of Taranto leading the vanguard. Bohemond, Raymond IV of Toulouse and Godfrey of Bouillon took positions at different gates for a siege of nine months.

10-21.title: The Earl of Derby defeats a larger French army at Auberoche
10-21.description: In the Gascon campaign of the Hundred Years' War, an Anglo-Gascon force of 1,200 under Henry, Earl of Derby, heavily defeated a French army of 7,000 under Louis of Poitiers at Auberoche, near Périgueux. The French leaders were killed or captured.

10-21.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the Battle of Sekigahara
10-21.description: Tokugawa Ieyasu defeated a coalition of western lords at Sekigahara, helped by defections mid-battle. The victory led to the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled a largely peaceful Japan for more than 250 years.

10-21.title: Nelson defeats the French and Spanish fleets at Trafalgar
10-21.description: Admiral Horatio Nelson's fleet destroyed the combined French and Spanish fleets off Cape Trafalgar, ending Napoleon's hopes of invading Britain. Nelson was mortally wounded by a musket ball during the battle.

10-21.title: Edison's carbon-filament lamp begins a 13-hour test
10-21.description: At Menlo Park, Thomas Edison's team lit a bulb with a carbonised cotton-thread filament that glowed for about 13.5 hours. The result made long-lasting electric lighting practical.

10-21.title: A colliery spoil tip engulfs a school at Aberfan
10-21.description: A coal waste tip slid down onto the Welsh village of Aberfan, burying Pantglas Junior School. The disaster killed 144 people, 116 of them children, and an inquiry blamed the National Coal Board.

10-22.title: Emperor Kanmu moves Japan's capital to Heian-kyō
10-22.description: On the 22nd day of the tenth month, Emperor Kanmu formally moved his court to the new capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial seat for over a thousand years; the Jidai Matsuri festival marks the date.

10-22.title: Ahmad ibn Kayghalagh leads an Abbasid raid into Byzantine lands
10-22.description: The Abbasid officer Ahmad ibn Kayghalagh led the annual raid against the Byzantine Empire from Tarsus with the local governor, Rustam ibn Baradu. According to al-Tabari, they defeated the Byzantines and reached the Halys River, taking 4,000 or 5,000 captives.

10-22.title: Nicola Boccasini is elected pope as Benedict XI
10-22.description: Nicola Boccasini was elected pope as Benedict XI, succeeding Boniface VIII, who had died weeks earlier, shortly after his seizure at Anagni in his conflict with Philip IV of France. Benedict's pontificate lasted until his death in July 1304.

10-22.title: Ferdinand I of Portugal dies, opening a succession crisis
10-22.description: King Ferdinand I of Portugal died without a legitimate male heir, ending the male line of the Portuguese House of Burgundy. His daughter Beatrice, wife of John I of Castile, claimed the throne, but many Portuguese backed John, Master of Aviz.

10-22.title: Peter the Great takes the title of emperor
10-22.description: After victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War, the Russian Senate conferred on Peter I the titles 'the Great' and Emperor of All Russia (22 October, Old Style). Russia was now formally an empire and a European great power.

10-22.title: André-Jacques Garnerin makes the first parachute descent from a balloon
10-22.description: Over the Parc Monceau in Paris, André-Jacques Garnerin cut his parachute free of a hydrogen balloon at about 1,000 metres. He landed safely despite violent swinging, the first frameless silk parachute jump.

10-22.title: Sam Houston becomes the first president of the Republic of Texas
10-22.description: Sam Houston, victor of San Jacinto, was inaugurated as the first elected president of the Republic of Texas at Columbia. Texas remained an independent republic until joining the United States in 1845.

10-22.title: Kennedy tells Americans of Soviet missiles in Cuba
10-22.description: In a televised address, John F. Kennedy revealed that Soviet nuclear missile sites were being built in Cuba and announced a naval 'quarantine' of the island. The crisis brought the superpowers closer to nuclear war than ever before.

10-23.title: Archbishop Ussher's date for the Creation
10-23.description: In his chronology of 1650, Archbishop James Ussher calculated from biblical genealogies that the world was created on the evening before Sunday 23 October 4004 BCE. The date was printed in many English Bibles for two centuries.

10-23.title: Brutus takes his own life after defeat at Philippi
10-23.description: Defeated by Mark Antony and Octavian in the second engagement at Philippi in Macedonia, Marcus Junius Brutus, a leader of Julius Caesar's assassins, took his own life. The triumvirs' victory ended the Liberators' civil war and the republican cause.

10-23.title: A synod at Palma refuses to judge Pope Symmachus
10-23.description: Urged by the Ostrogothic king Theodoric to settle the matter, the bishops met at Palma and declared they could not judge Pope Symmachus, successor of Peter the Apostle, leaving it to God. The resolutions were signed by 76 bishops.

10-23.title: Yusuf ibn Tashfin's Almoravids defeat Alfonso VI at Sagrajas
10-23.description: Near Badajoz, the Almoravid army of Yusuf ibn Tashfin, called in by the taifa rulers of al-Andalus, shattered the forces of King Alfonso VI of Castile. The victory preserved Muslim control of southern Spain under Almoravid influence.

10-23.title: Valdemar I defeats Sweyn III at Grathe Heath
10-23.description: Near Viborg in Jutland, Valdemar I defeated his rival for the Danish throne, Sweyn III, who was killed while fleeing. The battle ended the Danish civil wars, and Valdemar became sole king.

10-23.title: Scotland and France seal the first treaty of the Auld Alliance
10-23.description: A treaty between John Balliol of Scotland and Philip IV of France, signed in Paris, formed the Auld Alliance against England. Renewed by most later Scottish kings, it drew Scotland into repeated wars with England and effectively ended in 1560.

10-23.title: Royalists and Parliamentarians clash at Edgehill
10-23.description: Charles I's army fought Parliament's forces under the Earl of Essex at Edgehill in Warwickshire, the first pitched battle of the English Civil War. The indecisive result made clear the war would be long.

10-23.title: The Hungarian Revolution begins in Budapest
10-23.description: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a national uprising against the communist government and Soviet control. Soviet forces crushed it in November, leaving some 2,500 Hungarians dead and 200,000 in exile.

10-23.title: Truck bombs kill 241 US and 58 French troops in Beirut
10-23.description: Suicide bombers drove explosive-laden trucks into the US Marine barracks and a French paratroop building in Beirut. The attacks led to the withdrawal of the multinational peacekeeping force from Lebanon.

10-24.title: Baybars seizes the Mamluk throne after Qutuz is assassinated
10-24.description: Shortly after Qutuz and Baybars defeated the Mongols at Ain Jalut, Sultan Qutuz was assassinated, and Baybars seized the throne as the fourth Mamluk sultan of Egypt and Syria. He reigned until 1277.

10-24.title: Rudolf of Habsburg is crowned King of the Romans at Aachen
10-24.description: Rudolf of Habsburg, a Swabian count elected King of the Romans that year, was crowned in Aachen Cathedral, the first of his house to hold the title. His election ended the Great Interregnum after the fall of the Hohenstaufen.

10-24.title: The Treaty of Brétigny is ratified at Calais
10-24.description: Edward III and John II of France ratified at Calais the peace agreed at Brétigny in May. England gained Aquitaine and Calais in full sovereignty and a huge ransom for the captured French king, pausing the Hundred Years' War.

10-24.title: The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War
10-24.description: Treaties signed at Münster and Osnabrück ended the Thirty Years' War, which had devastated central Europe. The settlement confirmed the autonomy of the German princes and recognised Dutch and Swiss independence.

10-24.title: The Brabant Revolution begins in the Austrian Netherlands
10-24.description: An émigré army from the Dutch Republic invaded the Austrian Netherlands, beginning the Brabant Revolution against Emperor Joseph II's centralising and church reforms. The rebels drove out the Austrian forces and in January 1790 proclaimed the United Belgian States.

10-24.title: Black Thursday: panic selling hits Wall Street
10-24.description: Nearly 13 million shares changed hands as panic swept the New York Stock Exchange. Bankers briefly steadied prices, but the crash that followed the next week opened the way to the Great Depression.

10-24.title: The United Nations comes into being
10-24.description: The United Nations Charter entered into force once a majority of signatories, including the five permanent Security Council members, had ratified it. The date is celebrated annually as United Nations Day.

10-24.title: Concorde makes its last commercial flight
10-24.description: British Airways Concorde flight BA002 from New York landed at Heathrow, ending 27 years of supersonic passenger travel. The aircraft could cross the Atlantic in about three and a half hours.

10-25.title: Afonso I of Portugal takes Lisbon after a four-month siege
10-25.description: With crusader help, Afonso I, the first king of Portugal, ended a siege begun on 1 July and took Lisbon from the Moors. The siege, seen as pivotal in the Reconquista, was one of the few Christian victories of the Second Crusade.

10-25.title: Geoffrey Chaucer dies in London
10-25.description: Geoffrey Chaucer died, according to the date on his tomb in Westminster Abbey. His Canterbury Tales, written in English rather than French or Latin, helped establish English as a literary language.

10-25.title: Henry V defeats a larger French army at Agincourt
10-25.description: Henry V's outnumbered and exhausted army, largely archers, defeated the French at Agincourt as heavily armoured knights struggled across muddy ground. Many French nobles were killed or captured.

10-25.title: George III becomes king of Great Britain
10-25.description: George II died suddenly at Kensington Palace, and his 22-year-old grandson succeeded as George III. His 60-year reign saw the loss of the American colonies and victory over Napoleonic France.

10-25.title: The Light Brigade charges at Balaclava
10-25.description: A misunderstood order sent British light cavalry charging down a valley ringed by Russian guns. About 270 of some 670 riders were killed or wounded, and Tennyson's poem made the charge a byword for courage and blunder.

10-25.title: Zagonyi's Union cavalry wins the First Battle of Springfield
10-25.description: Near Springfield, Missouri, Major Charles Zagonyi, commander of the bodyguard of General Frémont, won a minor Union victory over Missouri State Guard recruits through a charge widely covered by the media. Federal troops occupied the city two days later.

10-25.title: Union troops defeat Sterling Price's Confederates at Marais des Cygnes
10-25.description: After their defeat at Westport on 23 October, Sterling Price's Confederate raiders withdrew into Kansas; Union troops then defeated them at Marais des Cygnes in Linn County, at Mine Creek and at the Marmiton River.

10-25.title: Japan launches its first organised kamikaze attacks
10-25.description: During the Battle of Leyte Gulf, Japanese pilots deliberately crashed their aircraft into American ships, sinking the escort carrier St. Lo. Suicide attacks became a central Japanese tactic for the rest of the war.

10-26.title: Alfred the Great dies
10-26.description: Alfred, king of the Anglo-Saxons, died after a reign spent defending Wessex against the Vikings. His fortified burhs, navy and promotion of learning in English laid foundations for a unified England.

10-26.title: The Uprising of Asen and Peter against Byzantine rule begins
