11-28.description: At least 3,000 men of the Scots Army under Tam Dalyell of the Binns defeated about 900 Covenanter insurgents led by James Wallace of Auchens at Rullion Green. The Covenanters, Scottish Presbyterians, were persecuted after the Restoration.

11-28.title: Arthur Griffith launches Sinn Féin's policy
11-28.description: At a convention in Dublin, Arthur Griffith set out the Sinn Féin policy, meaning 'we ourselves', of Irish self-reliance and a separate Irish parliament. The movement later became central to the struggle for independence.

11-28.title: Albania declares independence
11-28.description: In Vlorë, Ismail Qemali raised the Albanian flag and proclaimed independence from the Ottoman Empire during the First Balkan War. The great powers recognised the new state the following year.

11-28.title: Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin meet in Tehran
11-28.description: The 'Big Three' met together for the first time at the Tehran Conference. They committed to a cross-Channel invasion of France in 1944 and discussed the shape of post-war Europe.

11-29.title: Li Shimin destroys Xue Rengao's army at Qianshuiyuan
11-29.description: Li Shimin, the future Emperor Taizong of Tang, waited until the supplies of the Qin state ran short and then destroyed Xue Rengao's army at Qianshuiyuan, in present-day Shaanxi. Xue Rengao surrendered and was executed, opening the north-west to the Tang.

11-29.title: A great earthquake strikes Marash and the crusader lands
11-29.description: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 7.4 to 7.7 struck the area of Marash, now Kahramanmaraş, and also hit Antioch, Mamistra and Edessa in the crusader lands. At least 40,000 people were killed, a figure historians contest.

11-29.title: Cardinal Wolsey dies on his way to face treason charges
11-29.description: Thomas Wolsey, once Henry VIII's all-powerful Lord Chancellor, died at Leicester Abbey. He had fallen from favour after failing to obtain the annulment of Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon.

11-29.title: English East India Company ships defeat the Portuguese off Swally
11-29.description: The naval Battle of Swally, fought on 29 and 30 November off Suvali near Surat, ended in victory for four English East India Company galleons over four Portuguese galleons and 26 barks. It loosened the Portuguese Empire's hold on India.

11-29.title: British reinforcements end the Patriot siege of Fort Cumberland
11-29.description: British reinforcements ended a siege of Fort Cumberland by Patriot militia under Jonathan Eddy. With four to five hundred volunteers and Natives and little support from Massachusetts, Eddy had tried to bring the American Revolutionary War to Nova Scotia.

11-29.title: Colorado troops massacre Cheyenne and Arapaho at Sand Creek
11-29.description: Colonel John Chivington's volunteer cavalry attacked a peaceful camp at Sand Creek, Colorado, killing about 150 to 200 people, mostly women, children and the elderly. Congressional inquiries condemned the attack.

11-29.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
11-29.description: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, recommending separate Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control. Fighting broke out the next day.

11-29.title: Johnson sets up the Warren Commission
11-29.description: President Lyndon Johnson appointed a commission under Chief Justice Earl Warren to investigate Kennedy's assassination. Its 1964 report concluded that Lee Harvey Oswald acted alone.

11-30.title: Abu al-Abbas holds a victory parade in Baghdad after the Zanj Rebellion
11-30.description: Abu al-Abbas, the future caliph al-Mu'tadid, held a victory parade in Baghdad after the Zanj Rebellion. The revolt in southern Iraq, led by Ali ibn Muhammad and involving enslaved and freed Africans, had ended with the fall of al-Mukhtarah in August.

11-30.title: Edmund Ironside dies, leaving Cnut king of all England
11-30.description: Edmund II died weeks after agreeing to divide England with the Danish king Cnut. Cnut became sole king, later also ruling Denmark and Norway in a North Sea empire.

11-30.title: Jonathan Swift is born in Dublin
11-30.description: Jonathan Swift, later Dean of St Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, was born. His Gulliver's Travels and A Modest Proposal made him one of the great satirists in English.

11-30.title: Charles XII's Swedish troops rout the Russian army at Narva
11-30.description: About 8,000 Swedish troops under King Charles XII routed a Russian army three to four times their size that was besieging Narva, early in the Great Northern War. The defeat prompted Peter I's reforms, which gave Russia a standing professional army.

11-30.title: Samuel Clemens, later Mark Twain, is born
11-30.description: Samuel Langhorne Clemens was born in Florida, Missouri. As Mark Twain he wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, drawing on his boyhood on the Mississippi.

11-30.title: Scotland and England play the first international football match
11-30.description: Scotland and England drew 0-0 at Hamilton Crescent in Partick, Glasgow, before about 4,000 spectators. It is recognised by FIFA as the first official international football match.

11-30.title: The Soviet Union invades Finland
11-30.description: Soviet forces attacked Finland, starting the Winter War. Fierce Finnish resistance inflicted heavy losses before Finland ceded territory in March 1940, and the Red Army's poor showing was noted in Berlin.

11-30.title: Bill Clinton becomes the first US president to visit Northern Ireland
11-30.description: Bill Clinton addressed crowds in Belfast and Derry in support of the peace process. The visit added momentum to the talks that produced the Good Friday Agreement in 1998.

12-01.title: Charlemagne convenes an assembly in Rome to judge Pope Leo III
12-01.description: A week after arriving in Rome, Charlemagne called an assembly in St Peter's to hear charges against Pope Leo III, who cleared himself by oath. On Christmas Day Leo crowned Charlemagne emperor.

12-01.title: Henry V enters Paris in triumph
12-01.description: Henry V of England rode into Paris alongside Charles VI of France. Under the Treaty of Troyes he was regent and heir to the French throne, but his death in 1422 left the dual monarchy to his infant son.

12-01.title: Portuguese conspirators end Spanish rule in Lisbon
12-01.description: Nobles stormed the royal palace in Lisbon and proclaimed the Duke of Braganza king as John IV. The coup ended 60 years of union with Spain; the Braganza dynasty reigned until 1910.

12-01.title: Juan Lavalle overthrows Governor Manuel Dorrego in Buenos Aires
12-01.description: Returning with troops who had fought in the Cisplatine War, Juan Lavalle of the Unitarian Party mounted a coup in Buenos Aires Province, deposing Governor Manuel Dorrego, whom he captured and killed. The coup reignited the Argentine Civil Wars.

12-01.title: Ford installs a moving assembly line for the whole car
12-01.description: At Highland Park, Michigan, Ford began building the Model T on a moving assembly line. Assembly time fell from over 12 hours to about 90 minutes, and cheap cars reshaped modern industry.

12-01.title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
12-01.description: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give her seat to a white passenger. The 381-day bus boycott that followed brought Martin Luther King Jr. to national prominence.

12-01.title: Twelve nations sign the Antarctic Treaty
12-01.description: In Washington, twelve countries, including the United States and the Soviet Union, agreed to reserve Antarctica for peaceful scientific research. The treaty banned military activity and froze territorial claims.

12-01.title: Tunnellers from Britain and France meet under the Channel
12-01.description: British and French workers broke through the last wall of rock and shook hands beneath the English Channel. The tunnel opened in 1994, linking Britain to the Continent by rail.

12-02.title: Pope Innocent IV arrives at Lyon, threatened by Frederick II
12-02.description: Threatened by Emperor Frederick II, Pope Innocent IV arrived at Lyon. Early the next year he summoned the bishops to the First Council of Lyon, at which he excommunicated Frederick and declared him deposed.

12-02.title: Wren's new St Paul's Cathedral holds its first service
12-02.description: The choir of Christopher Wren's new St Paul's opened for worship with a thanksgiving service for the Peace of Ryswick. The cathedral, replacing the one lost in the Great Fire, was declared complete in 1711.

12-02.title: The Touro Synagogue is dedicated in Newport, Rhode Island
12-02.description: The Jeshuat Israel congregation dedicated the Touro Synagogue in Newport, Rhode Island, designed by Peter Harrison and built from 1759 under the leadership of Isaac Touro. It is the oldest surviving synagogue building in the United States.

12-02.title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor at Notre-Dame
12-02.description: In the presence of Pope Pius VII, Napoleon placed the imperial crown on his own head and then crowned Josephine. The ceremony proclaimed a new hereditary monarchy born of the Revolution.

12-02.title: Napoleon defeats Austria and Russia at Austerlitz
12-02.description: On the first anniversary of his coronation, Napoleon routed a larger Austro-Russian army at Austerlitz in Moravia. The 'Battle of the Three Emperors' knocked Austria out of the Third Coalition.

12-02.title: A Filipino rearguard holds Tirad Pass to cover Aguinaldo's escape
12-02.description: In northern Luzon, a 60-man Filipino rearguard under Brigadier General Gregorio del Pilar was overcome by more than 500 Americans, but delayed their advance long enough for President Emilio Aguinaldo and his troops to escape.

12-02.title: Fermi's team achieves the first controlled nuclear chain reaction
12-02.description: Under the stands of Stagg Field at the University of Chicago, Enrico Fermi's team started a self-sustaining chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1. It opened the way to atomic bombs and nuclear power.

12-02.title: The United Arab Emirates is founded
12-02.description: Six of the Trucial States, led by Abu Dhabi and Dubai, formed the United Arab Emirates after Britain's withdrawal from the Gulf. Ras al-Khaimah joined in 1972.

12-03.title: Pope John X crowns Berengar I of Italy as emperor
12-03.description: At St Peter's Basilica in Rome, Pope John X crowned Berengar I, King of Italy, as emperor, after Berengar had supplied troops for the campaign against the Saracens. Berengar in turn confirmed earlier emperors' donations to the papacy.

12-03.title: Mongol forces take the Burmese fort at Ngasaunggyan
12-03.description: After withstanding a Mongol siege for over two months, the Burmese fort at Ngasaunggyan fell to the invading forces of Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty. The invasions eventually toppled the 250-year-old Pagan Empire.

12-03.title: Francis Xavier dies within sight of China
12-03.description: The Jesuit missionary Francis Xavier died of fever on Shangchuan Island while waiting to enter mainland China. He had preached in India, South-East Asia and Japan, and was canonised in 1622.

12-03.title: John Paul Jones hoists the Continental Union Flag on the Alfred
12-03.description: In Philadelphia, Lieutenant John Paul Jones hoisted the Continental Union Flag aboard the Alfred, a frigate of the Continental Navy, the first vessel to fly the flag. It remained the de facto flag of the United States until 1777.

12-03.title: Moreau defeats the Austrians at Hohenlinden
12-03.description: French forces under General Jean Moreau crushed an Austrian army in snowy forest east of Munich. The defeat forced Austria to make peace at Lunéville in February 1801.

12-03.title: Georges Claude shows neon lighting at the Paris Motor Show
12-03.description: At the Paris Motor Show, the French engineer Georges Claude displayed glowing tubes of neon gas. Neon signs soon became a fixture of advertising and city nightlife worldwide.

12-03.title: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
12-03.description: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, Christiaan Barnard's team transplanted a heart into Louis Washkansky. He lived for 18 days before dying of pneumonia, but the operation launched transplant surgery.

12-03.title: Toxic gas leaks from a pesticide plant in Bhopal
12-03.description: Methyl isocyanate escaped from a Union Carbide plant in Bhopal overnight, killing thousands within days. Total deaths are estimated in the range of 15,000 or more, and hundreds of thousands suffered lasting harm.

12-04.title: Carloman dies, leaving Charlemagne sole king of the Franks
12-04.description: Carloman I, Charlemagne's brother and co-ruler, died suddenly. Charlemagne took over his kingdom, and Carloman's widow fled with her sons to the Lombards.

12-04.title: Louis IX and Henry III make peace in the Treaty of Paris
12-04.description: Kings Louis IX of France and Henry III of England signed the Treaty of Paris, by which Henry gave up his claims to Normandy, Anjou, Maine and Poitou and held Gascony as a duchy, paying homage for it to the French king.

12-04.title: Bertrand du Guesclin's French army defeats the English at Pontvallain
12-04.description: In two separate engagements, a French army of 5,200 men under Bertrand du Guesclin heavily defeated an English force of about the same size, which had broken away from the army of Sir Robert Knolles after a dispute between the commanders.

12-04.title: The Council of Trent holds its final session
12-04.description: The Council of Trent, which had opened on 13 December 1545, held its final session. Called in response to the Reformation, it had reaffirmed Catholic doctrine on scripture, justification and the seven sacraments and ordered reforms such as seminaries for priests.

12-04.title: The Observer is first published
12-04.description: The first issue of The Observer appeared in London. It is the world's oldest Sunday newspaper still in publication.

12-04.title: The National Grange is founded
12-04.description: Oliver Kelley and colleagues founded the Order of Patrons of Husbandry, known as the Grange, in Washington. It became a powerful voice for farmers against railway rates and monopolies.

12-04.title: The Mary Celeste is found drifting and abandoned
12-04.description: The crew of the Dei Gratia found the American brigantine Mary Celeste sailing unmanned in the Atlantic, her cargo intact and lifeboat gone. The fate of the ten people aboard has never been explained.

12-04.title: Pan Am ceases operations
12-04.description: Pan American World Airways flew its last flight after 64 years. The airline had pioneered transoceanic air travel and launched the Boeing 747, but it never recovered from deregulation, recession and the Lockerbie bombing.

12-05.title: The Senate condemns Catiline's fellow conspirators
12-05.description: After Cicero's fourth speech against Catiline, and Cato's demand for severity, the Senate voted to execute five conspirators without trial. Cicero was hailed as saviour of the Republic but later exiled for it.

12-05.title: The Fourth Council of Toledo opens under Isidore of Seville
12-05.description: All the bishops of Hispania gathered at the church of Saint Leocadia in Toledo for the council convened by the Visigothic king Sisenand, over which Isidore of Seville probably presided. It decreed a uniform liturgy throughout the kingdom.

12-05.title: An earthquake in the Jordan Rift Valley devastates the Levant
12-05.description: An earthquake in the Jordan Rift Valley, estimated at above magnitude 7.0, caused extreme devastation across the Levant and a tsunami along the Mediterranean coast. At least 70,000 people were killed.

12-05.title: John II creates the first franc
12-05.description: By an ordinance issued at Compiègne, the newly released John II of France created the gold franc, partly to raise his ransom. The franc remained the name of French currency until the euro.

12-05.title: Pope Innocent VIII issues a bull against witchcraft
12-05.description: The bull Summis desiderantes affectibus authorised the inquisitors Heinrich Kramer and Jacob Sprenger to pursue witches in Germany. Kramer printed it with his Malleus Maleficarum, fuelling later witch hunts.

12-05.title: Frederick the Great routs an Austrian army at Leuthen
12-05.description: West of Breslau in Silesia, Frederick the Great used the oblique order of attack to rout an Austrian army about twice the size of his own under Prince Charles of Lorraine. The victory restored Prussian control of Silesia.

12-05.title: Mozart dies in Vienna aged 35
12-05.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart died after a short illness, leaving his Requiem unfinished. In a career of barely three decades he wrote more than 600 works, including The Marriage of Figaro and The Magic Flute.

12-05.title: Prohibition ends in the United States
12-05.description: Utah became the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, repealing national Prohibition. The ban on alcohol had lasted almost 14 years and fed a boom in organised crime.

12-06.title: Leo VIII claims the papacy with the backing of Otto I
12-06.description: Leo VIII, a Roman prelate appointed by Emperor Otto I, was ordained a bishop and claimed the Holy See in opposition to John XII. The Catholic Church counts him an antipope until 23 June 964 and the legitimate pope thereafter.

12-06.title: Béla I is crowned king of Hungary at Székesfehérvár
12-06.description: Béla I, who had rebelled with Polish help when his brother Andrew I named his infant son Solomon as heir, was crowned at Székesfehérvár, the coronation place of Hungarian kings. He reigned until his death in 1063.

12-06.title: The Mongols sack Kiev
12-06.description: Batu Khan's army stormed Kiev after a siege, massacring much of the population. A traveller passing a few years later reported barely 200 houses standing; the city's ruin ended Kievan Rus as a power.

12-06.title: Christopher Columbus lands on Hispaniola
12-06.description: Christopher Columbus, who had mistaken Cuba for Japan, landed on Hispaniola at a bay he named San Nicolas, in present-day Haiti, and was welcomed by the Taíno. The island became the first base of Spanish colonisation in the Americas.

12-06.title: Spanish conquistadors found San Francisco de Quito
12-06.description: Sebastián de Benalcázar's men founded the Spanish city of Quito on the site of an Inca centre in the Andes. Its historic centre is today one of the best-preserved colonial cities in the Americas.

12-06.title: The Jacobite army turns back at Derby
12-06.description: Overruling Charles Edward Stuart, his commanders began a retreat from Derby, about 125 miles from London. The rising ended at Culloden in April 1746.

12-06.title: Edison records and plays back 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'
12-06.description: Thomas Edison spoke the nursery rhyme into his tinfoil phonograph and heard his voice played back. It was the first time a machine had reproduced recorded human speech.

12-06.title: Finland declares independence
12-06.description: The Finnish parliament adopted a declaration of independence from Russia, a month after the Bolshevik seizure of power. Lenin's government recognised it at the end of the month.

12-06.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed
12-06.description: Irish and British delegates signed a treaty in London creating the Irish Free State as a dominion, with Northern Ireland able to opt out. Divisions over it led to the Irish Civil War.

12-07.title: Cicero is killed on Mark Antony's orders
12-07.description: Proscribed by the Second Triumvirate, Marcus Tullius Cicero was overtaken by soldiers near Formiae and killed. His head and hands were displayed in the Forum, where he had attacked Antony in his Philippics.

12-07.title: Justin II proclaims his general Tiberius caesar
12-07.description: During a respite from a severe mental illness, the Eastern Roman emperor Justin II proclaimed his general Tiberius caesar and adopted him as his son. Tiberius became co-emperor in 578 and reigned until 582 as Tiberius II Constantine.

12-07.title: Apprentice boys shut the gates of Derry against a Jacobite force
12-07.description: In Derry, 13 apprentices shut the town's gates against Jacobite forces, an act of rebellion against James II. Its Protestant defenders went on to withstand a siege by James II's army for 105 days in 1689.

12-07.title: The mayor of Toruń and nine Lutheran officials are executed
12-07.description: After a Protestant crowd vandalised the Jesuit college in Toruń (Thorn) in Royal Prussia, the Polish supreme court blamed Mayor Johann Gottfried Rösner and nine other Lutheran officials for neglect of duty. They were sentenced to death and executed.

12-07.title: The Theatre Royal, Covent Garden, opens
12-07.description: John Rich opened his new theatre at Covent Garden with Congreve's The Way of the World. Twice rebuilt after fires, it became the Royal Opera House in 1892.

12-07.title: Marshal Ney is executed by firing squad
12-07.description: Michel Ney, whom Napoleon called 'the bravest of the brave', was shot in Paris for treason after joining his former emperor during the Hundred Days. He refused a blindfold and is said to have given the order to fire.

12-07.title: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
12-07.description: Japanese carrier aircraft struck the US Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, killing more than 2,400 Americans and sinking or damaging 19 ships. The United States entered the Second World War the next day.

12-07.title: Indonesia invades East Timor
12-07.description: Indonesian forces invaded East Timor nine days after Fretilin declared independence from Portugal. The occupation cost an estimated 100,000 to 180,000 lives before a UN-supervised vote led to independence.

12-08.title: Northern Wei destroys the Later Yan army at Canhe Slope
12-08.description: Tuoba Gui's Northern Wei forces surprised the retreating Later Yan army of Murong Bao, sent on a punitive campaign against its former vassal, and destroyed it. The victory opened the North China Plain to Tuoba Gui.

12-08.title: Du Fu returns to Chang'an with the Tang emperor
12-08.description: The poet Du Fu, who had escaped Chang'an during the An Lushan Rebellion and rejoined the court, returned to the capital with the emperor after government forces recaptured it. Nearly 1,500 poems attributed to him survive.

12-08.title: Washington's army retreats across the Delaware
12-08.description: The last of George Washington's beaten Continental Army crossed the Delaware into Pennsylvania, taking every boat to stop British pursuit. Weeks later he crossed back to strike at Trenton.

12-08.title: Sir William Howe withdraws to Philadelphia after White Marsh
12-08.description: The British commander-in-chief, Sir William Howe, withdrew his troops to Philadelphia, ending the Battle of White Marsh, a series of skirmishes around Whitemarsh Township, Pennsylvania. It was the last major engagement of 1777 between British and American forces.

12-08.title: Pius IX defines the Immaculate Conception
12-08.description: In the bull Ineffabilis Deus, Pope Pius IX declared as dogma that the Virgin Mary was conceived without original sin. Other Christian traditions do not accept the doctrine.

12-08.title: The United States and Britain declare war on Japan
12-08.description: Franklin Roosevelt asked Congress to declare war, calling 7 December 'a date which will live in infamy'. Congress agreed within the hour, and Britain also declared war on Japan.

12-08.title: John Lennon is shot dead in New York
12-08.description: Mark David Chapman shot John Lennon outside the Dakota building in Manhattan. The killing of the former Beatle prompted vigils around the world.

12-08.title: Leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agree to dissolve the USSR
12-08.description: Meeting in the Belovezha Forest, Boris Yeltsin, Leonid Kravchuk and Stanislav Shushkevich declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist and created the Commonwealth of Independent States.

12-09.title: Belisarius enters Rome unopposed as the Gothic garrison withdraws
12-09.description: The citizens of Rome, mindful of the fate of Naples, put up no resistance to Justinian's general Belisarius, and the 4,000-strong Gothic garrison withdrew. Belisarius went on to take Ravenna in 540.

12-09.title: The Khazars destroy an Umayyad army at Marj Ardabil
12-09.description: Near Ardabil in north-western Iran, a Khazar army led by Barjik destroyed the forces of the Umayyad Caliphate and killed their commander, al-Jarrah ibn Abdallah al-Hakami. The Khazars then raided deep into the caliphate as far as northern Mesopotamia.

12-09.title: Malcolm IV, the 'Maiden King' of Scotland, dies
12-09.description: Malcolm IV died unmarried at 24, after a reign in which he surrendered Northumbria and Cumbria to Henry II of England. His brother William the Lion succeeded him and reigned for 49 years.

12-09.title: Juan Diego reports a vision of the Virgin at Tepeyac
12-09.description: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to the Indigenous convert Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe became Mexico's most revered religious symbol.

12-09.title: Williamite dragoons rout an Irish Army detachment at Reading
12-09.description: Dutch States Army dragoons under Hans Bentinck, supported by Williamite civilians, routed an Irish Army detachment under Patrick Sarsfield from Reading in Berkshire. It was one of only two substantial battles fought in England during the Glorious Revolution.

12-09.title: Jerusalem surrenders to British forces
12-09.description: The mayor of Jerusalem surrendered the city to the British army, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule. General Allenby entered on foot two days later.

12-09.title: British forces launch Operation Compass in Egypt
12-09.description: British and Commonwealth troops attacked Italian camps in western Egypt. In two months they advanced 500 miles and took some 130,000 prisoners, before Rommel's arrival turned the tide.

12-09.title: Tanganyika becomes independent
12-09.description: Tanganyika became independent from Britain, with Julius Nyerere as prime minister. In 1964 it united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.

12-10.title: The League of Cambrai is formed against Venice
12-10.description: Pope Julius II, Louis XII of France, Emperor Maximilian I and Ferdinand of Aragon formally concluded the League of Cambrai against Venice. Routed at Agnadello in 1509, Venice had recovered most of its mainland territory by 1516.
links: War of the League of Cambrai

12-10.title: Luther burns the papal bull against him
12-10.description: Outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate, Martin Luther burned Leo X's bull threatening him with excommunication, along with books of canon law. Rome excommunicated him the following month.

12-10.title: Thomas Culpeper and Francis Dereham are executed
12-10.description: Thomas Culpeper, a close friend of Henry VIII accused of adultery with Queen Catherine Howard, was beheaded for treason. Francis Dereham, whose involvement with Catherine before her marriage to the king had been discovered, was also executed.

12-10.title: The Dutch Regiment de Marine is founded
12-10.description: The grand pensionary Johan de Witt and Admiral Michiel de Ruyter established the Regiment de Marine of the Dutch Republic. The Netherlands Marine Corps, the second-oldest marine corps still active, traces its origins to it.

12-10.title: Mississippi becomes the 20th US state
12-10.description: Mississippi was admitted to the Union. Its fertile lands became the heart of the cotton economy built on slavery, and later a key battleground of the civil rights movement.

12-10.title: Wyoming Territory gives women the vote
12-10.description: Governor John Campbell signed a law granting women in Wyoming Territory the right to vote and hold office, the first such law in the United States. Wyoming is still called the 'Equality State'.

12-10.title: Alfred Nobel dies in San Remo
12-10.description: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite, died in Italy. His will left most of his fortune to fund prizes, first awarded on the anniversary of his death in 1901.

12-10.title: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
12-10.description: Meeting in Paris, the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights without a vote against. The drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.

12-11.title: Emperor Xian abdicates, ending the Han dynasty
12-11.description: Emperor Xian, the last emperor of the Eastern Han dynasty and long a puppet of warlords, was forced to abdicate by Cao Pi, son of Cao Cao. Cao Pi founded the Wei dynasty, opening the Three Kingdoms period.

12-11.title: Julian enters Constantinople as sole Roman emperor
12-11.description: Julian entered Constantinople as sole emperor and, despite his rejection of Christianity, presided over the Christian burial of Constantius, escorting the body to the Church of the Apostles. The act demonstrated his lawful right to the throne.

12-11.title: The Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil is assassinated
12-11.description: Al-Mutawakkil, the tenth Abbasid caliph, was murdered by Turkish military officers. His death began the Anarchy at Samarra, which lasted until 870 and saw four caliphs made and unmade by rival military groups.

12-11.title: Emperor Nikephoros II Phokas is murdered by John Tzimiskes
12-11.description: The Byzantine emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, who had retaken Crete and Cyprus and conquered Cilicia, was murdered by his nephew, the general John Tzimiskes, who seized the throne as John I.

12-11.title: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, last native Prince of Wales, is killed
12-11.description: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd was killed near Cilmeri during Edward I's conquest of Wales. Wales lost its independence, and in 1301 Edward gave the title Prince of Wales to his own son.

12-11.title: James II flees London
12-11.description: As William of Orange advanced, James II slipped out of Whitehall and dropped the Great Seal into the Thames. Caught at Faversham, he escaped to France later that month; Parliament treated his flight as abdication.

12-11.title: Louis XVI goes on trial before the National Convention
12-11.description: The deposed king, now called Louis Capet, appeared before the National Convention to answer charges of treason. He was convicted and guillotined in January 1793.

12-11.title: Edward VIII abdicates to marry Wallis Simpson
12-11.description: The abdication took legal effect, and that evening Edward broadcast that he could not reign 'without the help and support of the woman I love'. His brother succeeded as George VI.

12-11.title: Germany and Italy declare war on the United States
12-11.description: Four days after Pearl Harbor, Hitler and Mussolini declared war on the United States. The decision brought American power fully into the war in Europe.

12-12.title: Heraclius defeats the Persians near Nineveh
12-12.description: The Byzantine emperor Heraclius routed a Sasanian army near the ruins of Nineveh in Mesopotamia. The victory ended a 26-year war, but both exhausted empires soon fell prey to the Arab conquests.

12-12.title: Marie of Enghien sells Argos and Nauplia to Venice
12-12.description: Unable to defend her possessions, Marie of Enghien sold the lordship of Argos and Nauplia to Venice for an annual subsidy of 700 ducats. Before the Venetians arrived, Theodore I Palaiologos and Nerio I Acciaioli seized both towns with Ottoman help.

12-12.title: Pennsylvania becomes the second state to ratify the US Constitution
12-12.description: Pennsylvania, where the Philadelphia Convention had drafted the Constitution earlier in the year, became the second state to ratify it. The Constitution, ratified in 1788 and in force from 1789, replaced the Articles of Confederation.

12-12.title: USS Cairo sinks after striking a mine on the Yazoo River
12-12.description: The Union river gunboat USS Cairo, lead ship of the City-class casemate ironclads, was sunk by a mine on the Yazoo River in Mississippi, which joins the Mississippi River just north of Vicksburg.

12-12.title: Marconi receives the first transatlantic radio signal
12-12.description: At Signal Hill in Newfoundland, Guglielmo Marconi heard the Morse letter 'S' sent from Poldhu in Cornwall, some 3,500 kilometres away. The feat showed that radio could span oceans.

12-12.title: George V announces the move of India's capital to Delhi
12-12.description: At the Delhi Durbar, attended by hundreds of thousands, King-Emperor George V announced that the capital of British India would move from Calcutta to Delhi. New Delhi was inaugurated in 1931.

12-12.title: Kenya gains independence with Jomo Kenyatta as prime minister
12-12.description: Kenya became independent from Britain. Jomo Kenyatta, jailed by the colonial authorities during the Mau Mau emergency, became prime minister and later the country's first president.

12-12.title: The Supreme Court halts the Florida recount in Bush v. Gore
12-12.description: By five votes to four, the US Supreme Court stopped the manual recount of presidential votes in Florida. The ruling left George W. Bush the winner of Florida, and of the presidency, by 537 votes.

12-13.title: Salerno surrenders to the Norman Robert Guiscard
12-13.description: Robert Guiscard, the Norman conqueror who had married Sikelgaita, daughter of Guaimar IV, took Salerno from his brother-in-law Gisulf II, its last Lombard prince. Gisulf held out in the citadel until May of the following year.

12-13.title: Pope Celestine V resigns after five months
12-13.description: The hermit-pope Celestine V renounced the papacy, overwhelmed by its politics. Dante appears to condemn him for 'the great refusal', but the church later canonised him.

12-13.title: The Council of Trent opens
12-13.description: The Catholic Church's council opened at Trent in northern Italy and met, with long breaks, until 1563. It reaffirmed Catholic doctrine against Protestant teaching and reformed clerical discipline.

12-13.title: Francis Drake sets sail from Plymouth to circle the world
12-13.description: Francis Drake left Plymouth with five ships on an expedition authorised by Queen Elizabeth I. Called a voyage of discovery but in effect a covert raiding voyage, it returned in September 1580 as the second circumnavigation of the world.

12-13.title: Abel Tasman sights New Zealand
12-13.description: Dutch navigator Abel Tasman sighted the west coast of New Zealand's South Island, the first recorded European sighting. A violent encounter with Māori in Golden Bay days later meant his crew never landed.

12-13.title: Sir William Waller surprises a Royalist garrison at Alton
12-13.description: Parliamentarian forces under Sir William Waller surprised a winter garrison of Royalist infantry and cavalry under the Earl of Crawford at Alton in Hampshire. It was the first decisive defeat of Sir Ralph Hopton, the Royalist leader in the south.

12-13.title: Japanese troops capture Nanjing
12-13.description: Japanese forces took China's capital, Nanjing, and began weeks of mass killing, rape and looting. Estimates of the dead range from tens of thousands to over 300,000, and the massacre remains bitterly contested.

12-13.title: British cruisers fight the Graf Spee at the River Plate
12-13.description: Three British cruisers engaged the German pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee off the River Plate estuary. Damaged, she took refuge in Montevideo, and four days later her captain scuttled her.

12-14.title: An earthquake shakes Constantinople and weakens Hagia Sophia
12-14.description: A powerful earthquake damaged much of Constantinople and cracked the great dome of Hagia Sophia, which collapsed the following May. It was rebuilt higher and rededicated in 562.

12-14.title: Emperor Wenzong's plot against the palace eunuchs fails
12-14.description: Emperor Wenzong of Tang and the chancellor Li Xun planned to lure the palace eunuchs to view sweet dew, an auspicious omen, and kill them. The eunuchs discovered the ambush, and their troops killed the chancellors and many officials.

12-14.title: Nostradamus is born in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence
12-14.description: Michel de Nostredame, physician and astrologer, was born in Provence. His Prophecies of 1555, written in vague rhymed quatrains, have been claimed as predictions of countless later events.

12-14.title: The Theresian Military Academy is founded at Wiener Neustadt
12-14.description: The Theresian Military Academy was founded in the castle of Wiener Neustadt in Lower Austria, once a residence of Emperor Frederick III. The Austrian Armed Forces still train their officers there.

12-14.title: Alexander Hamilton marries Elizabeth Schuyler in Albany
12-14.description: Alexander Hamilton, who served as George Washington's aide in the Revolutionary War, married Elizabeth Schuyler at the Schuyler Mansion in Albany, New York. From 1789 he was the first secretary of the treasury.

12-14.title: George Washington dies at Mount Vernon
12-14.description: George Washington died aged 67 after a throat infection, worsened by heavy bloodletting. Having twice given up power, as commander and as president, he was mourned as the father of his country.

12-14.title: Max Planck presents the quantum hypothesis
12-14.description: Before the German Physical Society in Berlin, Max Planck proposed that energy is emitted in discrete packets, or quanta. The idea, introduced to solve a problem in heat radiation, became the basis of quantum physics.

12-14.title: Roald Amundsen's party reaches the South Pole
12-14.description: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and four companions became the first people to reach the South Pole. Robert Falcon Scott's British party arrived 34 days later to find the Norwegian tent and flag.

12-15.title: The future emperor Nero is born at Antium
12-15.description: Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus, later the emperor Nero, was born at Antium to Agrippina the Younger. Adopted by Claudius, he became emperor at 16 and was the last of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

12-15.title: Belisarius defeats the Vandal king Gelimer at Tricamarum
12-15.description: West of Carthage, the Byzantine army of Belisarius defeated the Vandal king Gelimer, whose brother Tzazon was killed. Gelimer fled to the mountains and surrendered in 534, ending the Vandal Kingdom and restoring North Africa to the Roman Empire.

12-15.title: Constantine VIII becomes sole emperor after 63 years as co-emperor
12-15.description: Co-emperor in name since 962, alongside his father Romanos II, Nikephoros II Phokas, John I Tzimiskes and his brother Basil II, Constantine VIII became sole emperor on Basil's death. He ruled alone until 1028.

12-15.title: Jin emperor Wanyan Liang is assassinated by his own officers
12-15.description: After the Jin defeat by the Southern Song at the Battle of Caishi, officers of the Jurchen emperor Wanyan Liang rebelled and killed him in his camp. His successor posthumously demoted him to the rank of prince.

12-15.title: The Bill of Rights is ratified
12-15.description: Virginia's approval gave the first ten amendments to the US Constitution the required three-quarters of states. They guarantee freedoms of speech, religion, press and assembly, and rights to due process.

12-15.title: Sitting Bull is killed at Standing Rock
12-15.description: Lakota leader Sitting Bull, a leader at the victory over Custer at the Little Bighorn, was shot dead by Indian police trying to arrest him. Two weeks later came the massacre at Wounded Knee.

12-15.title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
12-15.description: The film of Margaret Mitchell's novel premiered at Loew's Grand Theatre in Atlanta. It won eight competitive Academy Awards, and allowing for inflation it remains the highest-grossing film ever.

12-15.title: The Leaning Tower of Pisa reopens
12-15.description: After eleven years of closure and stabilisation work, the Leaning Tower of Pisa reopened to visitors. Engineers had reduced its tilt by about 44 centimetres, securing it for centuries.

12-16.title: Pepin of Herstal, ruler of the Franks, dies
12-16.description: Pepin of Herstal, the mayor of the palace who held real power over the Frankish kingdoms, died at Jupille. After a struggle, his son Charles Martel took control and laid the ground for the Carolingian dynasty.

12-16.title: An Lushan launches his rebellion against the Tang
12-16.description: An Lushan, a Tang frontier general of Sogdian and Turkic descent, rose in revolt against his rival, the chancellor Yang Guozhong. The rebellion lasted until 763, captured both Tang capitals and permanently weakened central authority.

12-16.title: Henry VI is crowned king of France in Paris
12-16.description: The ten-year-old Henry VI of England was crowned king of France at Notre-Dame. By 1453 the English had lost all their French lands except Calais.

12-16.title: Admiral Yi Sun-sin is killed in the victory at Noryang
12-16.description: A combined Korean and Ming fleet under Yi Sun-sin and Chen Lin attacked Japanese ships gathering in the Noryang Strait to withdraw, sinking a large number. Yi was killed in this last major battle of the Imjin War.

12-16.title: The Boston Tea Party
12-16.description: Colonists, some disguised as Mohawk Indians, boarded three ships in Boston Harbor and threw 342 chests of East India Company tea into the water. Britain's punitive response pushed the colonies towards revolution.

12-16.title: Voortrekkers defeat a Zulu army at Blood River
12-16.description: A laager of about 470 Voortrekkers repelled thousands of Zulu warriors sent by King Dingane at the Ncome River. The victory became a central symbol of Afrikaner nationalism.

12-16.title: Germany launches the Battle of the Bulge
12-16.description: German forces attacked through the Ardennes in Belgium and Luxembourg, catching the Americans by surprise. The offensive was contained within weeks and used up Germany's last reserves in the west.

12-16.title: Kazakhstan declares independence
12-16.description: Kazakhstan became the last Soviet republic to declare independence, days before the USSR was dissolved. Nursultan Nazarbayev led the vast Central Asian country for nearly three decades.

12-17.title: Totila's Ostrogoths take Rome
12-17.description: After a long siege, the Ostrogothic king Totila entered Rome when Isaurian guards opened a gate. The city, fought over repeatedly in Justinian's Gothic War, was left largely depopulated.

12-17.title: Romanos I Lekapenos is crowned co-emperor with Constantine VII
12-17.description: Romanos I Lekapenos, an admiral of humble origin and father-in-law of the young Constantine VII, was crowned co-emperor and governed in his place. He made peace with Bulgaria in 927 and ruled until his sons deposed him in 944.

12-17.title: William Longsword of Normandy is murdered at Picquigny
12-17.description: William Longsword, son of Rollo and ruler of Normandy since about 927, was ambushed and killed by men of Arnulf I, Count of Flanders, at a peace conference at Picquigny. He left his young son Richard I as heir.

12-17.title: The Myinsaing brothers overthrow King Kyawswa of Pagan
12-17.description: King Kyawswa of Pagan, who held little more than the capital and had accepted Yuan overlordship to protect himself, was overthrown by the three Myinsaing brothers, nominally his viceroys. It marked the de facto end of the Pagan Kingdom.

12-17.title: Pope Paul III excommunicates Henry VIII
12-17.description: Pope Paul III published the bull of excommunication against Henry VIII, prepared in 1535 but suspended. It came after Henry's agents destroyed the shrine of Thomas Becket at Canterbury.

12-17.title: The Wright brothers make the first powered flights
12-17.description: At Kill Devil Hills near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, Orville Wright flew the Wright Flyer for 12 seconds and about 37 metres. Of four flights that day, Wilbur's longest lasted 59 seconds.

12-17.title: The Graf Spee is scuttled off Montevideo
12-17.description: Believing a superior British force waited outside, Captain Hans Langsdorff scuttled the Admiral Graf Spee in the River Plate. He took his own life three days later.

12-17.title: The Simpsons premieres as a series
12-17.description: Fox broadcast the first full episode of The Simpsons, a Christmas special. It became the longest-running American animated series and scripted primetime show.

12-18.title: Alfonso I of Aragon takes Zaragoza from the Almoravids
12-18.description: King Alfonso I of Aragon, known as the Battler, conquered Zaragoza, the most important Almoravid city in north-eastern Spain, and made it the capital of his kingdom. Its fall marked the deterioration of the Almoravids' northern front.

12-18.title: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty
12-18.description: Kublai Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan and Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan for his realm in China. The Yuan completed the conquest of the Southern Song in 1279 and ruled China until 1368.

12-18.title: An uprising against forced conversions breaks out in Granada
12-18.description: In Granada's Albaicín, a crowd killed a constable taking a woman away for questioning after she cried out that she was being forced to become Christian. It began the Rebellion of the Alpujarras against mass forced conversions.

12-18.title: Americans observe the first national day of thanksgiving
12-18.description: The Continental Congress set aside 18 December as a day of thanksgiving for the victory at Saratoga. It was the first such national observance by the new United States.

12-18.title: The 13th Amendment abolishing slavery is proclaimed
12-18.description: Secretary of State William Seward certified that the 13th Amendment had been ratified by the required number of states. It abolished slavery throughout the United States, freeing about four million people.

12-18.title: 'Piltdown Man' is presented to the Geological Society
12-18.description: Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward announced fossils from Piltdown in Sussex as an early human ancestor. In 1953 they were exposed as a forgery combining a human skull and an orang-utan jaw.

12-18.title: The Battle of Verdun ends
12-18.description: After ten months of fighting, French counter-attacks closed the Battle of Verdun. About 700,000 French and German soldiers were killed, wounded or missing, and the front was almost back where it began.

12-18.title: The US launches SCORE, the first communications satellite
12-18.description: An Atlas rocket placed Project SCORE in orbit. The next day it broadcast a recorded Christmas message from President Eisenhower, the first voice transmitted from space.

12-19.title: Henry II is crowned king of England at Westminster Abbey
12-19.description: Henry II, the first Plantagenet king, was crowned in Westminster Abbey. His lands in England, Normandy, Anjou and, through his wife Eleanor, Aquitaine were later called the Angevin Empire.

12-19.title: Anne of Brittany marries Maximilian I by proxy
12-19.description: Anne, Duchess of Brittany since 1488, was married by proxy to Maximilian I, King of the Romans. She went on to marry Charles VIII of France in 1491 and Louis XII in 1499, twice becoming queen of France.

12-19.title: Catholics and Huguenots clash at Dreux
12-19.description: The first major battle of the French Wars of Religion was fought at Dreux, west of Paris. Both armies' commanders were captured, and the bloody outcome showed the war would be long.

12-19.title: New England militia defeat the Narragansett in the Great Swamp Fight
12-19.description: In King Philip's War, New England colonial militia, with 150 Pequot allies, defeated the Narragansett people near Kingston, Rhode Island, inflicting a huge number of casualties, including many hundreds of women and children. It is also called the Great Swamp Massacre.

12-19.title: Washington's army goes into winter quarters at Valley Forge
12-19.description: About 12,000 Continental soldiers marched into camp at Valley Forge, Pennsylvania. Some 2,000 died of disease over the winter, but drilling under Baron von Steuben made the survivors a more effective army.

12-19.title: The Siege of Toulon ends as the British abandon the city
12-19.description: French artillery under Napoleon Bonaparte forced the British to abandon Toulon, ending the Republic's siege of the port, held by Royalists aided by the First Coalition. The recapture secured southern France from invasion.

12-19.title: Charles Dickens publishes A Christmas Carol
12-19.description: Charles Dickens's novella about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge went on sale and sold out its first printing by Christmas Eve. It shaped Victorian ideals of a charitable, family-centred Christmas.

12-19.title: The House impeaches President Clinton
12-19.description: The US House of Representatives impeached Bill Clinton for perjury and obstruction of justice related to the Monica Lewinsky affair. The Senate acquitted him in February 1999.

12-20.title: Romanos I Lekapenos is deposed by his sons
12-20.description: The Byzantine emperor Romanos I Lekapenos, regent and senior co-ruler for Constantine VII since 920, was arrested by two of his sons and forced to abdicate. He lived out his life as a monk.

12-20.title: The Synod of Sutri opens to settle rival claims to the papacy
12-20.description: The council called by Henry III, king of Germany, opened at Sutri, at the edge of the Duchy of Rome, to deal with rival claimants to the papacy. Henry deposed the rival popes and went on to install reforming German popes.

12-20.title: Mongol envoys meet Louis IX in Cyprus
12-20.description: In Cyprus, King Louis IX of France, bound for the Seventh Crusade, received two Mongol envoys bearing a letter from Eljigidei, the Mongol commander in Persia. They proposed that Louis land in Egypt while Eljigidei attacked Baghdad.

12-20.title: Virginia Company ships sail for America
12-20.description: The Susan Constant, Godspeed and Discovery left London with about 105 colonists. In May 1607 they founded Jamestown, the first permanent English settlement in North America.

12-20.title: The United States takes possession of Louisiana
12-20.description: In a ceremony in New Orleans, France formally handed the Louisiana Territory to the United States. The purchase roughly doubled the country's size and gave it control of the Mississippi.

12-20.title: South Carolina secedes from the Union
12-20.description: A convention in Charleston voted unanimously to leave the United States after Lincoln's election. Six more states followed before his inauguration, forming the Confederacy.

12-20.title: The United States invades Panama
12-20.description: US forces launched Operation Just Cause to remove Panama's military ruler Manuel Noriega, who was wanted in the US on drug trafficking charges. Noriega surrendered on 3 January 1990.

12-20.title: Argentina's president resigns amid riots
12-20.description: President Fernando de la Rúa resigned and fled the Casa Rosada by helicopter as protests over economic collapse left dozens dead. Days later Argentina declared the largest sovereign default to that date.

12-21.title: The Senate recognises Vespasian as emperor
12-21.description: The day after Vitellius was killed in Rome, the Senate granted Vespasian the powers of emperor, ending the Year of the Four Emperors. His Flavian dynasty restored stability and began the Colosseum.

12-21.title: Weinsberg surrenders to Conrad III after a siege
12-21.description: After a siege of several weeks, the town and castle of Weinsberg surrendered to King Conrad III, the first ruler of the Hohenstaufen dynasty. The siege was a decisive clash in the rivalry between the Hohenstaufen and the Welfs.

12-21.title: Batu Khan's Mongols sack Ryazan
12-21.description: After a short siege, the Mongol army of Batu Khan destroyed Ryazan, the first city of Kievan Rus' to be besieged in the invasion. The city never recovered, and the seat of the principality moved to Pereslavl-Ryazansky.

12-21.title: Castile defeats the forces of Granada at Linuesa
12-21.description: At Huesa in the Kingdom of Jaén, the forces of the Kingdom of Castile defeated those of the Emirate of Granada, the last independent Muslim state in Western Europe, in an action of the Reconquista.

12-21.title: A Mayflower party lands at Plymouth
12-21.description: An exploring party from the Mayflower landed at Plymouth harbour, where the Pilgrims decided to settle (11 December Old Style). Half the colonists died during the first winter.

12-21.title: The Curies identify radium
12-21.description: Working in a Paris shed, Marie and Pierre Curie detected a new, intensely radioactive element in pitchblende, announced days later as radium. Isolating it took Marie Curie another twelve years.

12-21.title: Apollo 8 launches for the Moon
12-21.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders lifted off on the first crewed flight to leave Earth's orbit. On Christmas Eve they orbited the Moon and photographed 'Earthrise'.

12-21.title: A bomb destroys Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie
12-21.description: A bomb exploded aboard a Boeing 747 over Lockerbie in Scotland, killing all 259 on board and 11 people on the ground. A Libyan intelligence officer was convicted in 2001.

12-22.title: The Damghan earthquake strikes the eastern Alborz mountains
12-22.description: An earthquake of estimated magnitude 7.9 struck near Damghan, capital of the province of Qumis in the Abbasid Caliphate, with its worst shaking along some 350 kilometres of the eastern Alborz. It caused approximately 200,000 deaths, though the toll is debated.

12-22.title: The rebel Huang Chao captures Luoyang, eastern capital of the Tang
12-22.description: Huang Chao's rebel army quickly took Luoyang, the eastern capital of the Tang dynasty. Emperor Xizong then abandoned Chang'an for Chengdu, and Huang entered the capital and declared himself emperor of a new state of Qi.

12-22.title: Stephen of Blois is crowned king of England
12-22.description: Weeks after Henry I's death, his nephew Stephen was crowned at Westminster despite having sworn to support Henry's daughter, the Empress Matilda. The civil war that followed became known as the Anarchy.

12-22.title: Pope Honorius III confirms the Dominican Order
12-22.description: With the bull Religiosam vitam, Pope Honorius III gave universal recognition to the Order of Preachers founded by the Castilian priest Dominic de Guzmán. Already recognised by the bishop of Toulouse, the order followed the Rule of St Augustine.

12-22.title: Almería submits to the Catholic Monarchs
12-22.description: The port city of Almería, part of the Nasrid emirate of Granada, submitted to the sovereignty of the Catholic Monarchs, Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile. The last Nasrid ruler, Muhammad XII, surrendered Granada itself in 1492.

12-22.title: The Old Pretender lands in Scotland, too late
12-22.description: James Francis Edward Stuart landed at Peterhead to lead the Jacobite rising. After the defeat at Preston and the stalemate at Sheriffmuir in November, the cause was failing, and he sailed back to France in February.

12-22.title: A court martial convicts Captain Alfred Dreyfus
12-22.description: A French military court convicted the Jewish officer Alfred Dreyfus of passing secrets to Germany and sentenced him to deportation for life. His innocence, and the cover-up, split France in the Dreyfus Affair.

12-22.title: The SR-71 Blackbird makes its first flight
12-22.description: Lockheed's SR-71 reconnaissance aircraft first flew at Palmdale, California. Able to cruise above Mach 3 at about 25,000 metres, it remains the fastest crewed jet-powered aircraft.

12-23.title: Childebert's death leaves Chlothar I king of all the Franks
12-23.description: Childebert died after a long illness without heirs, allowing his brother Chlothar I to reunite the Frankish kingdom, as their father Clovis I had done, and to seize Childebert's treasure. The realm was divided again among Chlothar's sons in 561.

12-23.title: Ghazan's Mongols defeat the Mamluks at Wadi al-Khaznadar
12-23.description: Near Homs, the Ilkhanate ruler Ghazan, joined by King Hethum II of Armenian Cilicia, defeated the army of the Mamluk Sultanate, the only major Mongol victory in their long conflict. Damascus surrendered soon after, but the Mongols made no lasting gains.

12-23.title: Mapuche warriors kill Governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola at Curalaba
12-23.description: In southern Chile, Mapuche warriors under Pelantaro ambushed and killed the Spanish governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola and his escort. The victory set off a general uprising that destroyed the Spanish towns south of the Biobío river.

12-23.title: James II flees England in the Glorious Revolution
12-23.description: King James II, the last Catholic monarch of England, Scotland and Ireland, fled England after William of Orange landed with a Dutch army in November. Parliament offered the crown to his daughter Mary II and her husband William III.

12-23.title: George Washington resigns his military command
12-23.description: In the Maryland State House at Annapolis, George Washington returned his commission to Congress. A victorious general giving up power voluntarily set a lasting precedent for civilian control of the military.

12-23.title: Jane Austen's Emma is published
12-23.description: John Murray published Emma, though its title page bore the date 1816. Austen's comedy of a confident young matchmaker is often judged her most accomplished novel.

12-23.title: Vincent van Gogh cuts off part of his ear
12-23.description: After a quarrel with Paul Gauguin in Arles, Vincent van Gogh cut off part of his left ear. Months later he entered the asylum at Saint-Rémy, where he painted The Starry Night.

12-23.title: Bell Labs demonstrates the transistor
12-23.description: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain showed colleagues at Bell Laboratories their point-contact transistor amplifying a signal. Transistors replaced vacuum tubes and made modern electronics possible.

12-24.title: Emperor Wu of Liang makes the infant Xiao Tong crown prince
12-24.description: Emperor Wu, founder of the Liang dynasty, made his one-year-old son Xiao Tong crown prince, having at first declined because the empire was not yet pacified. Xiao Tong later directed the compilation of the Wen Xuan, but never reigned.

12-24.title: Jawhar al-Siqilli defeats the Qarmatians at the gates of Cairo
12-24.description: The Fatimid general Jawhar al-Siqilli, who had fortified Ayn Shams just north of Cairo with a trench and wall, defeated the invading Qarmatians north of the city and forced them to withdraw from Egypt in disorder.

12-24.title: Imad al-Din Zengi captures Edessa from the crusaders
12-24.description: After a siege begun on 28 November, Imad al-Din Zengi, atabeg of Mosul and Aleppo, took Edessa, capital of the crusader County of Edessa, the first of the crusader states. Its fall prompted the Second Crusade.

12-24.title: Napoleon survives a bomb in the rue Saint-Nicaise
12-24.description: Royalist plotters exploded a barrel bomb in a Paris street as the First Consul's carriage passed, killing several bystanders but missing Napoleon. He used the attack to deport Jacobin opponents.

12-24.title: The Treaty of Ghent ends the War of 1812
12-24.description: British and American negotiators signed a peace treaty at Ghent, restoring pre-war borders. News travelled slowly, and the Battle of New Orleans was fought two weeks later.

12-24.title: Fire destroys much of the Library of Congress
12-24.description: A fire in the Capitol destroyed about 35,000 of the Library of Congress's 55,000 books, including around two-thirds of the collection bought from Thomas Jefferson in 1815.

12-24.title: The Christmas Truce begins on the Western Front
12-24.description: On Christmas Eve, soldiers along parts of the front sang carols across the lines. Over the next day many British and German troops met in no man's land, swapped gifts and buried their dead.

12-24.title: Apollo 8 orbits the Moon
12-24.description: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders became the first people to orbit the Moon. They photographed 'Earthrise' and read from Genesis in a Christmas Eve broadcast seen by millions.

12-25.title: The earliest recorded Christmas on 25 December
12-25.description: A Roman calendar compiled in 354 records the birth of Christ celebrated in Rome on 25 December 336, the earliest evidence for the date. Why it was chosen remains debated.

12-25.title: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor
12-25.description: During Christmas Mass in St Peter's, Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans. It revived a western imperial title unused since 476.

12-25.title: Emperor Leo V is murdered in the Great Palace of Constantinople
12-25.description: Followers of Michael II murdered the Byzantine emperor Leo V the Armenian in a church of the Great Palace of Constantinople. Michael took the throne as the first ruler of the Amorian dynasty.

12-25.title: Stephen I is crowned the first king of Hungary
12-25.description: Stephen I, son of Grand Prince Géza, was crowned at Esztergom as the first king of Hungary, which became a Christian kingdom. The coronation is dated either 25 December 1000 or 1 January 1001.

12-25.title: Mieszko II Lambert is crowned king of Poland at Gniezno
12-25.description: Mieszko II Lambert, son of Bolesław I the Brave, was crowned King of Poland in Gniezno Cathedral. His reign saw attacks by the Holy Roman Empire and Kievan Rus, revolts by his brothers and the loss of the royal crown.

12-25.title: Pope Clement II crowns Henry III emperor
12-25.description: Henry III, king of Germany since 1039, was crowned Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Clement II, the former bishop of Bamberg, whom Henry had made pope after the Synod of Sutri removed three rival claimants.

12-25.title: William the Conqueror is crowned at Westminster
12-25.description: William of Normandy was crowned king of England in Westminster Abbey. Norman soldiers, mistaking the congregation's acclamation for a riot, set fire to nearby houses.

12-25.title: Washington crosses the Delaware
12-25.description: On Christmas night, George Washington led about 2,400 soldiers across the ice-choked Delaware River. At dawn they surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton.

12-25.title: Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
12-25.description: In a televised address, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned. That evening the Soviet flag was lowered from the Kremlin and replaced by the Russian tricolour.

12-26.title: Leo III is elected pope
12-26.description: Leo III was elected pope, becoming bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States until his death in 816. On Christmas Day 800 he crowned Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica.

12-26.title: Shakespeare's King Lear is performed before King James I
12-26.description: William Shakespeare's tragedy King Lear, based on the legend of Leir of Britain, was performed before King James I, the earliest performance on record, noted in the Stationers' Register. The play was probably written in late 1605 or early 1606.

12-26.title: Handel's opera Agrippina premieres in Venice
12-26.description: George Frideric Handel's opera Agrippina, described as his first masterpiece, had its premiere in Venice. Its libretto by Cardinal Vincenzo Grimani followed Agrippina, mother of Nero, as she plotted the downfall of the emperor Claudius.

12-26.title: Washington defeats the Hessians at Trenton
12-26.description: Washington's army surprised the Hessian garrison at Trenton, capturing about 900 soldiers with few American losses. The victory revived the Revolution after months of defeat.

12-26.title: Louis XVI assents to the Civil Constitution of the Clergy
12-26.description: Having first opposed it, King Louis XVI gave his public assent to the Civil Constitution of the Clergy, which sought state control of the Catholic Church in France. The clergy's oaths followed, and the resulting schism lasted until 1801.

12-26.title: The Decembrist revolt fails in St Petersburg
12-26.description: Army officers led troops onto Senate Square to refuse allegiance to Nicholas I and demand reform. Cannon fire dispersed them; five leaders were hanged, and the Decembrists inspired later Russian radicals.

12-26.title: The Curies announce the discovery of radium
12-26.description: A paper presented to the French Academy of Sciences announced radium, a new element found in pitchblende by Marie and Pierre Curie with Gustave Bémont. It later proved vital in early cancer treatment.

12-26.title: An earthquake and tsunami devastate the Indian Ocean
12-26.description: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra sent tsunamis across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in 14 countries. Indonesia, Sri Lanka, India and Thailand were worst hit.

12-27.title: Justinian dedicates Hagia Sophia
12-27.description: Emperor Justinian dedicated the new church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built in under six years. It was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years and later served as a mosque and a museum.

12-27.title: The Zwickau prophets arrive in Wittenberg
12-27.description: Three men of the Radical Reformation, exiled from Zwickau, arrived in Wittenberg, where their ideas won favour with Andreas Karlstadt and others. The unrest that followed brought Martin Luther back from protective custody at the Wartburg in March 1522.

12-27.title: The Swedes lift their siege of the Jasna Góra Monastery
12-27.description: With their position in southern Lesser Poland deteriorating, the Swedish invaders lifted their siege of the Pauline monastery of Jasna Góra in Częstochowa, home of the Black Madonna icon. The defence galvanised Polish resistance and made the monastery a national symbol.

12-27.title: Residents of Flushing sign the Flushing Remonstrance
12-27.description: Some thirty residents of Flushing in New Netherland, none of them Quakers, signed a petition asking Director-General Peter Stuyvesant to exempt them from his ban on Quaker worship. It is considered a precursor of religious freedom in the Bill of Rights.

12-27.title: The schooner USS Carolina is destroyed, ending Patterson's makeshift fleet
12-27.description: The destruction of the schooner USS Carolina ended Commodore Daniel Patterson's makeshift fleet, whose delaying actions contributed to Andrew Jackson's victory over the British at New Orleans in 1815.

12-27.title: HMS Beagle sails with Charles Darwin aboard
12-27.description: HMS Beagle left Plymouth on a surveying voyage with the 22-year-old naturalist Charles Darwin. His observations over the five-year journey shaped his later theory of evolution.

12-27.title: Peter Pan opens on the London stage
12-27.description: J. M. Barrie's play Peter Pan, or the Boy Who Wouldn't Grow Up opened at the Duke of York's Theatre. Its story of Neverland, Captain Hook and Tinker Bell became a children's classic.

12-27.title: Soviet special forces kill Afghanistan's leader Hafizullah Amin
12-27.description: As Soviet troops poured into Afghanistan, commandos stormed the Tajbeg Palace in Kabul and killed President Amin. The decade-long war that followed cost hundreds of thousands of Afghan lives.

12-28.title: Majorian is acclaimed Western Roman emperor
12-28.description: Majorian, a prominent commander who with his ally Ricimer had deposed Emperor Avitus, was acclaimed emperor in the West. Ruling little more than Italy and Dalmatia, he campaigned for three years against the empire's enemies before his murder in 461.

12-28.title: Alaric II succeeds his father Euric as king of the Visigoths
12-28.description: At Toulouse, Alaric II, great-grandson of Alaric I, who sacked Rome in 410, succeeded his father Euric as king of the Visigoths. He inherited a realm covering most of Hispania and of Gaul south of the Loire.

12-28.title: An earthquake destroys Dvin, capital of medieval Armenia
12-28.description: An earthquake of magnitude about 6 struck around midnight and destroyed Dvin, the large commercial city that was the capital of early medieval Armenia, south of modern Yerevan. It caused approximately 30,000 casualties.

12-28.title: Edward the Confessor's Westminster Abbey is consecrated
12-28.description: Edward the Confessor's new abbey church at Westminster was consecrated, though the king was too ill to attend and died a week later. Every crowned English monarch since 1066 has been crowned there.

12-28.title: Galileo observes Neptune without realising it
12-28.description: While observing Jupiter, Galileo recorded a faint 'star' that was in fact Neptune. He did not recognise it as a planet, and its formal discovery came only in 1846.

12-28.title: John C. Calhoun becomes the first US vice-president to resign
12-28.description: John C. Calhoun resigned the vice-presidency to take a Senate seat, where he could better defend South Carolina during the Nullification Crisis. He had served under both John Quincy Adams and Andrew Jackson.

12-28.title: The Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film screening
12-28.description: At the Grand Café in Paris, Auguste and Louis Lumière projected ten short films to a paying audience. The screening is often taken as the birth of cinema.

12-28.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Messina
12-28.description: A powerful earthquake and tsunami struck the Strait of Messina, destroying Messina in Sicily and Reggio Calabria. Around 75,000 to 80,000 people died, making it Europe's deadliest recorded earthquake.

12-29.title: Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral
12-29.description: Four knights, believing they were carrying out Henry II's wishes, killed Archbishop Thomas Becket in his cathedral. Becket was canonised in 1173, and Canterbury became one of Europe's great pilgrimage sites.

12-29.title: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba routs the French on the Garigliano
12-29.description: After weeks of stalemate on the river Garigliano, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's Spanish army crossed by surprise and routed the French under Ludovico II of Saluzzo. After the French surrender at Gaeta, Spain controlled the Kingdom of Naples.

12-29.title: British forces capture Savannah
12-29.description: A British expedition took Savannah, Georgia, opening a new campaign in the American South. The southern strategy brought early gains but ended with surrender at Yorktown in 1781.

12-29.title: USS Constitution defeats and captures HMS Java off Brazil
12-29.description: In a three-hour single-ship action off the coast of Brazil, the American frigate USS Constitution defeated and captured HMS Java, a former French frigate taken by the British in 1811. Java had 426 aboard, the Constitution 475.

12-29.title: The Treaty of New Echota cedes Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi
12-29.description: US commissioners and a small minority faction of Cherokee signed a treaty at New Echota, Georgia, ceding all Cherokee lands east of the Mississippi. Rejected by Principal Chief John Ross and most Cherokee, it led to the Trail of Tears.

12-29.title: Texas becomes the 28th US state
12-29.description: Nine years after winning independence from Mexico, Texas was admitted to the Union as a slave state. The annexation helped provoke the Mexican-American War the following year.

12-29.title: US troops massacre Lakota at Wounded Knee
12-29.description: While disarming a band of Lakota at Wounded Knee Creek, South Dakota, the 7th Cavalry opened fire, killing some 250 to 300 men, women and children. It marked the end of the Plains wars.

12-29.title: Firebombs start the 'Second Great Fire of London'
12-29.description: German bombers dropped thousands of incendiaries on the City of London, starting some 1,500 fires. Much of the square mile burned, but St Paul's Cathedral survived amid the smoke.

12-30.title: The second edition of the Codex Justinianus takes effect
12-30.description: The revised Codex Justinianus, compiled on the orders of Emperor Justinian I and published in November as the Codex Repetitae Praelectionis, came into force. Its twelve books covered ecclesiastical, private, criminal and administrative law.

12-30.title: Brian Boru crushes Leinster and Dublin at Glenmama
12-30.description: Probably near Lyons Hill in County Kildare, the forces of Munster and Meath under Brian Boru and the High King Máel Sechnaill II crushed the armies of Leinster and Dublin led by King Máel Mórda, ending the brief Leinster revolt.

12-30.title: A Muslim mob in Granada kills the Jewish vizier Joseph ibn Naghrela
12-30.description: A Muslim mob stormed the royal palace of the Taifa of Granada, killed the Jewish vizier Joseph ibn Naghrela and massacred members of the city's Jewish community.

12-30.title: Richard, Duke of York, is killed at Wakefield
12-30.description: Lancastrian forces defeated and killed Richard, Duke of York, near Wakefield. His son Edward avenged him at Towton three months later and took the throne as Edward IV.

12-30.title: The Gadsden Purchase treaty is signed
12-30.description: US minister James Gadsden signed a treaty in Mexico City buying land south of the Gila River for a railway route. It fixed the modern border of southern Arizona and New Mexico.

12-30.title: Grigori Rasputin is murdered in Petrograd
12-30.description: Nobles led by Prince Felix Yusupov killed Rasputin, the mystic whose influence over the imperial family had become a scandal (17 December, Old Style). The murder did not save the monarchy, which fell weeks later.

12-30.title: The Soviet Union is formally established
12-30.description: Delegates from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian Federation approved the treaty creating the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. It lasted until 1991.

12-30.title: Saddam Hussein is executed in Baghdad
12-30.description: The former Iraqi president was hanged for crimes against humanity over the Dujail killings. A leaked mobile phone video of the jeering at his execution caused controversy.

12-31.title: Emperor Commodus is assassinated
12-31.description: Conspirators including his mistress Marcia and the praetorian prefect had the wrestler Narcissus strangle Commodus in his bath. The murder ushered in the turbulent Year of the Five Emperors.

12-31.title: Belisarius enters Syracuse in triumph after conquering Sicily
12-31.description: Having met Ostrogothic resistance only at Panormus, which fell after a quick siege, the Byzantine general Belisarius completed the conquest of Sicily and made a triumphal entry into Syracuse at the end of his consular year.

12-31.title: Ealdorman Æthelwulf defeats a Danish Viking army at Englefield
12-31.description: Æthelwulf, ealdorman of Berkshire, led a West Saxon force of 1,400 men to victory over a Danish Viking army at Englefield, near Reading. It was the first of a series of battles after the Danes invaded Wessex that month.

12-31.title: Henry V forces his father, Emperor Henry IV, to abdicate
12-31.description: At Ingelheim, Henry V, who had sided with his father's opponents among the imperial princes and the reform papacy in the Investiture Controversy, forced Emperor Henry IV to abdicate. He then ruled for five years in agreement with the princes.

12-31.title: Elizabeth I charters the East India Company
12-31.description: Elizabeth I granted a monopoly of English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope to a company of London merchants. The East India Company eventually ruled much of India until 1858.

12-31.title: Edison gives a public demonstration of electric lighting
12-31.description: Thomas Edison lit his Menlo Park laboratory and nearby streets with incandescent lamps for crowds who came by special train. The display showed electric light could be a practical system.

12-31.title: Truman proclaims the end of hostilities in the Second World War
12-31.description: President Truman formally proclaimed the cessation of hostilities, more than a year after Japan's surrender. The legal state of war with Germany and Japan ended later, with peace treaties.

12-31.title: The last Soviet institutions cease to function
12-31.description: By the end of the year, all remaining institutions of the Soviet Union had ceased to operate, days after Gorbachev's resignation. Fifteen independent states took its place.

12-31.title: Boris Yeltsin resigns and hands power to Vladimir Putin
12-31.description: In a New Year's Eve television address, Boris Yeltsin unexpectedly resigned as president of Russia. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin became acting president and won election in March 2000.
